# loco-ui

> A component library for Rust servers (Axum + Maud) that needs no JavaScript. Every component is a builder reached from `ui` (`ui.dialog("Delete")`) or written like an element inside `lui!`, rendering plain HTML; interactivity comes from the HTML and CSS platform and ordinary form posts. One optional script, `/lui/enhance.js`, updates marked regions in place.

Start a handler from `ui: Ui` (an Axum extractor, or `Ui::from_request(path, query, cookie)` on any server), build the page with `ui.page(title, html! { .. })` and return it. Required arguments go in the call; everything else is a chained setter. Each component below lists its constructors, its setters (props), the platform features it needs with the first Chrome, Firefox and Safari versions, its fallback, and its documentation.

# Enhancement script

`loco_ui::enhance`

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fetch` | 42 | 39 | 10.1 |
| `history.pushState` | 5 | 4 | 5 |
| `document.startViewTransition` | 111 | 144 | 18 |
| `CustomEvent` | 15 | 11 | 6 |
| `HTML drag and drop` | 4 | 3.5 | 3.1 |

- Fallback: none needed: without the script every form and link is a normal navigation and every data-lui-* attribute is inert
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: -

## Documentation

One small optional script that makes the same markup feel instant. Every page works
identically with it blocked, disabled or not yet loaded: it only intercepts what the
browser would otherwise do as a full navigation and does it in place.

**Platform features:** `<script defer>` (baseline 2010), `fetch` (Chrome 42, Firefox 39,
Safari 10.1), `DOMParser` (baseline 2010), `history.pushState` (Chrome 5, Firefox 4,
Safari 5), `document.startViewTransition` where present (Chrome 111, Firefox 144,
Safari 18) so swapped parts morph when the answer took over 150 ms (a faster one lands at
once, a frame sooner; a root marked `data-lui-morph` always morphs), `CustomEvent` (Chrome 15, Firefox 11, Safari 6) for
`lui:swap`.

**Fallback:** none needed. Without the script every form and link is a normal navigation;
the Blitz test suite renders every route with no script engine at all.

**Contract:** an element with an `id` and `data-lui="swap"` is a swap root. Submitting a
form or following a same-origin link inside it fetches the response, parses it, and
replaces the root with the element of the same `id` from the new document. The flash
messages, the toast list, `<title>` and `data-theme` are synced too, and the URL follows the response.
A form or link anywhere may name its root instead with `data-lui-target="#id"`, and
`data-lui-swap="outer|inner|append|prepend"` (default `outer`) says how the new element
lands: replace the root, replace its children, or add them at the end or the start. The
request is the same either way, so the server may answer an enhanced request (headers
`Lui-Enhance: 1` and `Accept: text/html`) with only the fragment it needs to; without the
script it is a full navigation to the same URL. `slim` (feature `axum`) does that for every page: an
enhanced request gets the page without its inline stylesheet, which the document already
has, and every HTML answer says `Vary: Lui-Enhance, Cookie`. User actions fetch with
`priority: "high"`. Links inside an element marked `data-lui-prefetch` are fetched at low
priority on hover or focus, and a click within five seconds reuses that answer. A response may also carry elements marked `data-lui-oob`
(out of band): each replaces the element of the same `id` anywhere in the page, in the
mode the attribute names (`outer` by default), and is dropped from the main swap; the
full page without the script already shows them in place. While a request is in flight
the root and the form carry `data-lui-busy` and `aria-busy="true"`, the form's submit
buttons are disabled, and an element named by `data-lui-indicator="#id"` (authored with
`hidden`) is shown; the `--lui-busy` property sets how much the busy root fades. A request
that fails becomes the plain navigation the browser would have made, so the server's
answer is always seen. The URL follows the response (links push a history entry, forms
replace it); `data-lui-push="false"` keeps the URL as it is and `data-lui-replace` always
replaces. Every swap stores a copy of the roots in the history entry, so Back and Forward
restore them without a request. After every swap the root dispatches a bubbling `lui:swap`
event with `{ id, url, mode }` in `detail`.
Rapid actions on one root are queued, so a counter clicked five times counts five. The
script also mirrors `<input type=range>` and `type=color` values while they move, counts
characters into the `<output for>` of a field with `maxlength`, sends multipart forms as
`FormData` so files survive (through `XMLHttpRequest`, filling a `<progress data-lui-progress>`
inside the form as the upload goes out, when the form has one), opens
the `:target` dialog fallback as a real modal, moves through an open popover menu with the
arrow keys, searches a combobox as you type and walks its results with the arrow keys.
A form marked `data-lui="autosubmit"` (a menu's checkbox or radio item) is sent when one
of its controls changes, and `<html data-lui-script>` lets CSS hide the buttons that only
the script-less page needs.
After a swap, an element marked `autofocus` in the new markup takes the focus (a form sent
back with an error summary starts there, as it would on a page load); otherwise the
element that had the focus gets it back, and when that element is gone the focus moves to
the new root's `h1`, or the root itself (`tabindex="-1"`), instead of falling to `<body>`.
A swap that changed the URL or the title says the new `document.title` through a
`role="status"` region the script adds to the page, as a screen reader hears a page load.
A tab title opens its panel and slides the underline on the click itself; the server's
answer replaces the strip quietly once the slide ends (a lazy panel fills in then). A
sortable list's item drags by its grip (HTML drag and drop); the drop posts the item's
own move form with its new index. A table's "select all matching" box ticks the row
boxes on the page as well. A code block's copy button (`data-lui="copy"`, rendered
`hidden`) is shown where `navigator.clipboard` (Chrome 66, Firefox 63, Safari 13.1) can
write, and copies the block on a click. A number field's steppers (`data-lui="steppers"`)
call `stepUp()`/`stepDown()` in place instead of posting, and a password's reveal button
(`data-lui="reveal"`, `hidden` without the script: the page carries `data-lui-js` on
`<html>` once the script runs) switches the field between `password` and `text`.

`script_tag` goes at the end of `<body>`; `router` (feature `axum`) serves the file with a content
hash in the URL so it caches forever. It is compatible with `script-src 'self'`.

```rust
use loco_ui::enhance;
let tag = enhance::script_tag().into_string();
assert!(tag.starts_with("<script src=\"/lui/enhance.js?v="));
```

# Layout

`loco_ui::layout`

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@view-transition` | 126 | no | 18.2 |
| `prefers-color-scheme` | 76 | 67 | 12.1 |
| `custom properties` | 49 | 31 | 9.1 |
| `@layer` | 99 | 97 | 15.4 |
| `light-dark()` | 123 | 120 | 17.5 |
| `forced-colors` | 89 | 89 | 16 |

- Fallback: plain navigations (root never cross-fades); without light-dark() the page is unthemed black on white
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes scales and depth, a Linear / Magic UI finish

## Documentation

The HTML shell every page uses: doctype, head, the stylesheet (inline, or linked to
`/lui.css`), a skip link, `<main id="main">`, the capability beacons that teach the server
what this browser supports, and the optional `crate::enhance` script tag (the page works
the same without it).

**Platform features:** cascade layers, `@layer` (Chrome 99, Firefox 97, Safari 15.4): the
stylesheet is `lui.reset`, `lui.tokens`, `lui.components`, `lui.blocks` and `lui.modes`,
and an app's own CSS (`Look::css`, `Page::css`) comes unlayered after
it, so it wins without `!important`. `light-dark()` (Chrome 123, Firefox 120, Safari 17.5)
holds both schemes in one declaration per token; `color-scheme` on `:root` picks one, from
`prefers-color-scheme` or `data-theme`. `@view-transition { navigation: auto }` (Chrome
126+, Safari 18.2+, not Firefox) lets elements with a `view-transition-name` morph across
full-page navigations; the root itself swaps instantly. `<link rel="expect"
blocking="render">` (Chrome 124+) holds the transition until `<main>` is parsed; it is
emitted only with `Cap::ViewTransitions`. `@media (forced-colors: active)`,
`(prefers-contrast: more)` and `print` adjust the components in `MODES`.

**Fallback:** browsers without view transitions navigate normally. A browser without
`light-dark()` (Chrome before 123) drops every colour token and shows the page in its
default black on white: readable, unthemed (FINDINGS, M39).

**Theming:** every colour, size, radius, shadow, duration and layer the components use is
one of the `--lui-*` custom properties. `Tokens` holds them; `ui.page(..).tokens(&tokens)` emits them
once per page after the stylesheet, so a different theme is a value, not a CSS file.
`docs/theming.md` lists each token and what it affects.

**Responsive (M34):** components respond to the box they sit in, not the viewport. Every
component root that changes layout sets `container: lui-<component> / inline-size`, and
its CSS writes the narrow layout as the base, then adds wider layouts with
`@container lui-<component> (width >= …)`. Three breakpoints, used everywhere and never
others: *narrow* below `30rem`, *medium* from `30rem`, *wide* from `48rem`. Custom
properties cannot appear in an `@container` condition, so the numbers are written
literally. Viewport `@media` is kept for `prefers-*`, `forced-colors`, `print` and
`pointer` only. Blitz does not support `@container` (FINDINGS, M34), so its shots show the
narrow base.

```rust
use std::borrow::Cow;
use loco_ui::{prelude::*, layout::{Palette, Tokens}};
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
let page = ui.page("Title", html! { p { "body" } });
let tokens = Tokens { light: Palette { primary: Cow::Borrowed("#7a3b1e"), ..Tokens::DEFAULT.light }, ..Tokens::DEFAULT };
assert!(page.tokens(&tokens).into_string().contains("--lui-primary: light-dark(#7a3b1e, var(--lui-brand-9))"));
```

# Capability beacons

`loco_ui::caps`

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@supports` | 28 | 22 | 9 |
| `selector()` | 83 | 69 | 14.1 |
| `background images` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `cookies` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: unknown browser gets every fallback; the first view always does
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: -

## Documentation

Server-side feature detection with no script. The page carries a few empty beacon elements;
`@supports` rules give each one a background image only when the browser understands the
feature. Loading that image hits `/lui/caps?flag=<name>`, which sets a cookie. From the next
request on, the server knows what the browser can do and every component emits only the
markup that browser needs.

**Platform features:** `@supports` (Chrome 28, Firefox 22, Safari 9), `@supports
selector()` (Chrome 83, Firefox 69, Safari 14.1), CSS background images, cookies.

**Fallback:** a browser with no cookie yet gets `Caps::ASSUMED`, the features at baseline
in every engine for over two years, and the fallback markup for everything else. The
beacons fire while that first view loads, and the second view is tailored. Browsers that
never load CSS images (`curl`, readers) stay on `ASSUMED`.

**Finding:** CSS cannot test HTML attributes, so `invokers` and `streaming_dsd` are proxies
for CSS features that shipped in the same release. See `docs/caps.md` in the loco-ui repo.

One cookie per flag (`lui-cap-<name>=1`) rather than one cookie holding a list: the beacons
fire in parallel, and parallel `Set-Cookie` headers on one name would overwrite each other.

This crate is the detection half of `loco-ui` and stands on its own: any server that can
read a `Cookie:` header and answer one tiny route can use it.

**Any server.** Three plain functions are the whole protocol, and none needs Axum:
`Caps::from_cookie_header` reads the flags out of a `Cookie:` header,
`Caps::from_query` lets `?caps=popover,anchor` force a set (tests, `curl`, clients
without cookies), and `beacon_cookie` turns the beacon route's query string into the
`Set-Cookie` value to answer with (status 204, `Cache-Control: no-store`). The `axum`
feature only wraps them: a `Caps` extractor and `router` for the beacon route.

```rust
use loco_ui_caps::{self as caps, Cap, Caps};
let caps = Caps::from_cookie_header("lui-cap-probed=1; lui-cap-popover=1; theme=dark");
assert!(caps.has(Cap::Popover));
assert!(!caps.has(Cap::Invokers));
assert_eq!(Caps::all().names().len(), Cap::ALL.len());
// A query string overrides the cookies, so any URL can be viewed as any browser.
assert!(Caps::from_query("caps=invokers,anchor").unwrap().has(Cap::Invokers));
// The beacon route, by hand: `GET /lui/caps?flag=popover` answers 204 with this cookie.
assert!(caps::beacon_cookie("flag=popover", false).unwrap().starts_with("lui-cap-popover=1"));
assert_eq!(caps::beacon_cookie("flag=nope", false), None);
// Over HTTPS (here, behind a proxy that says so) the cookie is `Secure`.
let https = caps::is_https(None, Some("https"), None);
assert!(caps::beacon_cookie("flag=popover", https).unwrap().ends_with("; Secure"));
```

# Button

`loco_ui::button` · demo: `/feedback`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Button` | `ui.button(text: &str)` | stable |
| `Button` | `ui.link_button(text: &str, href: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Button`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `primary` | switch |  | `off` |  | The main action of a form or page. |
| `danger` | switch |  | `off` |  | Destroys or removes something. |
| `ghost` | switch |  | `off` |  | No border or fill until hovered. |
| `soft` | switch |  | `off` |  | A quiet tinted fill in the brand colour, for a secondary action. |
| `surface` | switch |  | `off` |  | A pale brand fill inside a brand border. |
| `size` | choice: 1, 2, 3 | `size: impl Into<Size>` | `2` |  | 1 (2rem tall), 2 (2.25rem) or 3 (2.5rem); 2.75rem each on a touch screen. |
| `tone` | choice: neutral, brand, ok, warn, danger, info | `tone: Tone` | `neutral` |  | The colour; a tone other than neutral makes the button solid unless a variant is given. |
| `variant` | choice: solid, soft, surface, outline, ghost | `variant: Variant` | `outline` |  | How the tone is painted: solid, soft, surface, outline or ghost. |
| `radius` | choice: none, small, medium, large, full | `radius: Radius` | `small` |  | The corners, from square to a pill. |
| `small` | switch |  | `off` |  | Size 1: 2rem tall instead of 2.25rem. |
| `large` | switch |  | `off` |  | Size 3: 2.5rem tall, larger text. |
| `block` | switch |  | `off` |  | As wide as its container. |
| `leading` | value | `icon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An icon, or a glyph or emoji, before the text, hidden from assistive tech. |
| `trailing` | value | `icon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An icon, or a glyph or emoji, after the text, hidden from assistive tech. |
| `icon_only` | switch |  | `off` |  | Square, for a glyph or an icon. |
| `submit` | switch |  | `off` | `type` | `type="submit"`, the default unless a command or popover target is set. |
| `reset` | switch |  | `off` | `type` | `type="reset"`. |
| `command` | value | `command: &'a str, target: &'a str` |  | `command` | An invoker command (`command`, `commandfor`). |
| `popovertarget` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `popovertarget` | Toggle the popover with this id (`popovertarget`). |
| `form` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `form` | Submit the form with this id, wherever the button sits in the page (`form=`). |
| `name` | value | `name: &'a str` |  | `name` | Sent as `name=value` with the form when this button submits it. |
| `value` | value | `value: &'a str` |  | `value` | The submitted `value` that goes with `name`. |
| `aria_label` | value | `label: &'a str` |  | `aria-label` | `aria-label`. |
| `class` | value | `class: &'a str` |  | `class` | One more class after the button's own, for a component's part name. |
| `disabled` | switch |  | `off` | `disabled` | Greyed out and not clickable. |
| `loading` | condition | `on: bool` | `off` |  | A spinner before the text, `disabled` and `aria-busy`, while `on`. |
| `body` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | Markup to show instead of the text. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The element's `id`. |
| `role` | value | `role: &'a str` |  | `role` | `role`, for a button that is a menu item or a tab, or a link that acts as a button. |
| `title` | value | `title: &'a str` |  | `title` | `title`. |
| `style` | value | `style: impl Into<String>` |  | `style` | Inline `style`, for a per-element custom property or anchor name. |
| `aria_haspopup` | value | `kind: &'a str` |  | `aria-haspopup` | `aria-haspopup` (`"menu"`, `"dialog"`). |
| `pressed` | condition | `on: bool` | `off` | `aria-pressed` | `aria-pressed`, for a toggle button. |
| `accesskey` | value | `key: &'a str` |  | `accesskey` | `accesskey`. |
| `aria_keyshortcuts` | value | `keys: &'a str` |  | `aria-keyshortcuts` | `aria-keyshortcuts`, the shortcut spelled out for assistive technology. |
| `formmethod` | value | `method: &'a str` |  | `formmethod` | `formmethod`. |
| `formaction` | value | `action: &'a str` |  | `formaction` | `formaction`. |
| `formnovalidate` | switch |  | `off` | `formnovalidate` | `formnovalidate`. |
| `rel` | value | `rel: &'a str` |  | `rel` | `rel` of a link (`"prev"`, `"next"`). |
| `current` | condition | `on: bool` | `off` | `aria-current` | `aria-current="page"`. |
| `interestfor` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `interestfor` | Show the popover with this id while the button or link has the pointer or focus (`interestfor`). |
| `shimmer` | switch |  | `off` |  | A light sweeps across the button, over its own background. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `invoker commands` | 135 | 144 | 26.2 |
| `popovertarget` | 114 | 125 | 17 |
| `aria-busy` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `prefers-reduced-motion` | 74 | 63 | 10.1 |
| `translate` | 104 | 72 | 14.1 |

- Fallback: a popover command becomes popovertarget; other commands need the component's own fallback; a shimmer button is at rest without translate
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Button

## Documentation

The one button every other component builds on, drawn after Radix Themes' Button and
IconButton: a neutral outline by default, then any `Tone` in any
`Variant` (`.tone(..)`, `.variant(..)`), with switches for the
common ones: solid (`.primary()` with the brand gradient, `.danger()`), `.soft()`,
`.surface()` and `.ghost()`, which compose (`.danger().ghost()` is a red ghost button);
three sizes (`.size(1..=3)`, `.small()` for 1); `.radius(..)`; a square icon button. Pressed, busy and disabled each have their own look: a busy
button keeps its width and shows a spinner over its label, a disabled one turns gray.
`ui.link_button` gives a link the same look, for actions that are a navigation (GET) rather
than a post.

**Platform features:** `<button>` with its `type`, `name`/`value` (sent with the form that
submits it), `form=` (submit a form elsewhere on the page), invoker commands
(`command`/`commandfor`, Chrome 135, Firefox 144, Safari 26.2) and `popovertarget`
(Chrome 114, Firefox 125, Safari 17). A loading button is `disabled` and `aria-busy`, with a
CSS-only spinner that slows down under `prefers-reduced-motion`. `.shimmer()` sweeps a light
across the button: an `::after` layer over the button's own background, moved with the
`translate` property (Chrome 104, Firefox 72, Safari 14.1) under `@supports (translate: 100%)`
and `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`; the colours are `--lui-shimmer` over a filled
tone and `--lui-shimmer-surface` over the others, the pace `--lui-shimmer-duration`.

**Accessibility:** a native `<button>` or `<a>` (Enter and Space, or Enter for a link); an
icon button carries `aria-label`, a busy one `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled`, a toggle
`aria-pressed`, a menu trigger `aria-haspopup`. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on
every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical
violation).

**What it does not do without script:** turn itself into a loading button while its form
posts; the server sets `.loading(true)` on the page it renders (the enhancement script
marks a posting form `aria-busy` on its own).

**Fallback:** a popover command (`toggle-popover`, `show-popover`, `hide-popover`) in a
browser without invoker commands is written as `popovertarget` and `popovertargetaction`,
which popover browsers have had since 2023. Other commands (`show-modal`, `close`) have
no attribute fallback; the dialog component uses a `:target` link there instead. A
`.shimmer()` button without `translate`, or under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, is the
same button at rest, with no sweep.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
let save = ui.button("Save").primary().render().into_string();
assert!(save.contains(r#"class="lui-button lui-button-primary""#) && save.contains(r#"type="submit""#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Button("Save") primary; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), save);
// A small ghost icon button that toggles a popover, and a link that looks like a button.
let more = ui.button("\u{22ef}").ghost().small().icon_only().aria_label("More").command("toggle-popover", "menu");
let more = more.render().into_string();
assert!(more.contains(r#"commandfor="menu""#) && more.contains(r#"aria-label="More""#));
let docs = ui.link_button("Read the docs", "/docs").render().into_string();
assert!(docs.starts_with("<a") && docs.contains(r#"href="/docs""#));
// The server knows the job is still running, so the page it renders says so.
let busy = ui.button("Export").loading(true).render().into_string();
assert!(busy.contains("disabled") && busy.contains(r#"aria-busy="true""#));
// Radix's quieter variants and sizes.
let soft = ui.button("Invite").soft().size(3).render().into_string();
assert!(soft.contains(r#"class="lui-button lui-button-soft lui-button-large""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Button("Invite") soft size=3; }.into_string(), soft);
// Opt-in motion: a light sweeps across it, CSS only.
let shiny = ui.button("Upgrade").primary().shimmer().render().into_string();
assert!(shiny.contains(r#"class="lui-button lui-button-primary lui-button-shimmer""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Button("Upgrade") primary shimmer; }.into_string(), shiny);
// Tone and variant compose; each one set is also a `data-*` attribute on the root.
let remove = ui.button("Remove").danger().ghost().radius(Radius::Full).render().into_string();
assert!(remove.contains(r#"data-tone="danger" data-variant="ghost" data-radius="full""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Button("Remove") danger ghost radius="full"; }.into_string(), remove);
// Icons around the text, a larger size, the container's full width.
let next = ui.button("Continue").primary().large().block().trailing(Icon::ArrowRight).render().into_string();
assert!(next.contains("lui-button-large lui-button-block") && next.contains(r#"data-icon="arrow-right""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Button("Continue") primary large block trailing=(Icon::ArrowRight); }.into_string(), next);
```

# Input, checkbox, switch, radio group

`loco_ui::input` · demo: `/field`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Input` | `ui.input(name: &str, label: &str)` | stable |
| `Input` | `ui.checkbox(name: &str, label: &str)` | stable |
| `Input` | `ui.switch(name: &str, label: &str)` | stable |
| `RadioGroup` | `ui.radio_group(name: &str, legend: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Input`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `email` | switch |  | `off` | `type` | `type="email"`. |
| `password` | switch |  | `off` | `type` | `type="password"`. |
| `tel` | switch |  | `off` | `type` | `type="tel"`: a phone number, the phone keypad on a touch screen. |
| `url` | switch |  | `off` | `type` | `type="url"`: the browser checks it is an absolute URL. |
| `number` | value | `min: impl Into<Bound>, max: impl Into<Bound>` |  |  | A number from `min` to `max`, inclusive; `None::<f64>` for no bound. |
| `pattern` | value | `pattern: &'a str, hint: &'a str` |  | `pattern` | Text that must match `pattern`. |
| `textarea` | number | `rows: u8` |  |  | Multi-line text, `rows` high. |
| `file` | value | `accept: &'a str` |  |  | A file picker. |
| `date` | value | `min: &'a str, max: &'a str` |  |  | `type="date"`, bounds as `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `time` | value | `min: &'a str, max: &'a str` |  |  | `type="time"`, bounds as `HH:MM`. |
| `datetime` | value | `min: &'a str, max: &'a str` |  |  | `type="datetime-local"`, bounds as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`. |
| `month` | value | `min: &'a str, max: &'a str` |  |  | `type="month"`, bounds as `YYYY-MM`. |
| `week` | value | `min: &'a str, max: &'a str` |  |  | `type="week"`, bounds as `YYYY-Www`. |
| `multiple` | switch |  | `off` | `multiple` | The file picker takes several files. |
| `required` | switch |  | `off` | `required` | The `required` attribute, and a `*` after the label (hidden from screen readers, which say "required"). |
| `optional` | switch |  | `off` |  | "(optional)" after the label, for a form whose fields are mostly required. |
| `disabled` | switch |  | `off` | `disabled` | `disabled` and `aria-disabled`: shown greyed and not posted. |
| `readonly` | switch |  | `off` |  | Shown and posted, not editable (`readonly`, or a disabled control and a hidden input where HTML has no `readonly`). |
| `help` | value | `help: &'a str` |  |  | Help text under the field. |
| `maxlength` | number | `max: usize` |  | `maxlength` | `maxlength`, counted in an `<output>` under the field. |
| `value` | value | `value: &'a str` |  | `value` | The current value (ignored for files and passwords). |
| `checked` | condition | `checked: bool` | `off` | `checked` | Tick the checkbox or switch. |
| `error` | value | `message: &'a str` |  |  | A server message under the field. |
| `placeholder` | value | `placeholder: &'a str` |  | `placeholder` | Placeholder text. |
| `search` | switch |  | `off` | `type` | `type="search"`. |
| `hide_label` | switch |  | `off` |  | Only the control, the label kept as its `aria-label`; help, counter and error still follow it. |
| `list` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `list` | `list`. |
| `autocomplete` | value | `value: &'a str` |  | `autocomplete` | `autocomplete` (`"off"`, `"email"`, `"new-password"`). |
| `autofocus` | switch |  | `off` | `autofocus` | `autofocus`. |
| `inputmode` | value | `mode: &'a str` |  | `inputmode` | `inputmode` (`"numeric"`), the on-screen keyboard to show. |
| `step` | number | `step: impl Into<f64>` |  | `step` | `step` of a number field. |
| `aria_controls` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `aria-controls` | `aria-controls`. |
| `form` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `form` | `form`. |
| `class` | value | `class: &'a str` |  | `class` | A class on the control, for a component's part name. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The control's id, `f-<name>` by default. |
| `gradient_border` | switch |  | `off` |  | The border drawn with `--lui-gradient-ring`. |
| `leading` | value | `slot: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An icon or text inside the field's border, before the text. |
| `trailing` | value | `slot: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An icon or text inside the field's border, after the text. |
| `prefix` | value | `addon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An addon joined to the field's start (`"https://"`, `"$"`), outside its border. |
| `suffix` | value | `addon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An addon joined to the field's end (`"kg"`, `".com"`), outside its border. |
| `addon_button` | value | `button: Button<'a>` |  |  | A button joined to the field's end (Copy, Send). |
| `reveal` | switch |  | `off` |  | A password field's show/hide button, which only the enhancement script shows. |
| `width` | choice: 1, 2, 3 | `width: impl Into<Size>` |  |  | A narrower control: 1 (8rem), 2 (16rem) or 3 (24rem); the container's width by default. |
| `size` | choice: 1, 2, 3 | `size: impl Into<Size>` | `2` |  | A text field's height and text: Radix's sizes 1 to 3. |
| `variant` | choice: solid, soft, surface, outline, ghost | `variant: Variant` | `surface` |  | A text field's look: surface (a border), soft (a tint) or ghost (neither). |

## Props of `RadioGroup`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `option` | item | `value: &'a str, label: &'a str` |  |  | One choice posting `value`, labelled `label`. |
| `description` | modifier | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A line under the choice added last, read out with it. |
| `disabled` | modifier |  |  | `disabled` | The choice added last cannot be picked. |
| `cards` | switch |  | `off` |  | Each choice a selectable card, 1, 2 or 3 across by the container's width. |
| `value` | value | `value: &'a str` |  | `value` | The value of the choice that is selected. |
| `required` | switch |  | `off` | `required` | One choice must be picked before the form submits. |
| `help` | value | `help: &'a str` |  |  | Help text under the choices. |
| `error` | value | `message: &'a str` |  |  | A server message under the choices. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `constraint validation` | 10 | 4 | 10.1 |
| `type=date` | 20 | 57 | 14.1 |
| `:user-invalid` | 119 | 88 | 16.5 |
| `role="switch"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `appearance: none` | 84 | 80 | 15.4 |
| `<fieldset>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `linear-gradient(in oklch` | 111 | 127 | 16.2 |

- Fallback: none needed: native controls; the switch stays a checkbox without appearance: none; a gradient border is a plain one without in oklch gradients
- Needs script: partly: a live character count while typing needs the enhancement script
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: Radix Themes TextField, Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroup and RadioCards

## Documentation

One labelled field on its own: the label, the control, help text, a character counter and
the server's error, tied together with `aria-describedby`. `ui.checkbox`, `ui.switch` and
`ui.radio_group` are the same for choices. `crate::form` renders its fields with this
file, so a field looks and behaves the same inside a form built with `ui.form` and in a
form a route writes by hand.

The look follows Radix Themes (TextField, TextArea, Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroup and
RadioCards): a gray-7 border with no shadow, `.leading(..)`/`.trailing(..)` slots inside
the border, help in gray-11 and the error after a warning icon, a drawn checkbox, radio and
switch, and `.cards()` for a radio group of selectable cards. A text field takes Radix's
sizes (`.size(..)`, 1 to 3) and its surface, soft or ghost variant (`.variant(..)`).

**Platform features:** constraint validation (`required`, `pattern`, `min`, `max`,
`maxlength`, `type=email`, baseline 2015; `type=date`/`time`/`datetime-local`, Chrome 20, Firefox 57 (93 for `datetime-local`),
Safari 14.1); `:user-invalid` (baseline 2023) so a field is not red before it is touched;
`<output for>` counts characters; `role="switch"` on a checkbox (ARIA 1.2) drawn as a
track and thumb with `appearance: none`; `<fieldset>` + `<legend>` for a radio group;
`appearance: none` checkboxes and radios with the tick drawn in CSS; `:has()` (Chrome 105,
Firefox 121, Safari 15.4) for the slot wrapper's focus ring and the picked card; a
container query (Chrome 105, Firefox 110, Safari 16) lays radio cards 1, 2 or 3 across.
`.gradient_border()` draws a text field's or textarea's border with `--lui-gradient-ring`, a
padding-box layer over a border-box one, behind `@supports` for
`linear-gradient(in oklch, ..)` (Chrome 111, Firefox 127, Safari 16.2); nothing moves.

**Accessibility:** every field has a `<label for>`; help, counter and error are joined by
`aria-describedby`, a server error sets `aria-invalid` and is `role="alert"`; the switch is
a checkbox with `role="switch"`. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo
route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** keep the counter live while typing (the
enhancement script does; without it the counter shows the length the server rendered).

**Fallback:** none needed: every control is a native one, and the switch is still a
checkbox where `appearance: none` is not supported. Without `:has()` a slotted field keeps
the input's own focus outline and a picked card shows no ring; without container queries
radio cards stay one per row. A `.gradient_border()` field keeps its
plain border where `in oklch` gradients are not supported.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let name = ui.input("name", "Name").render().into_string();
assert!(name.contains(r#"<label for="f-name">Name</label>"#) && name.contains(r#"type="text""#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Input("name", "Name"); };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), name);
// An opt-in gradient border, a class on the control.
let key = ui.input("key", "API key").gradient_border().render().into_string();
assert!(key.contains(r#"class="lui-input-gradient-border""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Input("key", "API key") gradient_border; }.into_string(), key);
// Setters as on form fields, and one per input type.
let email = ui.input("email", "Email").email().required().value("ada@x.org")
    .help("We never share it.").error("Already taken.");
let email = email.render().into_string();
assert!(email.contains(r#"aria-describedby="f-email-help f-email-error""#));
assert!(email.contains(r#"aria-invalid="true""#) && email.contains(r#"type="email""#));
let on = ui.switch("digest", "Weekly digest").checked(true).render().into_string();
assert!(on.contains(r#"role="switch""#) && on.contains("checked"));
let plan = ui.radio_group("plan", "Plan").option("free", "Free").option("pro", "Pro").value("pro");
let plan = plan.render().into_string();
assert!(plan.contains("<legend>Plan</legend>") && plan.contains(r#"value="pro" checked"#));
// Text or an icon inside the border; text is read out with the field.
let site = ui.input("site", "Website").leading("https://").trailing(Icon::Search);
let site = site.render().into_string();
assert!(site.contains(r#"<div class="lui-input-slots"><span id="f-site-leading""#));
assert!(site.contains(r#"aria-describedby="f-site-leading""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Input("site", "Website") leading="https://" trailing=(Icon::Search); }.into_string(), site);
// A radio group of cards, 1, 2 or 3 across by the container's width.
let tier = ui.radio_group("tier", "Tier").cards()
    .option("hobby", "Hobby").description("One project")
    .option("team", "Team").description("Unlimited projects").value("team");
let tier = tier.render().into_string();
assert!(tier.contains("lui-radio-cards") && tier.contains(r#"aria-describedby="f-tier-1-description""#));
let same = lui! { RadioGroup("tier", "Tier") cards value="team" {
    option "hobby" "Hobby" description="One project";
    option "team" "Team" description="Unlimited projects";
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), tier);
// A small soft field, the size and variant on its root.
let q = ui.input("q", "Search").size(1).variant(Variant::Soft).render().into_string();
assert!(q.starts_with(r#"<div class="lui-field" data-size="1" data-variant="soft">"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Input("q", "Search") size=1 variant="soft"; }.into_string(), q);
```

# Badge

`loco_ui::badge` · demo: `/button`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Badge` | `ui.badge(text: impl Display)` | stable |

## Props of `Badge`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `secondary` | switch |  | `off` |  | A gray tone instead of the brand. |
| `danger` | switch |  | `off` |  | The `--lui-danger` tone. |
| `outline` | switch |  | `off` |  | A border and no fill (gray unless toned). |
| `ok` | switch |  | `off` |  | The `--lui-ok` tone. |
| `warn` | switch |  | `off` |  | The `--lui-warn` tone. |
| `solid` | switch |  | `off` |  | Filled with the tone, light text on it. |
| `surface` | switch |  | `off` |  | A pale tint inside a border of the tone. |
| `href` | value | `href: &'a str` |  | `href` | Make the badge a link. |
| `shimmer` | switch |  | `off` |  | A light sweeps across the badge, over its own fill. |
| `size` | choice: 1, 2, 3 | `size: impl Into<Size>` | `1` |  | Radix's sizes 1 to 3: more padding, and larger text at 3. |
| `tone` | choice: neutral, brand, ok, warn, danger, info | `tone: Tone` | `brand` |  | The colour. |
| `variant` | choice: solid, soft, surface, outline, ghost | `variant: Variant` | `soft` |  | How the tone is painted; ghost is the tone's text with no fill or border. |
| `radius` | choice: none, small, medium, large, full | `radius: Radius` | `small` |  | The corners, from square to a pill. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<span>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `translate` | 104 | 72 | 14.1 |

- Fallback: none needed; a shimmer badge is at rest without translate
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Badge

## Documentation

A short label beside something: a status, a count, a tag. After Radix Themes Badge: a tone
(the brand by default; `.secondary()` gray, `.danger()`, `.ok()`, `.warn()`, or any
`Tone` with `.tone(..)`) in a variant (soft by default: a tint with
darker text; `.solid()`, `.surface()`, `.outline()`, or `.variant(..)`), at Radix's size 1
unless `.size(..)` says 2 or 3, with no wrapping.

**Platform features:** a `<span>` (or an `<a>` with `.href()`); nothing interactive of its
own. `.shimmer()` sweeps a light across it, as on a button: an `::after` layer moved with
the `translate` property (Chrome 104, Firefox 72, Safari 14.1) under
`@supports (translate: 100%)` and `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, in
`--lui-shimmer` over a filled badge and `--lui-shimmer-surface` over a tinted or outlined one.

**Accessibility:** plain text in a `<span>`; the tone colours are mixed with the text colour
so they pass AA on their tint. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route,
both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** none needed. A `.shimmer()` badge without `translate`, or under
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, is the same badge at rest.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
assert_eq!(ui.badge("New").render().into_string(), r#"<span class="lui-badge">New</span>"#);
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Badge("New"); };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), ui.badge("New").render().into_string());
let paid = ui.badge("Paid").ok().render().into_string();
assert!(paid.contains("lui-badge lui-badge-ok"));
let tag = ui.badge("rust").outline().href("/tags/rust").render().into_string();
assert!(tag.starts_with(r#"<a class="lui-badge lui-badge-outline" data-variant="outline" href="/tags/rust">"#));
// Opt-in motion: a light sweeps across it.
let new = ui.badge("New").shimmer().render().into_string();
assert_eq!(new, r#"<span class="lui-badge lui-badge-shimmer">New</span>"#);
assert_eq!(lui! { Badge("New") shimmer; }.into_string(), new);
// Radix's other looks, in any tone.
let loud = ui.badge("Failed").danger().solid().render().into_string();
assert_eq!(loud, r#"<span class="lui-badge lui-badge-danger lui-badge-solid" data-tone="danger" data-variant="solid">Failed</span>"#);
assert_eq!(lui! { Badge("Failed") danger solid; }.into_string(), loud);
// The typed setters, written as strings in `lui!`.
let beta = ui.badge("Beta").tone(Tone::Info).variant(Variant::Surface).size(2).radius(Radius::Full);
let beta = beta.render().into_string();
assert!(beta.contains(r#"data-size="2" data-tone="info" data-variant="surface" data-radius="full""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Badge("Beta") tone="info" variant="surface" size=2 radius="full"; }.into_string(), beta);
```

# Card

`loco_ui::card` · demo: `/marquee`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Card` | `ui.card()` | stable |

## Props of `Card`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | value | `title: &'a str` |  |  | The heading at the top (`h3`). |
| `description` | value | `text: &'a str` |  |  | Muted text under the title. |
| `header` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | More header content, placed at the top right beside the title. |
| `body` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | The main content. |
| `footer` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | A row at the bottom, usually buttons, packed at its end like a dialog's. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The root's id, for a link to the card or a swap target. |
| `beam` | switch |  | `off` |  | A light runs round the border, drawn with a conic gradient. |
| `glow` | switch |  | `off` |  | A spotlight at the top centre that brightens and grows on hover. |
| `gradient_border` | switch |  | `off` |  | The border drawn with `--lui-gradient-ring`. |
| `reveal` | switch |  | `off` |  | Fades and rises as it scrolls into view. |
| `classic` | switch |  | `off` |  | Radix's classic card: a deeper shadow and no border line. |
| `ghost` | switch |  | `off` |  | No frame, fill or shadow: only the card's spacing. |
| `size` | choice: 1, 2, 3 | `size: impl Into<Size>` | `2` |  | The padding and gaps: 1rem, 1.5rem (the default) or 2rem. |
| `variant` | choice: solid, soft, surface, outline, ghost | `variant: Variant` | `surface` |  | Surface or ghost, as in Radix; the others draw as surface. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `grid` | 57 | 52 | 10.1 |
| `conic-gradient` | 69 | 83 | 12.1 |
| `@property` | 85 | 128 | 16.4 |
| `mask-composite` | 120 | 53 | 15.4 |
| `color-mix()` | 111 | 113 | 16.2 |
| `linear-gradient(in oklch` | 111 | 127 | 16.2 |
| `animation-timeline: view()` | 115 | no | 26 |

- Fallback: none needed; each showpiece effect is at rest without its feature or under reduced motion
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Card

## Documentation

A bordered box with a header (title, description, and anything else such as an action),
a body and a footer: shadcn's Card, in Radix Themes Card's variants (surface, `.classic()`,
`.ghost()`) and three of its sizes (`.size(..)`, the padding). Settings panels, pricing
tiers, sign-in boxes.

**Platform features:** plain `<div>`s and a heading; the header is a grid, so an action
put in `.header(..)` sits at the top right beside the title. Four opt-in showpiece
effects, CSS only, each off under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` where it moves:
- `.beam()`: a light running round the border, a `conic-gradient` (Chrome 69, Firefox 83,
  Safari 12.1) whose start angle is an `@property` (Chrome 85, Firefox 128, Safari 16.4)
  animated by `@keyframes`, cut to a 1px ring with `mask-composite: exclude` (Chrome 120,
  Firefox 53, Safari 15.4), in `--lui-beam`, once round every `--lui-beam-duration`.
- `.glow()`: a spotlight at the top centre, `--lui-glow` in a `radial-gradient`, that
  brightens and grows on `:hover`; it does not follow the pointer. Behind
  `@supports` for `color-mix()` (Chrome 111, Firefox 113, Safari 16.2).
- `.gradient_border()`: the border drawn with `--lui-gradient-ring`, a padding-box layer
  over a border-box one, behind `@supports` for `linear-gradient(in oklch, ..)`
  (Chrome 111, Firefox 127, Safari 16.2).
- `.reveal()`: fades and rises as it scrolls into view, a scroll-driven animation with
  `animation-timeline: view()` (Chrome 115, Firefox no, Safari 26).

**Accessibility:** a `<div>` of ordinary markup; its title is an `<h3>`, so it shows in the
outline. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every
demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** none needed. Each effect sits inside `@supports` for the feature it needs,
and in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` when it moves, so a browser without
it, or a visitor who asked for less motion, gets the card at rest: a plain border, no beam,
no glow, and shown in place from the start (a `.reveal()` card is never left hidden).

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.card().title("Team").body(html! { p { "3 members" } }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<h3 class="lui-card-title">Team</h3>"#) && m.contains("3 members"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Card title="Team" { p { "3 members" } } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// A description, an action in the header, and a footer of buttons.
let m = ui.card()
    .title("Plan")
    .description("Billed monthly.")
    .header(html! { (ui.badge("Current").secondary()) })
    .body(html! { p { "Pro, 12 seats" } })
    .footer(html! { (ui.button("Change plan").primary()) });
let m = m.render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("lui-card-description") && m.contains("lui-card-action") && m.contains("lui-card-footer"));
// Opt-in showpieces, one class each on the root.
let m = ui.card().title("Pro").beam().glow().gradient_border().reveal().render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<div class="lui-card lui-card-beam lui-card-glow lui-card-gradient-border lui-card-reveal">"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Card title="Pro" beam glow gradient_border reveal; }.into_string(), m);
// Tighter padding, and no frame.
let m = ui.card().title("Note").size(1).variant(Variant::Ghost).render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<div class="lui-card lui-card-ghost" data-size="1" data-variant="ghost">"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Card title="Note" size=1 variant="ghost"; }.into_string(), m);
```

# Icon

`loco_ui::icon` · demo: `/button`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Icon` | `ui.icon(icon: Icon)` | stable |

## Props of `IconMark`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | value | `label: &'a str` |  |  | The name a screen reader says, for an icon that carries meaning on its own. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<svg>` | 4 | 3 | 3.2 |
| `role="img"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Lucide

## Documentation

A small set of inline SVG icons, drawn in `currentColor` so they take the colour of the
text around them: the ones buttons, menus, tables and alerts need. The shapes are
[Lucide](https://lucide.dev)'s (ISC licence), the set shadcn/ui uses.

**Platform features:** inline `<svg>` (no icon font, no request, no sprite); an icon is
`aria-hidden` unless it is given a `.label()`, which makes it `role="img"` with that name.

**Accessibility:** decorative icons are `aria-hidden`; a meaningful one is `role="img"` with
`aria-label`. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability
variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let check = ui.icon(Icon::Check).render().into_string();
assert!(check.starts_with(r#"<svg class="lui-icon" aria-hidden="true""#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Icon(Icon::Check); };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), check);
// An icon that is the only content of a link or a button needs a name.
let warn = ui.icon(Icon::TriangleAlert).label("Warning").render().into_string();
assert!(warn.contains(r#"role="img" aria-label="Warning""#));
// An icon on its own renders decoratively, so it drops into any `html!`.
let m = html! { (Icon::Plus) " Add" };
assert!(m.into_string().contains("M12 5v14"));
```

# Avatar

`loco_ui::avatar` · demo: `/card`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Avatar` | `ui.avatar(name: &str)` | stable |
| `Avatars` | `ui.avatars(label: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Avatar`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `src` | value | `src: &'a str` |  | `src` | The picture's URL. |
| `size` | value | `size: u8` | `2` |  | Radix's sizes 1–5: 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3 or 4rem across. |
| `small` | switch |  | `off` |  | `.size(1)`: 1.5rem across, for lists and table rows. |
| `large` | switch |  | `off` |  | `.size(4)`: 3rem across, for a profile header. |
| `square` | switch |  | `off` |  | Rounded corners instead of a circle (a team, a project). |
| `tone` | choice: neutral, brand, ok, warn, danger, info | `tone: Tone` | `brand` |  | The colour of the initials' tile. |
| `variant` | choice: solid, soft, surface, outline, ghost | `variant: Variant` | `soft` |  | Soft (a tint) or solid (filled); Radix has no other, so the rest draw as soft. |
| `radius` | choice: none, small, medium, large, full | `radius: Radius` | `full` |  | The corners, from square to the circle. |

## Props of `Avatars`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `avatar` | item | `name: &'a str` |  |  | A person in the row. |
| `src` | modifier | `src: &'a str` |  |  | The picture of the person added last. |
| `max` | number | `max: usize` |  |  | Show this many, then a `+n` count of the rest. |
| `size` | value | `size: u8` | `2` |  | Radix's sizes 1–5 for every avatar in the row. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alt=""` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `loading="lazy"` | 77 | 75 | 15.4 |
| `role="img"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: the initials are the fallback
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Avatar

## Documentation

A round picture of a person, with their initials underneath for when there is no picture
or it fails to load. After Radix Themes Avatar: five sizes, the initials on a soft brand
tint, or any `Tone` soft or solid, and `.radius(..)` for the
corners.

**Platform features:** the initials are painted first and the `<img>` is stacked over
them; an image that fails to load has `alt=""`, so it renders nothing and the initials
show through, with no `onerror` handler. `loading="lazy"` defers images below the fold.
The root is `role="img"` named after the person, so a screen reader says the name once.

**Accessibility:** `role="img"` named by the person's name; the initials inside are
`aria-hidden`. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability
variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** the initials are the fallback.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.avatar("Ada Lovelace").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"role="img" aria-label="Ada Lovelace""#) && m.contains(">AL</span>"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Avatar("Ada Lovelace"); };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
let m = ui.avatar("Grace Hopper").src("/img/grace.jpg").large().render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<img src="/img/grace.jpg" alt="" loading="lazy">"#) && m.contains("lui-avatar-4"));
// A row of overlapping avatars, three shown and a count of the rest.
let team = ui.avatars("Team").max(3).avatar("Ada Lovelace").avatar("Grace Hopper").avatar("Alan Turing").avatar("Ken Thompson");
let team = team.render().into_string();
assert!(team.contains(r#"role="group" aria-label="Team""#) && team.contains(r#"aria-label="+1""#));
let same = lui! { Avatars("Team") max=3 { avatar "Ada Lovelace"; avatar "Grace Hopper"; avatar "Alan Turing"; avatar "Ken Thompson"; } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), team);
// A solid gray tile with rounded corners.
let bot = ui.avatar("Build Bot").tone(Tone::Neutral).variant(Variant::Solid).radius(Radius::Medium);
let bot = bot.render().into_string();
assert!(bot.contains(r#"data-tone="neutral" data-variant="solid" data-radius="medium""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Avatar("Build Bot") tone="neutral" variant="solid" radius="medium"; }.into_string(), bot);
```

# Stack

`loco_ui::stack` · demo: `/marquee`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Stack` | `ui.stack()` | stable |

## Props of `Stack`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `body` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | What is stacked: each top-level element under the one before. |
| `gap` | number | `n: u8` |  |  | The gap as a step of the `--lui-space-*` scale. |
| `align` | choice: start, center, end, baseline, stretch | `align: Align` | `stretch` |  | Where the children sit across the column (`align-items`). |
| `justify` | choice: start, center, end, between | `justify: Justify` | `start` |  | How the children share the column's height (`justify-content`). |
| `padding` | number | `n: u8` |  |  | Padding on every side as a step of the `--lui-space-*` scale. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gap` | 84 | 63 | 14.1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: -

## Documentation

Children one under the other with an even gap between them and no margins to fight: the
vertical rhythm of a form, a card body, a settings page.

**Platform features:** a flex column with `gap` (Chrome 84, Firefox 63, Safari 14.1);
the gap is a step of the `--lui-space-*` scale. `.align(..)` and `.justify(..)` write
`data-align` and `data-justify` (`align-items`, `justify-content`), `.padding(n)` a step
of the same scale, as Radix Themes Flex's props do.

**Accessibility:** layout only: no roles, reading order is source order. Checked by axe-core
in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no
serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.stack().body(html! { p { "One" } p { "Two" } }).render().into_string();
assert_eq!(m, r#"<div class="lui-stack"><p>One</p><p>Two</p></div>"#);
// `.gap(n)` picks a step: n × 4px with the default `--lui-space`.
let m = ui.stack().gap(2).body(html! { p { "Tight" } }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"class="lui-stack lui-gap-2""#));
// The same in `lui!`, where the block is the body:
let same = lui! { Stack gap=2 { p { "Tight" } } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// Centred across, packed at the end, with padding round it.
let m = ui.stack().align(Align::Center).justify(Justify::End).padding(4)
    .body(html! { p { "Done" } }).render().into_string();
assert_eq!(m, r#"<div class="lui-stack lui-pad-4" data-align="center" data-justify="end"><p>Done</p></div>"#);
let same = lui! { Stack align="center" justify="end" padding=4 { p { "Done" } } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
```

# Cluster

`loco_ui::cluster` · demo: `/feedback`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Cluster` | `ui.cluster()` | stable |

## Props of `Cluster`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `body` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | What goes in the row: each top-level element beside the one before. |
| `between` | switch |  | `off` |  | First child at the start, last at the end, the rest spread between. |
| `end` | switch |  | `off` |  | Children packed at the end of the row (a dialog's or card's actions). |
| `gap` | number | `n: u8` |  |  | The gap as a step of the `--lui-space-*` scale. |
| `align` | choice: start, center, end, baseline, stretch | `align: Align` | `center` |  | Where the children sit across the row (`align-items`). |
| `justify` | choice: start, center, end, between | `justify: Justify` | `start` |  | How the children share the row (`justify-content`). |
| `padding` | number | `n: u8` |  |  | Padding on every side as a step of the `--lui-space-*` scale. |
| `nowrap` | switch |  | `off` |  | Keep the children on one line; they shrink instead of wrapping. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flex-wrap` | 29 | 28 | 9 |
| `gap` | 84 | 63 | 14.1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: -

## Documentation

Children side by side, wrapping onto the next line when they run out of room: a row of
buttons, badges, filters or links.

**Platform features:** `flex-wrap` with `gap` (Chrome 84, Firefox 63, Safari 14.1), so a
wrapped line keeps the same spacing and no child carries a margin. `.align(..)` and
`.justify(..)` write `data-align` and `data-justify` (`align-items`, `justify-content`),
`.padding(n)` a step of the space scale, as Radix Themes Flex's props do.

**Accessibility:** layout only: no roles, reading order is source order. Checked by axe-core
in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no
serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.cluster().body(html! { (ui.badge("rust")) (ui.badge("maud")) }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<div class="lui-cluster">"#));
// A toolbar: the title on the left, the actions pushed to the right.
let m = ui.cluster()
    .between()
    .gap(4)
    .body(html! { h2 { "Orders" } (ui.button("New order").primary()) });
let m = m.render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"class="lui-cluster lui-cluster-between lui-gap-4""#));
// The same in `lui!`, where the block is the body:
let same = lui! { Cluster between gap=4 { h2 { "Orders" } Button("New order") primary; } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// On one line, on the text baseline, centred, with padding round it.
let m = ui.cluster().nowrap().align(Align::Baseline).justify(Justify::Center).padding(3)
    .body(html! { h2 { "Plan" } span { "$9" } }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<div class="lui-cluster lui-cluster-nowrap lui-pad-3" data-align="baseline" data-justify="center">"#));
let same = lui! { Cluster nowrap align="baseline" justify="center" padding=3 { h2 { "Plan" } span { "$9" } } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
```

# Grid

`loco_ui::grid` · demo: `/pricing`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Grid` | `ui.grid(min: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Grid`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `body` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | What is laid out: each top-level element is a cell. |
| `gap` | number | `n: u8` |  |  | The gap as a step of the `--lui-space-*` scale. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repeat(auto-fill` | 57 | 52 | 10.1 |
| `@media` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: -

## Documentation

As many equal columns as fit, each at least a given width: cards, stats, a gallery. It
drops to fewer columns on a narrow screen on its own.

**Platform features:** `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(<min>, 1fr))`
(CSS Grid, baseline 2017); the minimum travels in a `--lui-grid-min` custom property on
the element. Under a 30rem viewport an `@media` rule caps the minimum at the grid's width
with `min(<min>, 100%)`, so a wide minimum never overflows a phone. (Not at every width:
Taffy, Blitz's layout engine, lays out a single column whenever a track minimum uses
`min()`: FINDINGS, M21.)

**Accessibility:** layout only: no roles, reading order is source order. Checked by axe-core
in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no
serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.grid("15rem").body(html! { (ui.card().title("A")) (ui.card().title("B")) });
let m = m.render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<div class="lui-grid" style="--lui-grid-min: 15rem">"#));
let m = ui.grid("10rem").gap(2).body(html! { p { "x" } }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("lui-grid lui-gap-2"));
// The same in `lui!`, where the block is the body:
let same = lui! { Grid("10rem") gap=2 { p { "x" } } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
```

# Split

`loco_ui::split` · demo: `/layout`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Split` | `ui.split(side: Markup, main: Markup)` | stable |

## Props of `Split`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `side_width` | value | `width: &'a str` |  |  | The side's width, any CSS length. |
| `side_end` | switch |  | `off` |  | The side after the main part, in the markup and on screen. |
| `gap` | number | `n: u8` |  |  | The gap as a step of the `--lui-space-*` scale. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flex-wrap` | 29 | 28 | 9 |
| `min-inline-size` | 57 | 41 | 12.1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: -

## Documentation

A narrow side beside a wide main part, the side stacking on top when the main part would
get narrower than half the width: a settings nav beside its form, filters beside results.

**Platform features:** the "sidebar" flex pattern: `flex-wrap`, the side at its width and
the main part growing with `flex-grow: 999` and `min-inline-size: 50%`, so the switch to
one column happens by container width, with no media query.

**Accessibility:** layout only: no roles, reading order is source order. Checked by axe-core
in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no
serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.split(html! { nav { "Settings" } }, html! { p { "Form" } }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<div class="lui-split-side"><nav>Settings</nav></div>"#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Split(html! { nav { "Settings" } }, html! { p { "Form" } }); };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// A wider side, placed after the main part.
let m = ui.split(html! { aside { "Filters" } }, html! { p { "Results" } }).side_width("20rem").side_end();
let m = m.render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("--lui-split-side: 20rem") && m.find("Results") < m.find("Filters"));
```

# Calendar

`loco_ui::calendar` · demo: `/calendar`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Calendar` | `ui.calendar(name: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Calendar`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `today` | value | `date: &str` |  |  | The date to mark as today (`YYYY-MM-DD`), instead of the server's clock in UTC. |
| `min` | value | `date: &str` |  |  | The first day that can be picked (`YYYY-MM-DD`). |
| `max` | value | `date: &str` |  |  | The last day that can be picked (`YYYY-MM-DD`). |
| `disabled_dates` | value | `off: &'a dyn Fn(Date) -> bool` |  |  | Days for which `off` returns true cannot be picked. |
| `event` | item | `date: &str, text: &'a str` |  |  | A dot under the day `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), with `text` for screen readers and as the day's tooltip. |
| `sunday_first` | switch |  | `off` |  | Weeks start on Sunday, whatever the language's first day. |
| `radio` | switch |  | `off` |  | Each day is a radio button named after the calendar, to post inside a form, instead of a link. |
| `value` | value | `date: &str` |  | `value` | The picked day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) when it does not come from the query string. |
| `required` | switch |  | `off` | `required` | In radio mode, a day must be picked before the form submits. |
| `range` | value | `end: &'a str` |  |  | Pick a first and a last day: the first in the calendar's name, the last in `end`. |
| `weeks` | switch |  | `off` |  | A column of ISO 8601 week numbers before the days. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<table>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `aria-current="date"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `role="radiogroup"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `:has(:checked)` | 105 | 121 | 15.4 |

- Fallback: without :has() the picked radio's day is not filled in; it is still checked and posts
- Needs script: partly: changing month in place and arrow-key moves between days need script
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: shadcn Calendar

## Documentation

A month grid drawn on the server: previous and next month are links, each day is a link
(pick a day and the page comes back with it) or a radio button (the day is a form field,
for a date picker). Days before `.min()`, after `.max()` or ruled out by `.disabled_dates(..)`
cannot be picked; `.event(..)` puts a dot under a day. `.range(end)` picks two days, a
first and a last, into two parameters; `.weeks()` numbers the weeks (ISO 8601). Today is
`Ui::today`, which the app may set to the visitor's own day (`Ui::with_today`).

**Platform features:** a `<table>` of links or `<input type="radio">` inside `<label>`s,
`aria-current="date"` on today, `role="radiogroup"` when the days are radios, `:has(:checked)`
(Chrome 105, Firefox 121, Safari 15.4) to draw the picked radio's day. The month shown
travels in `?month.<name>=YYYY-MM`, the picked day in `?<name>=YYYY-MM-DD`.

**Accessibility:** a `<table>` with column headers (`abbr` holds the full weekday); each day
is a link or radio whose hidden text says the whole date, today is `aria-current="date"`,
the month title is `aria-live`; arrow keys are not wired (Tab moves through days). Checked
by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and
dark (no serious or critical violation).

A range is links only: the first click sets the first day, the second the last, a third
starts again; the days between are shaded.

**What it does not do without script:** change month without a page load (the enhancement
script swaps the calendar in place: it is a swap root), or move between days with the arrow
keys (Tab goes through them in order). In radio mode a month link leaves the page, so a
form's other unsaved fields are lost; put the calendar in its own form or step.

**Fallback:** without `:has()` the picked radio's day is not filled in, but the radio is
still checked and posts.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from_request("/book", "month.due=2026-09", "");
let m = ui.calendar("due").today("2026-09-24").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("September 2026") && m.contains(r#"aria-current="date""#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"href="/book?month.due=2026-09&amp;due=2026-09-15""#));
// Radios for a form, a window of days, weekends and holidays off (the closure may
// capture), a deadline marked, Sunday first, week numbers.
let holidays = [loco_ui::calendar::Date::parse("2026-09-16").unwrap()];
let off = |d: loco_ui::calendar::Date| d.weekday() >= 5 || holidays.contains(&d);
let m = ui.calendar("due").radio().required()
    .min("2026-09-10").max("2026-10-31")
    .disabled_dates(&off)
    .event("2026-09-30", "Invoice due")
    .sunday_first()
    .weeks();
let m = m.render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"type="radio" name="due" value="2026-09-11""#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"value="2026-09-12" disabled"#) && m.contains("Invoice due"));
assert!(m.contains(r#"value="2026-09-16" disabled"#) && m.contains("Week 38"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Calendar("due") radio required min="2026-09-10" max="2026-10-31"
    disabled_dates=(&off) event=("2026-09-30", "Invoice due") sunday_first weeks; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// A range: the first day is picked, so a later day's link sets the last one.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/stay", "from=2026-09-10", "");
let m = ui.calendar("from").range("to").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"href="/stay?from=2026-09-10&amp;to=2026-09-14""#));
```

# Date picker

`loco_ui::date_picker` · demo: `/calendar`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `DatePicker` | `ui.date_picker(name: &str, label: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `DatePicker`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | value | `date: &'a str` |  | `value` | The current value, `YYYY-MM-DD` (a saved date). |
| `min` | value | `date: &'a str` |  | `min` | The first day that can be picked, `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `max` | value | `date: &'a str` |  | `max` | The last day that can be picked, `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `disabled_dates` | value | `off: &'a dyn Fn(Date) -> bool` |  |  | Days for which `off` returns true cannot be picked (the native control ignores this). |
| `range` | value | `end: &'a str` |  |  | A first and a last day: the first in `name`, the last in `end`, one calendar in the page. |
| `disabled` | switch |  | `off` | `disabled` | Shown, not changeable and not posted. |
| `readonly` | switch |  | `off` |  | Shown and posted, not changeable. |
| `required` | switch |  | `off` | `required` | A day must be picked before the form submits. |
| `native` | switch |  | `off` |  | The browser's own `<input type="date">` instead of the calendar. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `popover` | 114 | 125 | 17 |
| `anchor-name` | 125 | 147 | 26 |
| `<input type="date">` | 20 | 57 | 14.1 |

- Fallback: without popover the calendar is laid out in the form; .native() is the browser's own control
- Needs script: partly: writing the picked day onto the button before the form is sent needs script
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: shadcn Date Picker

## Documentation

A form field for a date: a button showing the date, which opens a calendar in a popover;
picking a day checks a radio named after the field, so the form posts `name=YYYY-MM-DD`.
`.native()` gives the browser's own `<input type="date">` instead.

**Platform features:** `popover` with `popovertarget` (Chrome 114, Firefox 125, Safari 17);
CSS anchor positioning (`anchor-name`, `position-anchor`, Chrome 125, Firefox 147, Safari 26)
places it under the button; inside, the `crate::calendar` in radio mode. `.native()` is
`<input type="date">` with `min`/`max` (Chrome 20, Firefox 57, Safari 14.1).

**Accessibility:** a button naming the picked date that opens the calendar popover, the days
a radio group labelled by the field's legend; Escape closes the popover. Checked by axe-core
in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no
serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** write the picked day onto the button before the form
is sent (the button shows the saved value; the picked day is filled in the calendar), or
change month without a page load. A month link comes back with the calendar laid out in the
page instead of in the popover, because a popover cannot arrive open.

`.range(end)` picks a first and a last day into two names with one calendar, laid out in
the page (its days are links, so it cannot sit in a popover that a page load closes); the
form carries both days as hidden fields. `.disabled()` shows the date without a way to
change it and posts nothing; `.readonly()` shows it and posts it.

**Fallback:** without `popover` the calendar is laid out in the form under the label.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
let m = ui.date_picker("due", "Due date").value("2026-09-24").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"popovertarget="f-due-calendar""#) && m.contains("24 September 2026"));
assert!(m.contains(r#"type="radio" name="due" value="2026-09-24" checked"#));
// No popover support: the same calendar, in the page.
let old = Ui::from(Caps::default());
assert!(!old.date_picker("due", "Due date").render().into_string().contains("popover"));
// The browser's own control, with bounds.
let m = ui.date_picker("due", "Due date").min("2026-01-01").max("2026-12-31").native();
assert!(m.render().into_string().contains(r#"type="date" value="" min="2026-01-01" max="2026-12-31""#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { DatePicker("due", "Due date") min="2026-01-01" max="2026-12-31" native; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m.render().into_string());
// A stay: two names, one calendar; the form posts both.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/stay", "from=2026-09-10&to=2026-09-14", "");
let m = ui.date_picker("from", "Dates").range("to").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<input type="hidden" name="to" value="2026-09-14">"#));
assert!(m.contains("lui-calendar-between"));
```

# Dialog

`loco_ui::dialog` · demo: `/dialog`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Dialog` | `ui.dialog(trigger: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Dialog`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `body` | value | `body: Markup` |  |  | What the dialog says. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The dialog's id instead of `lui-dialog-` and the trigger's slug. |
| `open` | condition | `open: bool` | `off` | `open` | Render the dialog already open (non-modal, no backdrop). |
| `title` | value | `title: &'a str` |  |  | A title in a header with a close control. |
| `size` | value | `size: u8` | `2` |  | Radix's sizes 1–4: 20, 32, 42 or 56 rem wide, roomier padding as it grows. |
| `small` | switch |  | `off` |  | `.size(1)`: 20 rem wide. |
| `large` | switch |  | `off` |  | `.size(3)`: 42 rem wide. |
| `danger` | switch |  | `off` |  | A red solid confirm button. |
| `description` | value | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A line under the title, tied to the dialog by `aria-describedby`. |
| `footer` | value | `footer: Markup` |  |  | Markup at the start of the button row (a link, a note, a checkbox). |
| `fullscreen` | switch |  | `off` |  | Fill the viewport, without the rounded frame. |
| `confirm` | value | `label: &'a str, action: &'a str` |  |  | A confirm button labelled `label`. |
| `returns_to` | value | `path: &'a str` |  |  | Where the server should send the browser after the confirm form, posted as a hidden `returns_to` field. |
| `close` | value | `label: &'a str` | `Close` |  | Label of the closing button when there is no confirm form. |
| `cancel` | value | `label: &'a str` | `Cancel` |  | Label of the cancel button beside the confirm button. |
| `closedby` | value | `closedby: &'a str` | `any` | `closedby` | The `closedby` attribute. |
| `trigger` | value | `button: Button<'a>` |  |  | The opener as a styled button of the caller's (`ui.button(..).danger()`); its command or link is the dialog's. |
| `no_trigger` | switch |  | `off` |  | No opener: a link to `?dialog=<id>` or a button elsewhere opens it. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<dialog>` | 37 | 98 | 15.4 |
| `command="show-modal"` | 135 | 144 | 26.2 |
| `<form method="dialog">` | 37 | 98 | 15.4 |
| `closedby` | 134 | 141 | 26 |
| `@starting-style` | 117 | 129 | 17.5 |
| `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` | 117 | 129 | 17.4 |

- Fallback: link to #id opens it through a :target rule, chosen server-side; the confirm footer is a plain form either way
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: viewport
- Look after: Radix Themes Dialog and AlertDialog

## Documentation

A modal opened by a button and closed by a button, with no script. It can carry a title
with a close control, a size (Radix's 1–4), a `danger` variant, and a footer that is a real form: a
confirm button posting to a URL beside a cancel button, so "Delete account?" is one round
trip and the server redirects back to the page that opened it. `.description(..)` adds a
line under the title that names the dialog's purpose to assistive tech too,
`.footer(..)` puts markup at the start of the button row, and `.fullscreen()` fills the
viewport.

**Platform features:**
- `<dialog>` element (baseline 2022), its `::backdrop`, and `closedby` (Chrome 134+,
  Firefox 141+, Safari 26+) for Escape and light dismiss.
- Invoker commands: `<button command="show-modal" commandfor="id">` and `command="close"`
  (Chrome 135+, Firefox 144+, Safari 26.2+). Closing without a confirm form uses
  `<form method="dialog">` (baseline 2022).
- Motion: `@starting-style` (Chrome 117, Firefox 129, Safari 17.5) and
  `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` on `display` and `overlay` (Chrome 117,
  Firefox 129, Safari 17.4) fade and scale the dialog and its backdrop in and out; older
  browsers open and close it at once, and `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` zeroes it.
- Focus: the close control sits last in the markup, so the dialog's own focusing steps land
  on the first field in the body, then on the confirm button.

**Accessibility:** a native `<dialog>` opened modally: focus moves in, Escape closes, the
page behind is inert; named by its title through `aria-labelledby`. Checked by axe-core in
headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious
or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** return focus to the opener in the `:target`
fallback, trap focus there, or post a form and close without reloading.

**Fallback:** when `Caps` lacks `Invokers`, the opener is a link to `#id` and a `:target`
rule shows the dialog as a fixed overlay; links to `#` close and cancel it. Only one variant
is ever in the markup.

**Server state:** `?dialog=<id>` in the URL renders the dialog already open (non-modal, no
backdrop), as does `.open(true)`. The confirm form goes back to the page it came from
unless `returns_to` says otherwise. `returns_to` is posted
with the confirm form as a hidden `returns_to` field, so the handler knows where to send
the browser back; check it is a local path before redirecting to it.

**Without script:** `closedby` is honoured by the real `<dialog>` only; the `:target`
fallback closes through its links alone. Focus is not trapped in the fallback.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
let hi = ui.dialog("Say hi").body(html! { p { "Hello." } });
assert!(hi.render().into_string().contains(r#"commandfor="lui-dialog-say-hi""#), "the id is the trigger's slug");

let m = ui.dialog("Delete account")
    .id("confirm")
    .title("Delete account?")
    .size(1)
    .danger()
    .confirm("Delete", "/account/delete")
    .returns_to("/settings")
    .cancel("Keep it")
    .closedby("closerequest")
    .open(true)
    .body(html! {
        p { "This cannot be undone." }
        label { "Reason " input name="reason"; }
    });
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains("<dialog id=\"confirm\" class=\"lui-dialog-sm\" closedby=\"closerequest\" aria-labelledby=\"confirm-title\" open>"));
assert!(html.contains("<form method=\"post\" action=\"/account/delete\""));
assert!(html.contains("name=\"returns_to\" value=\"/settings\""));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Dialog("Delete account") id="confirm" title="Delete account?" size=1 danger
    confirm=("Delete", "/account/delete") returns_to="/settings" cancel="Keep it"
    closedby="closerequest" open=(true) {
    p { "This cannot be undone." }
    label { "Reason " input name="reason"; }
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);

// From the request: open when the URL says `?dialog=confirm`, and the confirm form
// returns to this page.
```
