let ui = Ui::from_request("/account", "dialog=confirm", "");
let html = ui.dialog("Delete account").id("confirm").confirm("Delete", "/account/delete").render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(" open>") && html.contains("value=\"/account\""));

// Radix's four sizes; `.small()` and `.large()` are sizes 1 and 3.
let wide = ui.dialog("Terms").size(4).render().into_string();
assert!(wide.contains(r#"class="lui-dialog-xl""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Dialog("Terms") size=4; }.into_string(), wide);

// A description, markup in the footer, and the whole viewport.
let m = ui.dialog("Edit photo").title("Edit photo").description("Crop and rotate before saving.")
    .footer(html! { a href="/help" { "Help" } }).fullscreen().render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"class="lui-dialog-md lui-dialog-full""#) && m.contains(r#"aria-describedby="lui-dialog-edit-photo-description""#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"<p id="lui-dialog-edit-photo-description" class="lui-dialog-description">"#) && m.contains(r#"<div class="lui-dialog-footer"><a href="/help">"#));
let same = lui! { Dialog("Edit photo") title="Edit photo" description="Crop and rotate before saving."
    footer={ a href="/help" { "Help" } } fullscreen; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);

// A styled opener of your own; the dialog sets its command. Or none at all.
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
let styled = ui.dialog("Delete").trigger(ui.button("Delete").danger().leading(Icon::Trash)).render().into_string();
assert!(styled.contains(r#"lui-button-danger""#) && styled.contains(r#"commandfor="lui-dialog-delete""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Dialog("Delete") trigger=(ui.button("Delete").danger().leading(Icon::Trash)); }.into_string(), styled);
let bare = ui.dialog("Terms").no_trigger().render().into_string();
assert!(bare.starts_with(r#"<div class="lui-dialog"><dialog id="lui-dialog-terms""#));
```

# Popover menu

`loco_ui::popover` · demo: `/popover`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Menu` | `ui.menu(label: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Menu`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `link` | item | `text: &'a str, href: &'a str` |  |  | A link. |
| `action` | item | `text: &'a str, action: &'a str` |  | `action` | A `<form method="post">` button posting to `action`. |
| `checkbox` | item | `text: &'a str, action: &'a str, name: &'a str` |  |  | A checkbox in its own form posting `name=on` (or nothing) to `action`. |
| `radio` | item | `text: &'a str, action: &'a str, name: &'a str, value: &'a str` |  |  | A radio button in its own form posting `name=value` to `action`. |
| `checked` | modifier | `checked: bool` |  | `checked` | The checkbox or radio item is ticked. |
| `group` | item | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A section heading. |
| `separator` | item |  |  |  | A rule between groups. |
| `submenu` | item | `text: &'a str, items: impl IntoIterator<Item = I>` |  |  | A nested menu of `items` (`MenuItem`s or `(text, href)` links). |
| `icon` | modifier | `icon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An icon, or a glyph or emoji, before the item's text (decorative, hidden from assistive tech). |
| `shortcut` | modifier | `keys: &'a str` |  |  | A shortcut shown after the item's text, as `<kbd>`. |
| `disabled` | modifier |  |  | `disabled` | The item is shown but not usable. |
| `danger` | modifier |  |  |  | The item is destructive. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The menu's id instead of `lui-menu-` and the label's slug. |
| `align_end` | switch |  | `off` |  | Open below the button with right edges aligned, for a button at the end of a row. |
| `open_right` | switch |  | `off` |  | Open to the right of the button. |
| `trigger` | value | `button: Button<'a>` |  |  | The opener as a styled button of the caller's; the menu sets its `popovertarget`. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `popover` | 114 | 125 | 17 |
| `anchor-name` | 125 | 147 | 26 |
| `@starting-style` | 117 | 129 | 17.5 |
| `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` | 117 | 129 | 17.4 |

- Fallback: no anchor: UA-centred popover; no popover: <details> dropdown (submenus nested); actions are plain post forms either way
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Popover and DropdownMenu

## Documentation

A dropdown menu that opens on click, closes on outside click or Escape, no script. Items
are links, `<form method="post">` actions, checkboxes and radio buttons that post their
own form, headings, separators and submenus; each item can show an icon and a keyboard
shortcut and be disabled or destructive.

**Platform features:**
- `popover` attribute + `popovertarget` button (Chrome 114, Firefox 125, Safari 17). Light
  dismiss and top-layer stacking come for free; a submenu is a nested popover, which the
  platform keeps open with its parent.
- CSS anchor positioning `anchor-name` / `position-anchor` / `position-area`
  (Chrome 125, Firefox 147, Safari 26) to place the menu under its button, at its end, or
  to its right (`.align_end()`, `.open_right()`), with `position-try-fallbacks` (Chrome
  128, Firefox 147, Safari 26) flipping it when there is no room; the areas are the
  generic `crate::popover_card::Popover`'s.
- A checkbox or radio item (`.checkbox(..)`, `.radio(..)`) is a native control with
  `role="menuitemcheckbox"` or `menuitemradio` in its own `<form method="post">`, with an
  Apply button beside it. The enhancement script submits the form on `change`
  (`data-lui="autosubmit"`) and then hides the Apply buttons.
- Motion: `@starting-style` (Chrome 117, Firefox 129, Safari 17.5) and
  `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` on `display` and `overlay` (Chrome 117,
  Firefox 129, Safari 17.4) fade the menu in and out with a 4px drop; the `<details>`
  fallback fades in only. Older browsers show and hide it at once.

**Accessibility:** a `popover` menu: `aria-haspopup="menu"` on the trigger, `role="menu"`
and `menuitem` on the items, Escape and a click outside close it; the script adds arrow
keys. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants,
light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** position itself against the opener where anchor
positioning is missing; it is centred instead.

**Fallback:** without `Caps::Anchor` the popover is UA-centred, which is still usable.
Without `Caps::Popover` the menu is a `<details>` dropdown (a submenu a nested one): it
opens and closes on click but has no light dismiss.

A checkbox or radio item needs its Apply button pressed without the script.

**Without script:** a shortcut shown beside an item is a label; binding the key needs
script the crate does not ship. Arrow keys move between items only with the enhancement
script; Tab always works.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
// The id is `lui-menu-` and the label's slug: this menu is `#lui-menu-account`.
let m = ui.menu("Account").link("Profile", "/profile").link("Sign out", "/logout");
assert!(m.render().into_string().contains(r#"id="lui-menu-account""#));
// `icon`, `shortcut`, `disabled` and `danger` apply to the item just added.
let m = ui.menu("Account")
    .group("Signed in as Ada")
    .link("Profile", "/profile").icon("@").shortcut("g p")
    .link("Billing", "/billing").disabled()
    .separator()
    .submenu("Theme", [("Light", "/?t=light"), ("Dark", "/?t=dark")])
    .separator()
    .action("Sign out", "/logout").danger()
    .align_end();
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains("<form method=\"post\" action=\"/logout\""));
assert!(html.contains("position-area: block-end span-inline-start") && html.contains(r#"id="lui-menu-account-theme""#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Menu("Account") align_end {
    group "Signed in as Ada";
    link "Profile" "/profile" icon="@" shortcut="g p";
    link "Billing" "/billing" disabled;
    separator();
    submenu "Theme" ([("Light", "/?t=light"), ("Dark", "/?t=dark")]);
    separator();
    action "Sign out" "/logout" danger;
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
// A styled opener of your own: the menu sets its popover target.
let more = ui.button("").ghost().icon_only().aria_label("More").leading(Icon::Ellipsis);
let m = ui.menu("More").link("Rename", "/rename").trigger(more).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"class="lui-button lui-button-ghost lui-button-icon""#) && m.contains(r#"popovertarget="lui-menu-more""#));
// Checkbox and radio items post their own form; `checked` applies to the item just added.
let m = ui.menu("View")
    .checkbox("Show grid", "/view", "grid").checked(true)
    .radio("Compact", "/view", "density", "compact")
    .radio("Comfortable", "/view", "density", "comfortable").checked(true);
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"<form method="post" action="/view" data-lui="autosubmit">"#));
assert!(html.contains(r#"<input class="lui-popover-check" type="checkbox" role="menuitemcheckbox" name="grid" value="on" checked>"#));
assert!(html.contains(r#"type="radio" role="menuitemradio" name="density" value="comfortable" checked>"#));
let same = lui! { Menu("View") {
    checkbox "Show grid" "/view" "grid" checked=(true);
    radio "Compact" "/view" "density" "compact";
    radio "Comfortable" "/view" "density" "comfortable" checked=(true);
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Tabs

`loco_ui::tabs` · demo: `/tabs`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Tabs` | `ui.tabs(name: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Tabs`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tab` | item | `title: &'a str, body: Markup` |  |  | A tab titled `title` with its panel. |
| `lazy` | item | `title: &'a str, body: impl Fn() -> Markup + 'a` |  |  | A tab whose panel is rendered only when it is the open one. |
| `badge` | modifier | `text: impl Display` |  |  | A count after the title of the tab added last. |
| `vertical` | switch |  | `off` |  | Titles in a column on the left, the open panel beside them. |
| `select_below` | switch |  | `off` |  | Under 30rem of its own width the titles give way to a `<select>`. |
| `underline` | switch |  | `off` |  | Titles on a hairline, the open one marked by a 2px bar (Radix TabNav). |
| `size` | choice: 1, 2, 3 | `size: impl Into<Size>` | `2` |  | The titles' text and padding: smaller at 1, larger at 3. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hidden` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `view-transition-name` | 111 | 144 | 18 |

- Fallback: no view transitions: the chip appears on the new tab; the narrow-screen select has a Go button
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: Radix Themes Tabs and TabNav

## Documentation

Tab strip where exactly one panel is open at a time, no script. Tabs can carry a badge
count, be lazy (their body rendered only when open), run vertically, and collapse to a
`<select>` when the tabs are narrow (a container query), take an `.underline()` look after Radix
TabNav instead of the pill, and come in Radix's sizes (`.size(..)`, 1 to 3); the open tab
morphs to the next one on switch.

**Platform features:**
- Links and the `hidden` attribute (baseline): each title is a link to its own tab, every
  panel but the open one is `hidden`. The markup follows Radix Tabs: a `.lui-tabs-list` of
  `.lui-tabs-trigger` links and one `.lui-tabs-panel` per tab, each with
  `data-state="active|inactive"`.
- `view-transition-name` (Chrome 111, Firefox 144, Safari 18) on the open tab's chip
  (an empty `.lui-tabs-mark`, never the title, so no text moves): the raised chip slides to
  the new tab, across documents through the layout's `@view-transition` rule and in place
  with the enhancement script. `view-transition-class: lui-tabs-mark` (Chrome 125,
  Firefox 144, Safari 18.2) gives the slide the `--lui-ease-spring` curve.

**Accessibility:** each tab is a link, the open one `aria-current="true"` (one tab stop
each, Enter follows it); the narrow select is named "Tab"; not the ARIA tablist pattern,
which needs script (FINDINGS, M29 · axe-core over every route). Checked by axe-core in
headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no
serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** arrow keys between tabs (the WAI-ARIA tabs
pattern); each tab is a link reached by Tab.

**Fallback:** none needed: links, a flex row and a grid work everywhere. Without
`Caps::ViewTransitions` the chip carries no transition name and simply appears on the new
tab.

**Server persistence:** the open tab comes from the request's `?tab.<name>=` (see
`crate::UiState::tab`) and each title is a link to `?tab.<name>=i`, so the choice survives
navigation (query first, cookie after). The strip is a
swap root, so the `crate::enhance` script replaces just the strip instead of the page;
it also opens the clicked tab before the request, so the switch shows on the click.
Because every switch is a request, a lazy tab (`Tabs::lazy`) costs nothing until
opened: the component calls its closure only when it is the open tab.

**Without script:** the narrow `<select>` needs its "Go" button; the script submits
it on change.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let mut ui = Ui::from_request("/docs", "tab.docs=1", "");
ui.caps = Caps::all();
// `badge` applies to the tab added last.
let m = ui.tabs("docs")
    .tab("Install", html! { p { "cargo add" } })
    .tab("Use", html! { p { "html!" } }).badge(3)
    .lazy("Changelog", || html! { p { "(long)" } })
    .vertical()
    .select_below();
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains("href=\"/docs?tab.docs=0\""));
assert!(html.contains("view-transition-name: lui-tabs-docs"));
assert!(html.contains("<select name=\"tab.docs\""));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Tabs("docs") vertical select_below {
    tab "Install" { p { "cargo add" } }
    tab "Use" badge=3 { p { "html!" } }
    lazy "Changelog" || { p { "(long)" } }
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
// Radix's underline look instead of the pill.
let line = ui.tabs("line").tab("One", html! {}).tab("Two", html! {}).underline().render().into_string();
assert!(line.contains("lui-tabs lui-tabs-underline"));
assert_eq!(lui! { Tabs("line") underline { tab "One" {} tab "Two" {} } }.into_string(), line);
// Smaller titles.
let small = ui.tabs("small").tab("One", html! {}).size(1).render().into_string();
assert!(small.contains(r#"class="lui-tabs" data-size="1""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Tabs("small") size=1 { tab "One" {} } }.into_string(), small);
```

# Accordion

`loco_ui::accordion` · demo: `/accordion`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Accordion` | `ui.accordion(group: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Accordion`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `item` | item | `title: &'a str, body: Markup` |  |  | A section titled `title` with its body. |
| `icon` | modifier | `icon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An icon, or a glyph or emoji, before the title of the section added last, hidden from assistive tech. |
| `description` | modifier | `summary: &'a str` |  |  | A muted line under the title of the section added last, visible while it is closed. |
| `multiple` | switch |  | `off` |  | Several sections may be open at once (`?open.<group>=0,2`). |
| `controls` | switch |  | `off` |  | "Expand all" and "Collapse all" links above the sections (with `multiple`). |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hidden` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: none needed: every toggle, expand and collapse is a link
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: shadcn Accordion

## Documentation

Stacked disclosure sections, no script. Exclusive by default (one open at a time), or
`multiple` so several stay open, with "Expand all" and "Collapse all" links. An item can
carry a summary line under its title and an icon before it, and a body can hold another
accordion.

**Platform features:** links and the `hidden` attribute (baseline). The markup follows
Radix Accordion: a `.lui-accordion-item` per section holding a `.lui-accordion-trigger`
link and a `.lui-accordion-body`, each with `data-state="open|closed"`.

**Accessibility:** each title is a link to its own state, with `aria-expanded` and
`aria-controls` naming its body; icons are `aria-hidden`. Checked by axe-core in headless
Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or
critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** arrow keys between titles (the WAI-ARIA accordion
pattern). The body does not animate its height: it is shown by the server's answer.

**Fallback:** none needed; the markup is the same everywhere. Before M38 each title was a
link inside a `<summary>`, a link inside the summary's implicit button, which is not
conforming. Every click already went to the server, so the server alone decides what is open.

**Server persistence:** the open sections come from the request's `?open.<group>=0,2` (a
comma list, see `crate::UiState::opens`) and each title is a link that toggles its own index in
that list, so the choice survives navigation. "Expand all" links to every index, "Collapse
all" to `open.<group>=` (which removes the key). The group is a swap root for the
`crate::enhance` script. A nested accordion is its own group with its own key.

**Without script:** nothing is lost.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
// Items 0 and 2 of "faq" were left open, as the URL records it.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/help", "open.faq=0,2", "");
// `icon` and `description` apply to the item added last.
let m = ui.accordion("faq")
    .item("Install", html! { p { "cargo add" } }).icon("\u{1F4E6}").description("One line.")
    .item("Use", html! { p { "html!" } })
    .item("More", html! { (ui.accordion("faq-more").item("Nested", html! { p { "Own group." } })) })
    .multiple()
    .controls();
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"href="/help?open.faq=2" data-state="open" aria-expanded="true""#), "open item's link removes itself from the list");
assert!(html.contains("href=\"/help?open.faq=0%2C1%2C2\">Expand all"));
assert!(html.contains("class=\"lui-accordion-summary\">One line."));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Accordion("faq") multiple controls {
    item "Install" icon="\u{1F4E6}" description="One line." { p { "cargo add" } }
    item "Use" { p { "html!" } }
    item "More" { (lui! { Accordion("faq-more") { item "Nested" { p { "Own group." } } } }) }
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Combobox

`loco_ui::combobox` · demo: `/combobox`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Combobox` | `ui.combobox(name: &str, action: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Combobox`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `options` | value | `values: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a str>` |  |  | Suggestions with no `<optgroup>`. |
| `group` | value | `label: &'a str, values: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a str>` |  |  | Suggestions under `<optgroup label>`. |
| `results` | value | `results: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a str>` |  |  | The server's own results for the query. |
| `multiple` | switch |  | `off` |  | Results add to the selection instead of replacing it. |
| `create` | value | `action: &'a str` |  |  | A "Create" row posting to `action` when the query matches nothing. |
| `label` | value | `label: &'a str` | `Search` | `aria-label` | Accessible name of the input. |
| `placeholder` | value | `placeholder: &'a str` | `Type to search…` |  | Placeholder of the input. |
| `keep` | item | `name: &'a str` |  |  | A query parameter of this page (`view`) carried, with the request's value, by the search form, every result and every chip's remove link. |
| `disabled` | switch |  | `off` | `disabled` | The box and its button disabled, the chips without remove links, no results. |
| `readonly` | switch |  | `off` |  | The box `readonly`, the chips without remove links, no results. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<datalist>` | 20 | 4 | 12.1 |
| `<optgroup>` | 20 | 4 | 12.1 |
| `<search>` | 118 | 118 | 17 |
| `aria-live` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: none needed: chips, results and the create row are links and forms
- Needs script: partly: static suggestions and per-submit results; live filtering and arrow keys into the results need script
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: shadcn Combobox

## Documentation

A text input with native suggestions, a server-filtered result list, and a selection
shown as removable chips, no script. Suggestions can be grouped, several values can be
selected, a "create" row appears when nothing matches, and the selection survives every
re-filter because it travels in the form as hidden fields.

**Platform features:**
- `<input list>` + `<datalist>` (baseline 2020) gives native type-ahead from a fixed list
  the server already knows; `<optgroup>` inside it (Chrome 20, Firefox 4, Safari 12.1)
  groups the suggestions where the browser draws them grouped.
- `<search>` element (baseline 2023) for semantics; the results are a plain list of links
  (a `listbox` of options cannot hold links, and without script it could not be operated
  as one), named "Results", with `aria-live="polite"` so a swapped list is announced.
- Submitting the form (Enter or the button) re-renders with the server's results. Every
  result is a link that adds it to the selection (or replaces it, unless `multiple`), every
  chip has a link that removes it, and the "create" row is a plain post form.

**Accessibility:** a `<search>` form: a labelled search input with a datalist, results a
plain list of links named "Results" in an `aria-live` region, chips removable by named
links. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability
variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** filter as you type against the server or move
through results with arrow keys and a live `aria-activedescendant`; suggestions come from
the `<datalist>` sent with the page.

**Fallback:** none needed; `Caps` is accepted for uniformity and unused.

**Without script:** results update per round trip and the arrow keys do not move into
the list (Tab does). With the enhancement script the form is submitted as you type and
ArrowDown/ArrowUp walk the input and the results.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
// The text is `?q=` and the selection `?sel=`, read from the request.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/langs", "q=ru&sel=Zig", "");
let m = ui.combobox("q", "/langs")
    .group("Systems", ["Rust", "Zig"])
    .options(["Ruby"])
    .multiple()
    .create("/langs/new")
    .label("Language")
    .placeholder("Type a language");
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains("<optgroup label=\"Systems\">"));
assert!(html.contains("name=\"sel\" value=\"Zig\""), "the selection rides along with the next search");
assert!(html.contains("href=\"/langs?q=ru&amp;sel=Zig&amp;sel=Rust\""), "a result adds itself");
assert!(html.contains("href=\"/langs?q=ru\" aria-label=\"Remove Zig\""), "a chip removes itself");
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Combobox("q", "/langs") group=("Systems", ["Rust", "Zig"])
    options=(["Ruby"]) multiple create="/langs/new" label="Language"
    placeholder="Type a language"; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Load-more list

`loco_ui::pager` · demo: `/list`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Pager` | `ui.pager(href: &str, total: usize)` | stable |

## Props of `Pager`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `per_page` | number | `per_page: usize` | `10` |  | Rows per page. |
| `rows` | value | `row: impl Fn(usize) -> Markup + 'a` |  |  | Row `i` (0-based) of the list. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view-transition-name` | 111 | 144 | 18 |
| `scroll-margin` | 69 | 90 | 14.1 |

- Fallback: plain navigation to ?page=n#more
- Needs script: partly: click-to-load; scroll-to-load needs script
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: shadcn Pagination

## Documentation

A long list delivered a page at a time with a "Load more" link, no script.

**Platform features:**
- Ordinary links to `?page=n`. The key stays bare: a load-more list has no id, and a page
  holds one. A paged table beside it pages by its own `page.<id>` (see `crate::table`),
  so the two no longer move together.
- `view-transition-name` on the list, together with the layout's
  `@view-transition { navigation: auto }` (Chrome 126+, Safari 18.2+) or the enhancement
  script's `startViewTransition`, so the new rows fade in under the old ones. The button
  has no name on purpose: a named button morphs from its old spot to its new one, which
  reads as a green block sliding down over the fresh rows.
- `scroll-margin` + fragment `#more` keeps the viewport on the new rows after navigation.

**Accessibility:** a real link for "Load more"; the new rows land after an anchor so focus
and reading continue there. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route,
both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** infinite scroll or keeping the scroll position
across pages.

**Fallback:** without `Caps::ViewTransitions` the transition names are omitted and the page
navigates normally; the `#more` fragment still scrolls to the new rows.

**Finding:** true infinite scroll (loading on scroll) is impossible without script.
Cumulative pages (`?page=3` shows rows 1..3×N) give the same *feel* with one click per page.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
// `?page=2` of 30 rows, 10 at a time: rows 0 to 19 are shown.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/list", "page=2", "");
let list = ui.pager("/list", 30).per_page(10);
assert_eq!(list.shown(), 20);
let m = list.rows(|i| html! { "Row " (i + 1) }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("Row 20") && !m.contains("Row 21") && m.contains("?page=3#more"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Pager("/list", 30) per_page=10 rows=|i| { "Row " (i + 1) }; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
```

# Table

`loco_ui::table` · demo: `/app/notes`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Row` | `Row::new(cells: impl IntoIterator<Item = Markup>)` | stable |
| `Table` | `ui.table(id: &str, href: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Row`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | value | `key: &'a str` |  |  | The value posted for this row when its checkbox is ticked; also names its menu. |
| `detail` | value | `detail: Markup` |  |  | A block shown under the first cell when its `<details>` is opened. |
| `values` | value | `values: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a str>` |  |  | The raw text of each cell, in column order, for editing the row in place. |
| `menu` | value | `items: impl IntoIterator<Item = MenuItem<'a>>` |  |  | Items of the row's action menu (needs a `key`). |
| `href` | value | `href: &'a str` |  |  | The whole row links to `href`: a click anywhere on it that is not a control opens it. |
| `disabled` | switch |  | `off` |  | The row cannot be selected or opened: no checkbox, no row link, muted. |
| `ok` | switch |  | `off` |  | The row tinted with the `--lui-ok` tone. |
| `warn` | switch |  | `off` |  | The row tinted with the `--lui-warn` tone. |
| `danger` | switch |  | `off` |  | The row tinted with the `--lui-danger` tone. |

## Props of `Table`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `column` | item | `key: &'a str, label: &'a str` |  |  | A column. |
| `sortable` | modifier |  |  |  | The column added last sorts the table. |
| `filterable` | modifier |  |  |  | The column added last gets a text box in the "Filters" panel, `?q.<id>.<key>=`. |
| `numeric` | modifier |  |  |  | The column added last holds numbers. |
| `editable` | modifier |  |  |  | The column added last becomes a text box when its row is edited in place (`Table::edit`). |
| `edit` | value | `action: &'a str` |  |  | Rows (with a `Row::key`) can be edited in place. |
| `width` | modifier | `width: &'a str` |  |  | A CSS width for the column added last, such as `6rem` or `30%`. |
| `priority` | modifier | `priority: u8` | `1` |  | 1 always shown, 2 hidden in a narrow table, 3 below a medium one; values then show under the first cell. |
| `rows` | value | `rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = R>` |  |  | The rows, already sorted and filtered as `Table::sort` and `Table::filter` say: `Row`s, or tuples of cells. |
| `keep` | item | `name: &'a str` |  |  | A query parameter of this page (`status`) carried, with the request's value, by every sort link, the search form, the pager and the CSV link. |
| `filter_select` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str, options: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'a str, &'a str)>` |  |  | A `<select>` of `(value, text)` options in the search form, filtering by the query parameter `name`, which the table then keeps. |
| `hide_search` | switch |  | `off` |  | No search box (a display-only table, or one filtered by `filter_select` alone). |
| `paged` | number | `total: usize` |  |  | Page the rows. |
| `paged_from` | value | `meta: &PagerMeta` |  |  | Page the rows from what Loco's `query::fetch_page` or `query::paginate` returns (feature `loco`). |
| `choose_columns` | switch |  | `off` |  | A "Columns" chooser. |
| `bulk` | value | `action: &'a str, buttons: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'a str, &'a str)>` |  |  | A checkbox per row (rows need a `Row::key`) and a bar of `(value, label)` buttons posting to `action`. |
| `select_all` | switch |  | `off` |  | A header checkbox posting `all=1` to the bulk action, whose URL carries the query: every row the filter matches. |
| `csv` | value | `href: &'a str` |  |  | A "Download CSV" link to `href` with the current sort, filter and columns appended. |
| `json` | value | `href: &'a str` |  |  | A "Download JSON" link to `href` with the current sort, filter and columns appended. |
| `empty` | value | `message: impl Render` | `No rows match.` |  | What the body says when there are no rows: text, or markup (a call to action). |
| `loading` | condition | `loading: bool` | `off` |  | Skeleton rows with `aria-busy` instead of the rows. |
| `caption` | value | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A `<caption>` naming the table for assistive tech, visually hidden. |
| `total` | value | `key: &'a str, text: &'a str` |  |  | The cell of the column `key` in a totals row in `<tfoot>`. |
| `footer` | item | `row: impl Into<Row<'a>>` |  |  | A row in `<tfoot>`, after the totals. |
| `striped` | switch |  | `off` |  | Every other row on a gray band. |
| `density` | value | `density: Density` | `Density::Comfortable` |  | `Density::Compact` halves the cell padding. |
| `group_by` | value | `key: &'a str` |  |  | A group header row wherever the column `key`'s cell changes (rows sorted by it). |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `?sort.<id>=<col>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `<search>` | 118 | 118 | 17 |
| `aria-sort` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `form attribute` | 10 | 4 | 5.1 |
| `<details>` | 12 | 49 | 6 |
| `<colgroup>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `tabular-nums` | 52 | 34 | 9.1 |
| `position: sticky` | 56 | 32 | 13 |
| `view-transition-name` | 111 | 144 | 18 |
| `aria-busy` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: none needed: sorting, filtering, column choice and the bulk form are plain navigations and posts; select-all posts `all=1` with the query instead of ticking boxes
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: shadcn data table, Origin UI

## Documentation

A data table an admin panel can sort, filter, select from and act on, no script: every
column header is a link that re-requests the page sorted by that column (by several, in
order), a search box and per-column filters narrow the rows on the server, checkboxes
pick rows (or every matching row) for a bulk form, a "Columns" chooser hides columns
through `?cols.<id>=`, a row can expand a detail block, carry its own action menu, link
as a whole and take a tone, numbers line up, a `<tfoot>` holds totals, CSV and JSON links
download the current filter, and a row can be edited in place (`?edit.<id>=<key>` draws
it as text boxes posting to one form, Post/Redirect/Get).

**Platform features:**
- Ordinary links to `?sort.<id>=<col>` in each `<th>` (`-<col>` descending, a comma list
  for several keys: `name,-size`); clicking the first sort column again flips it, and
  once sorted, a "then by" link (`+`) beside another header adds it as the next key. The
  first key's header carries `aria-sort`; each sorted header shows its place when there
  are several.
- `<form method="get">` inside a `<search>` element (baseline 2023) for the filter; the
  sort, page size and hidden columns are kept in hidden inputs so filtering never loses
  them and the URL stays shareable. Column filters (`?q.<id>.<col>=`) sit in a
  `<details>` "Filters" panel of that form, open while one is set.
- Row selection through the form attribute (`form="id"`, Chrome 10, Firefox 4, Safari 5.1):
  each checkbox belongs to a
  bulk `<form method="post">` that sits after the table, so nothing nests and the row's
  own menu can still post. The row being edited uses the same attribute: its text boxes
  and "Save" belong to an edit form after the table, since a form cannot wrap a row.
- `<details>` (baseline 2020) in the first cell for a row's detail block; the row's menu
  is a `crate::Ui::menu`.
- `<colgroup>` widths and `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (Chrome 52, Firefox 34,
  Safari 9.1) for numeric columns.
- `position: sticky` (Chrome 56, Firefox 32, Safari 13) on the header row and the first
  column (`inset-inline-start: 0`, so it is the right edge in a right-to-left page).
- A row link is a link in a last cell whose `::after` box covers the row, which is
  `position: relative` (positioned table rows: Firefox 30, Chrome 91; Safari unchecked,
  see FINDINGS).
- `view-transition-name` on the body so re-sorted rows fade rather than jump.
- `aria-busy` on a loading body, drawn as skeleton bars, for a table filled by a later
  stream chunk.

**Accessibility:** a `<table>` with `scope="col"` headers, an optional hidden
`<caption>`, `aria-sort` on the first sort key, labelled filter and page-size controls,
visually hidden names for the select, edit, actions and link columns, `aria-disabled` on
a disabled row. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both
capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** resize or reorder columns by dragging (the
"Columns" chooser and `?cols.<id>=` choose and order them), collapse a group, or keep row
selection across sorts.

**Fallback:** none needed. Without `Caps::ViewTransitions` the transition name is
omitted; sorting, filtering, choosing columns and the bulk form are plain navigations and
posts either way.

**Without script:** ticking every box at once needs script. `.select_all()` instead puts
a box in the header that posts `all=1` with the table's query in the bulk form's URL, so
the server acts on every row the filter matches; the enhancement script also ticks the
visible boxes. Everything else works the same.

**Finding:** the server sorts and filters; the component only renders what it is given and
the links to ask for something else. That is what keeps it usable with `curl`.

**Query keys:** each carries the table's id, the way its page size (`per.<id>`) and in-place
edit (`edit.<id>`) do: `q.<id>`, `q.<id>.<col>`, `sort.<id>`, `page.<id>` and `cols.<id>`
(`Keys`), so two tables on one page sort, filter and page on their own. They live in the
URL only; the page size alone is state, remembered in the `lui-ui` cookie.

```rust
use loco_ui::{prelude::*, table::Row};
// The URL says: sorted by name, filtered to "a", only two columns shown.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/table", "sort.files=name&q.files=a&cols.files=name,size", "");
// `sortable`, `numeric` and `width` apply to the column added last.
let files = ui.table("files", "/table")
    .column("name", "Name").sortable()
    .column("size", "Size").sortable().numeric().width("6rem")
    .column("note", "Note")
    .choose_columns()
    .bulk("/files/bulk", [("archive", "Archive"), ("delete", "Delete")])
    .csv("/table.csv")
    .empty("No files yet.");
// The route fetches its data with what the table read from the URL.
assert_eq!((files.sort(), files.filter()), (&[("name", false)][..], "a"));
let row = Row::new([html! { "a.txt" }, html! { "1 KB" }, html! { "—" }])
    .key("a.txt")
    .detail(html! { p { "Modified today." } })
    .menu([MenuItem::link("Open", "/files/a.txt"), MenuItem::action("Delete", "/files/a.txt/delete").danger()]);
let html = files.rows([row.clone()]).render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains("aria-sort=\"ascending\""));
assert!(html.contains("<input type=\"checkbox\" class=\"lui-table-check\" name=\"row\" value=\"a.txt\" form=\"lui-table-files-bulk\""));
assert!(html.contains("href=\"/table.csv?sort.files=name&amp;q.files=a&amp;cols.files=name%2Csize\""));
assert!(!html.contains("<td>—</td>"), "a hidden column's cells are not rendered (its name stays in the chooser)");
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Table("files", "/table") choose_columns csv="/table.csv" empty="No files yet." {
    column "name" "Name" sortable;
    column "size" "Size" sortable numeric width="6rem";
    column "note" "Note";
    bulk "/files/bulk" ([("archive", "Archive"), ("delete", "Delete")]);
    rows ([row]);
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
// Priorities: 2 hides the column in a narrow table, 3 below a medium one; the values
// then show under the first cell.
let ui = Ui::default();
let t = ui.table("t", "/t").column("name", "Name").column("size", "Size").priority(2)
    .rows([(html! { "a.txt" }, html! { "1 KB" })]).render().into_string();
assert!(t.contains(r#"<td class="lui-table-p2">1 KB</td>"#) && t.contains(r#"<div class="lui-table-more-p2"><dt>Size</dt><dd>1 KB</dd>"#));
let same = lui! { Table("t", "/t") { column "name" "Name"; column "size" "Size" priority=2; rows ([(html! { "a.txt" }, html! { "1 KB" })]); } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), t);
```

**Fetching first, in `lui!`:** `Ui::table_query` reads the same sort, filter, page and page
size before the markup, and sorts and slices a `Vec` for you; rows can be tuples of
anything `Render`. A filter of the page's own (`?status=`) is a `.filter_select(..)` in the
search form, or a `.keep(..)` when the page draws it elsewhere: either way every sort link,
the search form and the pager carry it.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from_request("/orders", "status=paid&sort.orders=-total", "");
let orders = [(1, "Ada", "paid", 12.5_f64), (2, "Grace", "pending", 30.0), (3, "Ken", "paid", 20.0)];
let q = ui.table_query("orders", &["id", "total"]);
let status = ui.param("status").unwrap_or("");
let mut found: Vec<_> = orders.iter().filter(|o| (status.is_empty() || o.2 == status) && q.matches(o.1)).collect();
q.sort_by(&mut found, |a, b, key| match key { "total" => a.3.total_cmp(&b.3), _ => a.0.cmp(&b.0) });
let (page, total) = q.page_of(&found);
let html = lui! { Table("orders", "/orders") paged=(total) {
    column "id" "Order" sortable numeric;
    column "customer" "Customer";
    column "status" "Status";
    column "total" "Total" sortable numeric;
    filter_select "status" "Status" ([("", "All"), ("paid", "Paid"), ("pending", "Pending")]);
    rows (page.iter().map(|o| (o.0, o.1, ui.badge(o.2), format!("${:.2}", o.3))));
} }.into_string();
assert!(html.contains("<td>Ken</td>") && !html.contains("Grace"));
assert!(html.contains(r#"href="/orders?sort.orders=total&amp;status=paid&amp;"#), "kept by the sort links");
assert!(html.contains(r#"<option value="paid" selected>Paid</option>"#));
// A display-only table: no search box, no sortable column, no pager, so no link at all.
let recent = lui! { Table("recent", "") hide_search {
    column "who" "Who"; column "what" "What";
    rows ([("Ada", "upgraded to Pro"), ("Ken", "signed up")]);
} }.into_string();
assert!(!recent.contains("<a ") && !recent.contains("<form"));
```

**More of a data table:** column filters, select-all, a caption, totals and footer rows,
stripes, a compact density, group rows, row links, disabled and toned rows, JSON, and
markup when there are no rows.

```rust
use loco_ui::{prelude::*, table::Density};
let ui = Ui::from_request("/orders", "q.orders.customer=a&sort.orders=status,-total", "");
let q = ui.table_query("orders", &["status", "total"]);
let orders = [(1, "Ada", "paid", 12.5_f64), (2, "Grace", "due", 30.0), (3, "Ken", "paid", 20.0)];
let mut found: Vec<_> = orders.iter().filter(|o| q.matches_in("customer", o.1)).collect();
q.sort_by(&mut found, |a, b, key| match key { "total" => a.3.total_cmp(&b.3), _ => a.2.cmp(b.2) });
let row = |o: &&(u32, &'static str, &'static str, f64)| {
    let r = Row::from((o.0, o.1, o.2, format!("${:.2}", o.3))).href("/orders/1");
    if o.2 == "due" { r.warn() } else { r }
};
let html = ui.table("orders", "/orders")
    .column("id", "Order").numeric()
    .column("customer", "Customer").filterable()
    .column("status", "Status").sortable()
    .column("total", "Total").sortable().numeric()
    .bulk("/orders/bulk", [("archive", "Archive")]).select_all()
    .caption("Orders").total("total", "$32.50").striped().density(Density::Compact)
    .group_by("status").json("/orders.json").empty(html! { a href="/orders/new" { "Add an order" } })
    .rows(found.iter().map(row)).render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"<details class="lui-table-filters" open>"#) && html.contains(r#"name="q.orders.customer""#));
assert!(html.contains(r#"aria-label="Select all 2 matching rows""#));
assert!(html.contains(r#"<tr class="lui-table-group"><td colspan="6">paid</td></tr>"#));
assert!(html.contains("<tfoot>") && html.contains("$32.50"));
let same = lui! { Table("orders", "/orders") select_all caption="Orders" striped density=(Density::Compact)
        group_by="status" json="/orders.json" empty={ a href="/orders/new" { "Add an order" } } {
    column "id" "Order" numeric;
    column "customer" "Customer" filterable;
    column "status" "Status" sortable;
    column "total" "Total" sortable numeric;
    bulk "/orders/bulk" ([("archive", "Archive")]);
    total "total" "$32.50";
    rows (found.iter().map(row));
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Paged table

`loco_ui::paged_table`

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `?page.<id>=n` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `<select>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `<input type="number">` | 6 | 29 | 5.1 |
| `<output>` | 10 | 4 | 7 |

- Fallback: none needed: every control is a link or a form
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: shadcn data table, Origin UI

## Documentation

A `crate::Ui::table` with `.paged(total)`, for data too long for one page: first, previous, numbered, next and last
links with an ellipsis over long ranges, a jump-to-page form, a page-size `<select>`, and a
line saying which rows of how many are shown (`1–10 of 1,234`). Everything is a URL, so a
page can be bookmarked, and the sort, filter and columns survive paging.

**Platform features:**
- Ordinary links to `?page.<id>=n` that keep the table's sort, filter, columns and page
  size (`sort.<id>`, `q.<id>`, `q.<id>.<col>`, `cols.<id>`, `per.<id>`); the current page is `aria-current="page"` and the previous/next links are `rel="prev"` /
  `rel="next"`. Past seven pages only the first, the last and the current one's neighbours
  are numbered; the gaps are an `aria-hidden` ellipsis.
- `<form method="get">` with `<input type="number">` (`min`, `max`) to jump to a page, and another
  with a `<select>` for rows per page. Their buttons submit them, so both work with no script
  and by keyboard.
- The whole block (table and pager) is one swap root, so with the enhancement script a
  sort, filter, page or size change replaces both and the page links never go stale.
- `<output>` for the range, so assistive tech announces it as a result. Counts use a comma
  every three digits.

**Accessibility:** the pages are a `<nav>` named "Pages" of links with `rel=prev/next` and
`aria-current` on the current page; the page jump and page size are labelled forms. Checked
by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and
dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** load the next page on scroll; paging, sorting and
filtering are each a navigation.

**Fallback:** none needed. Every control is a link or a form.

**Server state:** the page size is `per.<id>`, a state key, so the size a visitor picked
is remembered in the `lui-ui` cookie and read back through `state.per_page(id)`. Every
page link still names it, so a shared URL shows the same rows for everyone. The page
itself (`page.<id>`), like the sort and the filter, is a query key only: a bookmark of the
bare path starts on page 1. Each key carries the table's id, so two paged tables on one page
page on their own.

```rust
use loco_ui::{prelude::*, table::Row};
// The URL's sort, filter and page, and the page size the visitor picked before.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/table", "sort.files=-name&q.files=a&page.files=20", "lui-ui=per.files=25");
let files = ui.table("files", "/table").column("name", "Name").sortable().column("note", "Note");
assert_eq!((files.page(), files.per_page()), (20, 25), "what a database query needs");
// Only this page's rows, and the total after filtering.
let html = files.rows([Row::new([html! { "a" }, html! { "b" }])]).paged(1234).render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains("476–500 of 1,234"));
assert!(html.contains("per.files=25&amp;page.files=50\">Last"));
assert!(html.contains("<select name=\"per.files\""));
```

# Wizard

`loco_ui::wizard` · demo: `/wizard`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Wizard` | `ui.wizard(id: &str, action: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Wizard`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `step` | item | `title: &'a str, body: impl Into<StepBody<'a>>` |  |  | A step titled `title` showing `body`. |
| `review` | item | `title: &'a str` |  |  | The last step. |
| `optional` | modifier |  |  |  | The step added last can be skipped. |
| `values` | value | `values: &'a [(String, String)]` |  |  | What the visitor entered so far, by field name, for every step's fields and the review. |
| `at` | number | `n: usize` |  |  | Show step `n` whatever the request says. |
| `errors` | value | `errors: &'a [(&'a str, &'a str)]` |  |  | Server messages `(field name, message)` for the posted step. |
| `finish` | value | `label: &'a str` | `Finish` |  | Label of the last step's submit button. |
| `hide_progress` | switch |  | `off` |  | No `<progress>` element (the connectors still show progress on screen). |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<form method="post">` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `aria-current="step"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `<fieldset>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `formnovalidate` | 4 | 4 | 5 |
| `<progress>` | 8 | 16 | 6 |

- Fallback: none needed: one form per step, PRG between them
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: Origin UI Stepper

## Documentation

A form split into steps, no script: each step is one `<form method="post">`, the server
checks it and either re-renders it with messages beside the fields or stores it and
redirects to the next step. Optional steps can be skipped, a progress bar shows how far
along the visitor is, the last step is a review whose every value links back to its step,
and a visitor who closes the tab comes back to the step they left.

The look follows the Origin UI Stepper: the progress is a `Steps` list,
numbered dots (a check when done) with the title and "optional" beside them, joined by
connectors that are the progress on screen (primary after a done step). A column in a
narrow container, a row from 30rem.

**Platform features:**
- Post/Redirect/Get per step: a redirect after each valid POST, so refresh never
  re-submits. An invalid POST answers with the same step, the values kept and the
  messages beside the fields (`Wizard::errors`), and the step list shows it in error.
- The current step is a `step.<id>` key in `crate::UiState`: it travels in `?step.<id>=n`
  and the `lui-ui` cookie, like a tab, so the URL of a step can be shared, Back/Forward in
  the browser work, and a bare visit resumes where the cookie says
  (`crate::UiState::remembered`) with a "Start over" link.
- `<ol>` step list with `aria-current="step"` on the current one; done steps are links.
- `<fieldset>` + `<legend>` for the step's fields, `<button name="skip" formnovalidate>`
  (baseline 2015) to skip an optional step without the browser checking its fields.
- `<progress>` (baseline 2015) for the steps done out of the total, read by assistive tech
  (visually hidden: the connectors show it); a container query (Chrome 105, Firefox 110,
  Safari 16) turns the step column into a row.
- `Wizard::review` renders the review as a `<dl>` with an "Edit" link per value.

**Accessibility:** an ordered list of steps with `aria-current="step"`, a labelled
`<progress>`, one `<fieldset>` per step with the step in its `<legend>`, `aria-invalid` on a
step with errors. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both
capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** keep the step inputs when the browser drops the form
on back; state travels in hidden fields and the query.

**Fallback:** none needed. Everything is a link or a form.

**Finding:** the entered values are the app's data, not UI state, so they do not belong
in the URL. The demo keeps them in one cookie; a real app would use its session store.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
// The request is on step 2 (0-based): the review.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/wizard", "step.signup=2", "");
let m = ui.wizard("signup", "/wizard")
    .step("Account", ui.fields().email("email", "Email").required().value("a@b.c"))
    .step("Newsletter", ui.fields().text("topics", "Topics")).optional()
    // Every field of the steps before, each with a link back to its step.
    .review("Review")
    .finish("Create account");
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains("aria-current=\"step\""));
assert!(html.contains("<progress class=\"lui-wizard-progress\" value=\"2\" max=\"2\""));
assert!(html.contains("href=\"/wizard?step.signup=0\" aria-label=\"Edit Email\""));
assert!(html.contains("(skipped)"), "an empty value");
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Wizard("signup", "/wizard") {
    step "Account" (ui.fields().email("email", "Email").required().value("a@b.c"));
    step "Newsletter" (ui.fields().text("topics", "Topics")) optional;
    review "Review";
    finish "Create account";
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Validated form

`loco_ui::form` · demo: `/app/signin`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Form` | `ui.form(action: &str)` | stable |
| `Form` | `ui.fields()` | stable |

## Props of `Form`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | item | `legend: &'a str` |  |  | A `<fieldset>` with this `<legend>` around the fields added after it. |
| `description` | modifier | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A line under the legend of the group added last. |
| `text` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str` |  |  | Single-line text. |
| `password` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str` |  |  | `type="password"`. |
| `email` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str` |  |  | `type="email"`. |
| `number` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str, min: impl Into<Bound>, max: impl Into<Bound>` |  |  | A number from `min` to `max`, inclusive. |
| `pattern` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str, pattern: &'a str, hint: &'a str` |  |  | Text that must match `pattern` (the HTML `pattern` attribute). |
| `textarea` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str, rows: u8` |  |  | Multi-line text, `rows` high. |
| `file` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str, accept: &'a str` |  |  | A file picker. |
| `date` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str, min: &'a str, max: &'a str` |  |  | `type="date"`, bounds as `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| `time` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str, min: &'a str, max: &'a str` |  |  | `type="time"`, bounds as `HH:MM`. |
| `datetime` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str, min: &'a str, max: &'a str` |  |  | `type="datetime-local"`, bounds as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`. |
| `select` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str, options: impl IntoIterator<Item = O>` |  |  | A `<select>` of `options`: `&str`s, or `(value, label)` pairs. |
| `radio` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str, options: impl IntoIterator<Item = O>` |  |  | Radio buttons under a legend, one per option: `&str`s, or `(value, label)` pairs. |
| `checkboxes` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str, options: impl IntoIterator<Item = O>` |  |  | Checkboxes under a legend posting `<name>[]`, one per option. |
| `search` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str` |  |  | `type="search"`. |
| `url` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str` |  |  | `type="url"`. |
| `tel` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str` |  |  | `type="tel"`. |
| `color` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str` |  |  | A colour picker with its swatch. |
| `range` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str, min: impl Into<f64>, max: impl Into<f64>` |  |  | A slider from `min` to `max`, its value beside it. |
| `checkbox` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str` |  |  | A checkbox posting `true` when ticked and nothing when not (so a `bool` with `#[serde(default)]` reads it). |
| `switch` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str` |  |  | A checkbox drawn as an on/off switch, posting like `.checkbox(..)`. |
| `hidden` | item | `name: &'a str, value: &'a str` |  |  | `type="hidden"`. |
| `body` | item | `markup: Markup` |  |  | Any markup at this point among the fields: a control built with its own setters. |
| `required` | modifier |  |  |  | The `required` attribute, and a `*` after the label; the form says what the star means. |
| `optional` | modifier |  |  |  | "(optional)" after the label. |
| `disabled` | modifier |  |  | `disabled` | `disabled` and `aria-disabled`: shown greyed and not posted. |
| `readonly` | modifier |  |  |  | Shown and posted, not editable; a posted value never replaces it. |
| `help` | modifier | `help: &'a str` |  |  | Help text under the field. |
| `maxlength` | modifier | `max: usize` |  |  | `maxlength`, counted in an `<output>` under the field. |
| `value` | modifier | `value: &'a str` |  | `value` | The field's current value (ignored for files). |
| `checked` | modifier | `checked: bool` |  |  | Tick the checkbox. |
| `error` | modifier | `message: &'a str` |  |  | A server message beside the field. |
| `placeholder` | modifier | `placeholder: &'a str` |  |  | Placeholder text. |
| `multiple` | modifier |  |  |  | The file picker takes several files; a select, several options. |
| `autocomplete` | modifier | `value: &'a str` |  | `autocomplete` | `autocomplete` (`"email"`, `"new-password"`, `"off"`). |
| `width` | modifier | `width: impl Into<Size>` |  |  | A narrower control: 1 (8rem), 2 (16rem) or 3 (24rem). |
| `submit` | value | `label: &'a str` | `Submit` |  | Label of the submit button. |
| `action_secondary` | value | `label: &'a str, href: &'a str` |  |  | A second action beside the submit button, a link (Cancel, Back). |
| `method_override` | value | `method: &'a str` |  |  | A hidden `_method` (`"delete"`, `"put"`) that `loco::method_override` turns into the request's method. |
| `inline` | switch |  | `off` |  | Labels beside the fields on screens wider than 40rem, above them on narrower ones. |
| `get` | switch |  | `off` |  | `method="get"`: the fields go in the URL of the page it answers with (a filter, a search). |
| `values` | value | `values: &'a [(String, String)]` |  |  | Submitted values by field name, as a form post parses them. |
| `errors` | value | `errors: &'a [(&'a str, &'a str)]` |  |  | Server messages `(field name, message)`. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | What the swap root's id is built from, when two forms on a page post to the same action (one per tab, say). |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `required` | 4 | 4 | 5 |
| `pattern` | 4 | 4 | 5 |
| `:user-invalid` | 119 | 88 | 16.5 |
| `<fieldset>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `<output>` | 10 | 4 | 7 |
| `type=date` | 20 | 57 | 14.1 |
| `accept` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `field-sizing` | 123 | no | no |

- Fallback: server re-renders with messages; no early styling; textareas keep their rows; the counter shows the submitted length
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: shadcn Forms, Radix Themes

## Documentation

A validated form: the browser blocks bad input before submit, the server checks again and
re-renders with messages. Fields come in groups with legends, carry help text, count their
characters, take files, dates, times and bounded numbers, and lay out stacked (label above)
or inline (label beside). No script needed.

The look follows the shadcn Forms examples and the Radix Themes settings layouts: a group
is a section (a heading, an optional `.description(..)` and its fields) drawn without a
frame, a hairline between sections. The form is its own container: `.inline()` puts the
label and its help beside the field once the form is 30rem wide, and the submit button
fills a narrower form and sits at the end of a wider one.

**Platform features:**
- Constraint validation attributes `required`, `pattern`, `min`, `max`, `maxlength`,
  `type=email` (baseline 2015); `type=date` and `type=time` with `min`/`max` (Chrome 20,
  Firefox 57, Safari 14.1).
- `:user-invalid` / `:user-valid` (baseline 2023): styles only after the user has interacted,
  so fields are not red on first paint.
- `<fieldset>` + `<legend>` per `Form::group`, described by its `.description(..)`; help
  text and the error are tied to the field with `aria-describedby`.
- Container queries (Chrome 105, Firefox 110, Safari 16) for the side labels and the
  submit row.
- `<output>` counts characters for a field with a `maxlength`: the server renders the count
  of the value it has, the enhancement script keeps it live while typing.
- `<input type=file accept>` (baseline 2015); any file field makes the form
  `enctype="multipart/form-data"`.
- `field-sizing` (Chrome 123, not yet in Firefox or Safari): a textarea grows with its
  content.
- Post/Redirect/Get for success; on error the server re-renders the form with values and
  messages, and an error summary at the top that links to each
  field in error and takes the focus.

**Accessibility:** labelled fields grouped in `<fieldset>`/`<legend>`, native constraint
validation, and an error summary that takes the focus when the server sends the form back.
Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light
and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** validate against the server as you type, or warn
about unsaved changes on leaving the page.

**Fallback:** without container queries the labels stay above the fields and the button
fills the form's width. Without `field-sizing` a textarea keeps its `rows` and can be resized by
hand. Without the script the counter shows the length of the last submitted value and
`maxlength` still stops input at the limit.

**Enhanced:** the form is a swap root, so with the `crate::enhance` script a submit
replaces only the form (errors included) and a successful redirect swaps in the result.

**Finding:** custom cross-field rules (password confirmation, async uniqueness) only run
on the server round trip, and warning about unsaved changes when leaving needs script.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
let m = ui.form("/signup").email("email", "Email").required();
assert!(m.render().into_string().contains(r#"type="email" value="" required"#));

// `required`, `help`, `maxlength`, `value` and friends apply to the field added last;
// `group` starts a fieldset for the fields after it.
let m = ui.form("/profile")
    .group("About you").description("Shown on your public page.")
    .textarea("bio", "Bio", 3).maxlength(280).value("Hi").help("Shown on your profile.")
    .file("avatar", "Avatar", "image/png,image/jpeg")
    .date("born", "Born", "1900-01-01", "2026-12-31")
    .select("digest", "Digest", ["daily", "weekly", "never"]).value("weekly")
    .submit("Save profile")
    .inline();
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains("enctype=\"multipart/form-data\""));
assert!(html.contains(r#"<legend class="lui-form-group-legend">About you</legend>"#));
assert!(html.contains(r#"aria-describedby="lui-form-about-you-description""#));
assert!(html.contains(">2 / 280</output>"));
assert!(html.contains("accept=\"image/png,image/jpeg\""));
assert!(html.contains(r#"<option value="weekly" selected>"#));

// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Form("/profile") submit="Save profile" inline {
    group "About you" description="Shown on your public page.";
    textarea "bio" "Bio" 3 maxlength=280 value="Hi" help="Shown on your profile.";
    file "avatar" "Avatar" "image/png,image/jpeg";
    date "born" "Born" "1900-01-01" "2026-12-31";
    select "digest" "Digest" (["daily", "weekly", "never"]) value="weekly";
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m.render().into_string());
```

**Any control.** `.switch(..)` adds a switch like a checkbox, and `.body(..)` puts any
markup at that point among the fields (a date picker, a range, a toggle group, a select
built with its own setters), so it sits inside the form's swap root, under its error
summary and before its button. `.get()` makes it a GET form: a filter or a search whose
answer is a page with the choices in its URL.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from_request("/filters", "size=l", "");
let m = ui.form("/filters")
    .get()
    .text("q", "Search")
    .switch("open", "Open only").checked(true)
    .body(html! { (ui.select("size", "Size").options([("s", "Small"), ("l", "Large")])) })
    .submit("Apply");
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"method="get" action="/filters""#));
assert!(html.contains(r#"role="switch""#) && html.contains(r#"<option value="l" selected>"#));
assert!(html.find("f-size") < html.find("lui-form-actions"), "the markup before the button");
// The same in `lui!`: a block of markup among the items is `body { .. }`, and a block with
// no items at all is the body.
let same = lui! { Form("/filters") get submit="Apply" {
    text "q" "Search";
    switch "open" "Open only" checked=(true);
    body { Select("size", "Size") options=([("s", "Small"), ("l", "Large")]); }
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Error summary

`loco_ui::error_summary`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `ErrorSummary` | `ui.error_summary(errors: &[(&str, &str)])` | beta |

## Props of `ErrorSummary`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | value | `text: &'a str` | `There is a problem` |  | The heading. |
| `field` | item | `name: &'a str, label: &'a str` |  |  | The label of the field `name`, written before its message as a form's summary does. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `role="alert"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `aria-labelledby` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `autofocus` | 79 | 110 | 15.4 |

- Fallback: where autofocus only works on form controls the summary is still first in the form and read out as an alert
- Needs script: partly: moving the focus into the field a link points to needs script
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Callout

## Documentation

The list of what went wrong, at the top of a form the server sent back (GOV.UK's error
summary): a heading, then one link per field in error that jumps to the field. The page
opens with the focus on it, so a keyboard or screen reader user starts at the problems
instead of hunting for them. `Form` shows one by itself whenever it
has messages; `ui.error_summary(..)` is for a form built from loose inputs.

**Platform features:**
- `role="alert"` (read out when the page loads) with `aria-labelledby` naming the heading.
- `autofocus` on the heading's link (global attribute on any focusable element: Chrome
  79, Firefox 110, Safari 15.4): the focus starts in the summary.
- Fragment links (`href="#f-email"`) to each field's `id`.

**Accessibility:** `role="alert"` named by its heading; the heading link has `autofocus`,
each item links to its field by id. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo
route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** move the focus into the field a link points to;
the page scrolls to it, and Tab goes on from there.

**Fallback:** where `autofocus` only works on form controls, the summary is still the
first thing in the form and is read out as an alert.

**Enhanced:** when the enhancement script swaps a form in place, it focuses the
`autofocus` element of the new markup too, as a page load would.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let errors = [("email", "Enter an email address."), ("password", "At least 8 characters.")];
let m = ui.error_summary(&errors).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r##"<a href="#f-email" autofocus>There is a problem</a>"##));
assert!(m.contains(r##"<li><a href="#f-password">At least 8 characters.</a></li>"##));
assert!(ui.error_summary(&[]).render().into_string().is_empty());

// With the fields' labels, each message reads as a form's summary writes it.
let m = ui.error_summary(&errors).field("email", "Email").title("Check your details");
let m = m.render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"role="alert""#) && m.contains(">Check your details</a>"));
assert!(m.contains(r##"<a href="#f-email">Email: Enter an email address.</a>"##));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { ErrorSummary(&errors) title="Check your details" { field "email" "Email"; } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
```

# Counter

`loco_ui::counter` · demo: `/counter`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Counter` | `ui.counter(action: &str, value: impl Into<f64>)` | stable |

## Props of `Counter`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `min` | number | `min: impl Into<f64>` |  | `min` | Lowest value. |
| `max` | number | `max: impl Into<f64>` |  | `max` | Highest value. |
| `step` | number | `step: impl Into<f64>` | `1` | `step` | How far one click moves (above 0). |
| `typed` | switch |  | `off` |  | A number field and a Set button posting `op=set&value=n`. |
| `disabled` | switch |  | `off` | `disabled` | Every button and the number field disabled. |
| `readonly` | switch |  | `off` |  | The value shown, its buttons off and the number field `readonly`. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<form method="post">` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `<button name value>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `<input type="number">` | 6 | 29 | 5.1 |
| `cookie` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: -

## Documentation

The canonical "click me" demo done with a form round trip. State lives on the server
(here: a cookie), no script.

**Platform features:** `<form method="post">`, `<button name value>` so one form carries
several actions, Post/Redirect/Get, and `view-transition-name` (only when `Caps` says the
browser has view transitions) so the number morphs instead of flashing. With
`.min()`, `.max()`, `.step()` and `.typed()` the buttons are `disabled` at `min` and `max`, step by `step`, and the
value can be typed into an `<input type="number">` with `min`, `max`, `step` (baseline 2015), posted
with `op=set`; the browser refuses a typed value off the bounds or the step.

**Accessibility:** native buttons named "increment" and "decrement" (disabled at the
bounds), a labelled number field, the bounds in text. Checked by axe-core in headless
Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or
critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** change the number without a round trip; each step is
a POST and a redirect.

**Fallback:** without view transitions the page simply reloads.

**Enhanced:** the form is a swap root (`data-lui="swap"`), so with the `crate::enhance`
script each click is a background POST and only the form is replaced; rapid clicks queue.

**Finding:** without the script every click is a full navigation, and a click that lands
while the page unloads is dropped. There is no optimistic update and no offline behaviour.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
let plain = ui.counter("/counter", 3);
let bounded = ui.counter("/counter", 10).min(0).max(10).step(2).typed();
let html = bounded.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains("value=\"inc\" aria-label=\"increment\" disabled"));
assert!(html.contains("name=\"value\" type=\"number\" value=\"10\" min=\"0\" max=\"10\" step=\"2\""));
// The handler's half: the same counter applies the posted `op`, clamped to its bounds.
assert_eq!(bounded.apply("dec", None), 8.0);

// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Counter("/counter", 10) min=0 max=10 step=2 typed; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), bounded.render().into_string());
```

# Theme toggle

`loco_ui::theme`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `ThemeToggle` | `ui.theme_toggle(action: &str)` | stable |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prefers-color-scheme` | 76 | 67 | 12.1 |
| `color-scheme` | 81 | 96 | 13 |
| `cookie` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: OS preference
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes SegmentedControl

## Documentation

Light/dark theme chosen by the user and remembered by the server.

**Platform features:** `prefers-color-scheme` (baseline 2020), `color-scheme` property,
CSS custom properties. The toggle is a `<form method="post">`; the server stores the choice
in a cookie and sets `data-theme` on `<html>`.

**Accessibility:** three native buttons with `aria-pressed` on the current theme. Checked by
axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark
(no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** follow a change of the OS preference while a cookie
choice is set; the cookie wins until reset to auto.

**Fallback:** none needed. Without a cookie the OS preference wins. Colours are switched by
a media query and `data-theme`, so `light-dark()` support (`Caps::LightDark`) is only
reported, never required. The form is a swap root: the `crate::enhance` script applies
the new `data-theme` without a reload.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from_request("/", "", "theme=dark");
let m = ui.theme_toggle("/theme").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"value="dark" aria-pressed="true""#));

// The handler the toggle posts to keeps the choice for a year.
let r = ui.redirect("/").theme(Theme::parse("light"));
assert!(r.set_cookies()[0].starts_with("theme=light;"));

// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { ThemeToggle("/theme"); };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
```

# Flash

`loco_ui::flash` · demo: `/settings`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Flash` | `ui.flash()` | stable |

## Props of `Flash`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dismiss` | switch |  | `off` |  | A dismiss link on each message, back to this page (which no longer has the flash). |
| `auto_hide` | switch |  | `off` |  | Fade calm messages out after a few seconds. |
| `variant` | choice: solid, soft, surface, outline, ghost | `variant: Variant` | `soft` |  | Each message's callout: soft, surface or outline, as on an alert. |
| `title` | value | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A bold line over each message. |
| `action` | value | `label: &'a str, href: &'a str` |  |  | A link button under each message ("Undo", "View"). |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cookie` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `role="status"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `role="alert"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `@keyframes` | 43 | 16 | 9 |
| `prefers-reduced-motion` | 74 | 63 | 10.1 |

- Fallback: without CSS animations the message stays
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Callout

## Documentation

One-shot status messages that survive a Post/Redirect/Get, no script. Four levels
(`info`, `ok`, `warn`, `danger`), several at once stacked in arrival order, an optional
dismiss link, and an optional auto-hide for the calm levels. Each message is an alert's
callout, soft unless `.variant(..)` makes them surface or outline. `.title(..)` puts a
bold line over each message and `.action(..)` a link button under it.

**Platform features:** a cookie with `Max-Age=60` set by `crate::Ui::redirect` on the
redirect, read on the next request through `UiState`, and cleared by the next
`crate::Ui::page` that shows it. `role="status"` announces info, ok and warn politely;
`role="alert"` announces danger at once. Auto-hide is a CSS animation
(`@keyframes`, `animation-fill-mode: forwards`) that `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`
switches off, so the message then stays until the next page.

The cookie value is plain text: one message per line, each optionally prefixed with its
level (`ok:Saved.`). A line without a known prefix is `info`. `ui.redirect(to).ok(..)`
writes it; `stack` builds the same text by hand.

**Dismiss:** a link back to the page (`.dismiss()`). Reading the flash already
queued the cookie's deletion on that response, so following the link renders the page
without it; with `/lui/enhance.js` inside a swap root it updates in place.

**Accessibility:** `role="status"` for information, `role="alert"` for errors; the dismiss
link is named with the message. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route,
both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** it cannot vanish in place when dismissed; the
dismiss link is a navigation.

**Fallback:** without CSS animations the message stays; nothing else differs.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from_request("/settings", "", "lui-flash=Saved.");
let m = ui.flash().render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("lui-flash-info") && m.contains("Saved."));
assert_eq!(Ui::default().flash().render().into_string(), "", "no message, no banner");

// What `ui.redirect("/settings").ok("Saved.").danger("Avatar too large.")` sends, shown
// with a dismiss link and auto-hide.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/settings", "", "lui-flash=ok%3ASaved.%0Adanger%3AAvatar%20too%20large.");
let m = ui.flash().dismiss().auto_hide().render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"role="alert""#) && m.contains("lui-flash-auto"));
assert_eq!(m.matches(r#"href="/settings""#).count(), 2);

// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Flash dismiss auto_hide; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// Outlined callouts instead of tinted ones.
let m = ui.flash().variant(Variant::Outline).render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<div class="lui-flash" data-variant="outline">"#) && m.contains("lui-callout-outline"));
assert_eq!(lui! { Flash variant="outline"; }.into_string(), m);
// A title over the message and a link under it.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/notes", "", "lui-flash=ok%3ANote%20moved%20to%20Archive.");
let m = ui.flash().title("Moved").action("Open Archive", "/archive").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<p class="lui-flash-title">Moved</p><p class="lui-flash-text">Note moved to Archive.</p>"#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"href="/archive""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Flash title="Moved" action=("Open Archive", "/archive"); }.into_string(), m);
```

# UI state

`loco_ui::state`

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `links` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `cookies` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `303 See Other` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: without cookies, state still travels in links on one page
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: -

## Documentation

Where UI state lives when there is no script: in the URL and in a cookie.

`UiState` is a small string map with five kinds of keys: `tab.<name>` (open tab index),
`open.<group>` (open accordion indexes, a comma list), `step.<wizard>` (current wizard step),
`per.<table>` (rows per page of a paged table) and `dialog` (id of a dialog to render open). It is
read from the query string first and a `lui-ui` cookie second, so a link can change one key
while everything else is remembered. In Axum it is an extractor, and returning it as part
of the response writes the cookie back when the query changed something.

**State or query.** A table's other keys (`q.<id>`, `q.<id>.<col>`, `sort.<id>`, `page.<id>`,
`cols.<id>`, `edit.<id>`) are named the same way but are not state: they describe one view
and live in the URL only, read with `ui.param` by the table (`crate::table::Keys`). Only
what a visitor would expect to find again on their next visit (a tab, an open section, a
wizard step, a page size) is remembered.

**One cookie for the site.** Keys are site-wide: two tab groups with one id share a
memory, so give each its own id. Every browser tab writes the same cookie, and the last
page view wins. The value stays under `MAX_COOKIE` bytes by dropping remembered keys this
request did not set. It is `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` over HTTPS, and readable by page
script, since it holds nothing but view preferences.

**Platform features:** links, cookies, `303 See Other`. Nothing newer than 1997.

**Fallback:** none needed. Without cookies, state still travels in links on the same page.

**Post/Redirect/Get:** `crate::Ui::redirect` answers a form POST with a redirect and a
one-shot `lui-flash` cookie; the next page renders it with `ui.flash()` and, as a
`crate::Page`, clears it.

**Any server.** The protocol is plain strings: `UiState::from_request` reads path, query
and the `Cookie:` header; `UiState::set_cookies` gives the `Set-Cookie` values to send
back. The `axum` feature adds the extractor and the `IntoResponseParts` impl on top.

```rust
use loco_ui::UiState;
let state = UiState::parse("/settings", "tab.settings=1&page.files=3", "open.faq=2");
assert_eq!(state.tab("settings"), 1);
assert_eq!(state.open("faq"), Some(2));
assert_eq!(state.link("tab.settings", "0"), "/settings?open.faq=2&tab.settings=0");

// By hand, from a raw request: the cookie header carries both state and flash.
let state = UiState::from_request("/settings", "tab.settings=1", "lui-ui=open.faq=2; lui-flash=Saved.");
assert_eq!(state.flash(), Some("Saved."));
assert_eq!(state.set_cookies().len(), 2); // remember tab.settings, clear the flash

# Select

`loco_ui::select` · demo: `/inputs`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Select` | `ui.select(name: &str, label: &str)` | stable |
| `SelectOption` | `SelectOption::new(value: &str, text: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Select`
