| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `options` | value | `options: impl IntoIterator<Item = O>` |  |  | Options with no `<optgroup>`. |
| `group` | value | `label: &'a str, options: impl IntoIterator<Item = O>` |  |  | Options under `<optgroup label>`. |
| `groups` | value | `groups: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'a str, G)>` |  |  | Several labelled groups at once. |
| `search` | value | `action: &'a str` |  |  | A filter box submitting `<name>-q` to `action` with GET. |
| `search_over` | number | `n: usize` | `15` |  | Show the filter box above this many options (default 15). |
| `value` | value | `value: &'a str` |  |  | The chosen option's value, instead of the query's `name` (once more per pick with `.multiple()`). |
| `error` | value | `message: &'a str` |  |  | A server message under the select, which gets `aria-invalid`. |
| `help` | value | `help: &'a str` |  |  | Help text under the select. |
| `placeholder` | value | `placeholder: &'a str` |  |  | A first option posting nothing ("Choose…"), picked until another is. |
| `required` | switch |  | `off` | `required` | An option other than the placeholder must be picked. |
| `disabled` | switch |  | `off` | `disabled` | `disabled` and `aria-disabled`: shown greyed and not posted. |
| `readonly` | switch |  | `off` |  | Shown and posted, not changeable: a disabled select and a hidden input per picked value. |
| `multiple` | switch |  | `off` | `multiple` | Several options may be picked (a list box; no rich trigger). |
| `hide_label` | switch |  | `off` |  | Only the select, the label kept as its `aria-label`. |
| `size` | choice: 1, 2, 3 | `size: impl Into<Size>` | `2` |  | The trigger's height and text: Radix's sizes 1 to 3. |
| `variant` | choice: solid, soft, surface, outline, ghost | `variant: Variant` | `surface` |  | The trigger's look: surface (a border), soft (a tint) or ghost (neither). |

## Props of `SelectOption`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | value | `icon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An icon before the label. |
| `body` | value | `content: Markup` |  |  | Rich markup instead of the text (with `Caps::BaseSelect` only). |
| `disabled` | switch |  | `off` | `disabled` | Shown, but cannot be picked. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<selectedcontent>` | 135 | no | 27 |
| `appearance: base-select` | 135 | no | 27 |
| `<optgroup label>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `formmethod` | 9 | 4 | 5.1 |

- Fallback: plain <select>, chosen server-side
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Select

## Documentation

A `<select>` whose closed state shows the chosen option's full content, no script. Options
come in labelled groups and can carry an icon; a long list gets a filter box.

**Platform features:**
- `<select>` with a `<button>` first child holding `<selectedcontent>` (Chrome 135, Safari
  27; Firefox behind flags): the button is the closed control and `<selectedcontent>`
  mirrors the picked option's markup into it, so options can carry a swatch or an icon.
- `appearance: base-select` on the select and its `::picker(select)` pseudo-element hands
  both to author CSS.
- `<optgroup label>` (baseline) for `Select::group`.
- A filter box when there are more than `Select::search_over` options: an
  `<input type="search" name="<name>-q">` and a button with `formmethod="get"` and
  `formaction` (baseline 2015), so filtering re-requests the page through the enclosing
  form without saving it. The server renders only the options whose text contains the
  query, and always the selected one.

**Accessibility:** a native `<select>` with its `<label>`; the filter box is a labelled
search field. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability
variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** type-ahead search beyond what the browser offers;
long lists get a server-side filter box instead.

**Fallback:** without `Caps::BaseSelect` a plain `<select>` with plain options (icons as
text before the label). Older parsers also drop a `<button>` inside `<select>`, so the
enhanced markup is only emitted when the browser is known to want it.

**Enhanced:** the enhancement script filters as you type, through the same GET.

```rust
use loco_ui::{prelude::*, select::SelectOption};
// The chosen value is the query's `food`, as a form posted back by GET leaves it.
let mut ui = Ui::from_request("/shop", "food=leek&food-q=k", "");
ui.caps = Caps::all();
// Plain tuples of (value, label) or (value, label, icon) are options.
let m = ui.select("size", "Size").options([("s", "Small", "🐭"), ("l", "Large", "🐘")]).value("l");
let m = m.render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("<selectedcontent>") && m.contains(r#"<label for="f-size">Size</label>"#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"<option value="l" selected>"#));
// A server error, linked from the error summary like a form field's.
let bad = ui.select("size", "Size").options([("s", "Small")]).error("Pick a size.");
assert!(bad.render().into_string().contains(r#"aria-describedby="f-size-error""#));

let m = ui.select("food", "Food")
    .group("Fruit", [SelectOption::new("apple", "Apple"), SelectOption::new("kiwi", "Kiwi").body(html! { b { "Kiwi" } })])
    .group("Vegetables", [("leek", "Leek")])
    .search("/shop")
    .search_over(2);
let m = m.render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("<optgroup label=\"Fruit\">") && !m.contains("Apple"), "filtered to 'k'");
assert!(m.contains("formmethod=\"get\" formaction=\"/shop\""));

// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Select("food", "Food") search="/shop" search_over=2 {
    group "Fruit" ([
        SelectOption::new("apple", "Apple"),
        SelectOption::new("kiwi", "Kiwi").body(html! { b { "Kiwi" } }),
    ]);
    group "Vegetables" ([("leek", "Leek")]);
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// A small soft trigger.
let sort = ui.select("sort", "Sort").options([("new", "Newest")]).size(1).variant(Variant::Soft);
let sort = sort.render().into_string();
assert!(sort.contains(r#"<span class="lui-select" data-size="1" data-variant="soft">"#));
let same = lui! { Select("sort", "Sort") options=([("new", "Newest")]) size=1 variant="soft"; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), sort);
```

# Range

`loco_ui::range` · demo: `/inputs`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Range` | `ui.range(name: &str, label: &str)` | stable |
| `Range` | `ui.range_pair(name: &str, label: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Range`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | number | `value: impl Into<f64>` |  | `value` | The value (a pair's low one), instead of the query's. |
| `values` | value | `low: impl Into<f64>, high: impl Into<f64>` |  |  | A pair's two values, put in order, instead of the query's. |
| `min` | number | `min: impl Into<f64>` | `0` | `min` | Lowest value. |
| `max` | number | `max: impl Into<f64>` | `100` | `max` | Highest value. |
| `step` | number | `step: impl Into<f64>` | `1` | `step` | Distance between allowed values (above 0). |
| `disabled` | switch |  | `off` | `disabled` | `disabled` and `aria-disabled`: shown greyed and not posted. |
| `readonly` | switch |  | `off` |  | Shown and posted, not movable: a disabled slider and a hidden input with its value. |
| `ticks` | switch |  | `off` |  | The lowest, middle and highest values marked under the track. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The slider's id, `f-<name>` by default. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<input type="range">` | 4 | 23 | 3.1 |
| `<datalist>` | 20 | 110 | 12.1 |
| `pointer-events` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: ticks not drawn
- Needs script: partly: value shown after submit; live mirroring needs script
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Slider

## Documentation

A slider whose value the server remembers, no script.

**Platform features:** `<input type="range">` (Chrome 4, Firefox 23, Safari 3.1) with
`min`, `max`, `step`, and an `<output>` that shows the value the server last saw. A
`list` of `<datalist>` ticks (Chrome 20, Firefox 110, Safari 12.1) labels the stops.

`Ui::range_pair` is a min/max pair: two range inputs (`<name>_min`, `<name>_max`) laid over
one track in a CSS grid cell. The track ignores the pointer (`pointer-events: none`) and
only the thumbs take it (`::-webkit-slider-thumb`, `::-moz-range-thumb`), so either thumb
can be dragged. Each has its own `<output>`.

**Accessibility:** native range inputs, each named (the pair's thumbs as "Minimum" and
"Maximum"); the value is shown in an `<output>`. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on
every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical
violation).

**What it does not do without script:** show the value while dragging (the `<output>` holds
the value the server last saw), or stop the two thumbs of a pair crossing; the server
reorders them with `order`.

**Fallback:** none needed. Without `list` support the ticks are simply not drawn. A pair
whose thumbs cross posts a low above the high; `order` swaps them back on the server.

The look follows Radix Themes Slider: a thin gray track filled in the primary colour up to
the value (between the thumbs for a pair; `--lui-range-fill`, or `--lui-range-lo` and
`--lui-range-hi`, set by the server), a round white thumb, and `.ticks()` for the lowest,
middle and highest values under the track. The value stays beside the slider: CSS cannot
place a label over a thumb that moves without script.

**Enhanced:** the enhancement script mirrors each slider into its `<output for>` and its
fill while it moves. Without it the `<output>` shows the value the server last saw.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
// The values are the query's (`volume`; `price_min` and `price_max` for a pair), or
// `.value(..)` and `.values(..)` (saved ones).
let ui = Ui::from_request("/", "volume=40&price_min=80&price_max=20", "");
let m = ui.range("volume", "Volume").step(5).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<label for="f-volume">Volume</label>"#) && m.contains("<output for=\"f-volume\">40</output>"));
assert!(ui.range("volume", "Volume").value(70).render().into_string().contains("<output for=\"f-volume\">70</output>"));
assert!(m.contains(r#"style="--lui-range-fill: 40%""#));
let ticked = ui.range("volume", "Volume").ticks().render().into_string();
assert!(ticked.contains(r#"<div class="lui-range-ticks" aria-hidden="true"><span>0</span>"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Range("volume", "Volume") ticks; }.into_string(), ticked);
// A pair posted the wrong way round is put back in order.
let m = ui.range_pair("price", "Price").step(10).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("name=\"price_min\"") && m.contains("name=\"price_max\""));
assert!(m.contains("<output for=\"f-price_min\">20</output>"));

// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { RangePair("price", "Price") step=10; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
```

# Color

`loco_ui::color` · demo: `/inputs`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Color` | `ui.color(name: &str, label: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Color`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | value | `value: &'a str` |  | `value` | The `#rrggbb` colour, instead of the query's `name`. |
| `presets` | value | `presets: &'a [&'a str]` |  |  | `#rrggbb` swatches that post `<name>-preset` when clicked. |
| `alpha` | number | `percent: u8` |  |  | An opacity slider (`<name>-alpha`) at `percent`, clamped to 100. |
| `disabled` | switch |  | `off` | `disabled` | `disabled` and `aria-disabled`: shown greyed and not posted. |
| `readonly` | switch |  | `off` |  | Shown and posted, not changeable: disabled controls and hidden inputs with the values. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<input type="color">` | 20 | 29 | 12.1 |
| `color-mix()` | 111 | 113 | 16.2 |

- Fallback: text field accepting #rrggbb
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes TextField

## Documentation

A colour picker whose value the server remembers, no script. It can offer a row of preset
swatches and an opacity slider.

**Platform features:** `<input type="color">` (Chrome 20, Firefox 29, Safari 12.1). The
swatch beside it is a plain `<span>` painted with the server's current value through the
custom properties `--lui-color-value` and `--lui-color-alpha`, mixed with `color-mix()`
(Chrome 111, Firefox 113, Safari 16.2) over a checkerboard so transparency shows. Presets
are `<button name="<name>-preset" value="#rrggbb">`: one click posts the form with that
colour. Opacity is an `<input type="range">` named `<name>-alpha` (0 to 100).

**Accessibility:** a native colour input with its label; presets are named buttons in a
labelled group with `aria-pressed`. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo
route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** a live preview of the chosen colour before the form
is sent, and an eyedropper.

**Fallback:** none needed; a browser without a colour picker shows a text field that
accepts `#rrggbb`.

**Enhanced:** the enhancement script repaints the swatch and the code while the picker moves
and mirrors the opacity into its `<output>`.

```rust
use loco_ui::{prelude::*, color::hex_alpha};
// The value is the query's `accent`, or `.value(..)` (a saved colour).
let ui = Ui::from_request("/", "accent=%232f5bea", "");
assert!(ui.color("accent", "Accent").render().into_string().contains(r##"value="#2f5bea""##));
let m = ui.color("accent", "Accent").value("#2f5bea").presets(&["#1f6f5f", "#b3261e"]).alpha(80);
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains("name=\"accent-preset\" value=\"#b3261e\""));
assert!(html.contains("name=\"accent-alpha\"") && html.contains(r#"<label for="f-accent">"#));
assert_eq!(hex_alpha("#2f5bea", 80), "#2f5beacc");

// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! {
    Color("accent", "Accent") value="#2f5bea" presets=(&["#1f6f5f", "#b3261e"]) alpha=80;
};
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m.render().into_string());
```

# Streaming

`loco_ui::stream`

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<template shadowrootmode="open">` | 111 | 123 | 16.4 |
| `<slot name` | 53 | 63 | 10 |
| `Chunked transfer` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: in-order streaming with in-place splicing
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: Radix Themes Skeleton

## Documentation

Out-of-order streaming: the page is sent at once with placeholders, and each slow section
is appended to the response whenever it finishes, in any order. The browser moves each
chunk into its placeholder. No script.

**Platform features:**
- Declarative shadow DOM, `<template shadowrootmode="open">` (Chrome 111, Firefox 123,
  Safari 16.4). `<body>` becomes a shadow host whose shadow tree is the page, with a
  `<slot name="id">placeholder</slot>` per section.
- Named slots: a light-DOM child `<div slot="id">` of `<body>` replaces the placeholder the
  moment the parser sees it, wherever it arrives in the byte stream.
- Chunked transfer: the response body is a stream of HTML chunks. `Streamed::into_stream`
  is that stream for any server (`http` feature); the `axum` feature turns it into a
  response with `IntoResponse`.

**Accessibility:** the page is complete HTML in document order however the slots arrive;
placeholders are ordinary text until filled. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on
every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical
violation).

**What it does not do without script:** fill slots out of order where declarative shadow DOM
streaming is missing; the fallback keeps document order.

**Fallback:** without `Caps::StreamingDsd`, `ui.slot` leaves an HTML comment marker and the
response is streamed *in document order*: the bytes up to the first marker go out at once,
then each section as soon as it and everything before it are ready. Every browser renders
that progressively; only the out-of-order part is lost.

**Finding:** shadow trees do not see document stylesheets, so the stylesheet is inlined
twice in DSD mode, once in `<head>` for the slotted chunks and once in the shadow tree.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
let page = ui.stream("Feed", html! {
    h1 { "Feed" }
    (ui.slot("news", html! { p { "Loading news…" } }))
})
.fill("news", async { html! { p { "Fresh news." } } });
assert!(page.out_of_order());

// The same slot in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Slot("news", (html! { p { "Loading news…" } })); };
let slot = ui.slot("news", html! { p { "Loading news…" } });
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), slot.into_string());
```

# Upload

`loco_ui::upload` · demo: `/upload`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Upload` | `ui.upload(action: &str, name: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Upload`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `accept` | value | `types: &'a str` |  | `accept` | `accept`. |
| `multiple` | switch |  | `off` | `multiple` | Several files at once. |
| `help` | value | `text: &'a str` |  |  | Small print in the drop zone. |
| `file` | item | `name: &'a str, size: u64` |  |  | A file the server already holds, `size` in bytes. |
| `preview` | modifier | `src: &'a str` |  |  | A thumbnail for the file added last (an image URL). |
| `href` | modifier | `href: &'a str` |  | `href` | A link to the file added last, on its name. |
| `remove` | value | `action: &'a str` |  |  | A Remove button per file, posting `<name>=<file name>` to `action`. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<input type="file" accept multiple>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `<progress>` | 6 | 6 | 6 |
| `loading="lazy"` | 77 | 75 | 15.4 |

- Fallback: none needed: a plain multipart post; the progress bar needs the enhancement script
- Needs script: partly: upload progress and a preview before sending need script
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: Origin UI file upload

## Documentation

A file upload: a drop zone around a file input, an Upload button, and under it the files the
server already holds, with a thumbnail for images and a Remove button each. The list is what
the server says after the round trip, so it is always true.

The look follows the Origin UI file upload: a dashed drop zone with its icon in a round
tile, tinted on hover and while it has focus, roomier in a wide container; each kept file
a row of thumbnail, name (cut with an ellipsis, whole in its `title`) over its size, and
a remove button.

**Platform features:** `<input type="file" accept multiple>` (baseline 2015) in a
`<form method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">`; a file dropped on the input is picked
like a chosen one, with no script; `<progress>` (baseline 2013) for the upload bar;
`loading="lazy"` thumbnails; Post/Redirect/Get after the upload and after each removal.

**Accessibility:** a native file input inside its label (Enter or Space opens the picker), a
labelled upload button, and remove buttons named with the file. Checked by axe-core in
headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious
or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** show the upload's progress (the enhancement script
sends the form through `XMLHttpRequest` and fills the `<progress data-lui-progress>` bar;
without it the browser shows its own loading indicator), preview a file before it is sent,
or accept a drop anywhere but on the input.

**Fallback:** none needed: the form is a plain multipart post.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.upload("/files", "file").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"enctype="multipart/form-data""#) && m.contains(r#"type="file""#));
// Images only, several at once, and what the server already has.
let m = ui.upload("/files", "file")
    .accept("image/*").multiple().help("PNG or JPEG, up to 200 KB.")
    .file("cat.png", 48_213).preview("/files/cat.png")
    .file("notes.txt", 1_024).href("/files/notes.txt")
    .remove("/files/remove");
let m = m.render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"accept="image/*" multiple"#) && m.contains(r#"src="/files/cat.png""#));
assert!(m.contains("47.1 KB") && m.contains(r#"name="file" value="notes.txt""#));

// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Upload("/files", "file")
    accept="image/*" multiple help="PNG or JPEG, up to 200 KB." {
    file "cat.png" 48_213 preview="/files/cat.png";
    file "notes.txt" 1_024 href="/files/notes.txt";
    remove "/files/remove";
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
```

# Kanban

`loco_ui::kanban` · demo: `/kanban`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Kanban` | `ui.kanban(action: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Kanban`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `column` | item | `key: &'a str, title: &'a str` |  |  | A column. |
| `limit` | modifier | `limit: usize` |  |  | A work-in-progress limit for the column added last. |
| `card` | modifier | `key: &'a str, title: &'a str` |  |  | A card in the column added last. |
| `description` | modifier | `text: &'a str` |  |  | Small print under the card added last. |
| `badge` | modifier | `text: impl Display` |  |  | A badge in the meta row of the card added last: a label, an estimate, a tag. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<form method="post">` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `scroll-snap-type` | 69 | 68 | 11 |
| `view-transition-name` | 111 | 144 | 18 |
| `@container` | 105 | 110 | 16 |

- Fallback: without view transitions a moved card is simply in its new column; without container queries the board keeps its narrow, snapping form
- Needs script: partly: drag and drop and reordering within a column need script
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: Dice UI Kanban

## Documentation

A board of columns and cards. Moving a card is a form post: each card carries arrow buttons
to the column on its left and on its right, posting `card=<key>&to=<column>`; the route
saves the move and redirects back. A column can have a work-in-progress limit.

**Platform features:** `<form method="post">` with `name`/`value` buttons, Post/Redirect/Get;
each column is a `<section>` with a heading and an ordered list; the board scrolls sideways
(`overflow-x: auto`, `scroll-snap-type`, Chrome 69, Firefox 68, Safari 11) with each column
at 85% of the board's width when the board is narrow, so the next one peeks; `@container`
(Chrome 105, Firefox 110, Safari 16) puts the columns side by side from 48rem; `view-transition-name` per card (Chrome 111, Firefox 144, Safari 18) so, with the
enhancement script, a moved card slides to its new column.

**Accessibility:** each column is a `<section>` labelled by its heading; every card moves
with named buttons ("Move … to …") instead of drag and drop. Checked by axe-core in headless
Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or
critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** drag and drop, or reorder cards within a column
(the server decides the order: a moved card goes last in its new column).

**Fallback:** without view transitions a card is simply in its new column after the move;
without container queries the board keeps its narrow form (snapping columns that scroll).

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
let board = ui.kanban("/board/move")
    .column("todo", "To do").card("c1", "Write the docs")
    .column("doing", "Doing").limit(2).card("c2", "Calendar").description("M23").badge("Beta")
    .card("c3", "Upload")
    .column("done", "Done");
let m = board.render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"name="card" value="c1""#) && m.contains(r#"name="to" value="doing""#));
assert!(m.contains("2/2") && m.contains(">Beta</span>") && !m.contains(r#"value="todo" aria-label="Move Write"#));

// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Kanban("/board/move") {
    column "todo" "To do" { card "c1" "Write the docs"; }
    column "doing" "Doing" limit=2 {
        card "c2" "Calendar" description="M23" badge="Beta";
        card "c3" "Upload";
    }
    column "done" "Done";
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
```

# Sortable list

`loco_ui::sortable` · demo: `/sortable`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Sortable` | `ui.sortable(label: &str, action: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Sortable`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `item` | item | `key: &'a str, title: &'a str` |  |  | An item, after the ones added before it. |
| `description` | modifier | `text: &'a str` |  |  | Small print under the item added last. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<form method="post">` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `view-transition-name` | 111 | 144 | 18 |
| `@media (scripting: enabled)` | 120 | 113 | 17 |

- Fallback: without view transitions a moved item is simply in its new place
- Needs script: partly: dragging needs the script; the named buttons move items one place at a time without it
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Dioxus Components drag and drop list

## Documentation

A vertical list whose order the server keeps. Each item has a grip and two named buttons,
"Move … up" and "Move … down", in a form posting `item=<key>&to=<index>` (the index the
item should end at); the route saves the order and redirects back. With the enhancement
script the grip also drags: dropping posts the same form with the new index, and the list
is replaced in place.

**Platform features:** `<form method="post">` with `name`/`value` buttons, Post/Redirect/Get;
an ordered list labelled by `aria-label`; `view-transition-name` per item (Chrome 111,
Firefox 144, Safari 18) so a moved item slides; `@media (scripting: enabled)` (Chrome 120,
Firefox 113, Safari 17) for the grab cursor; with the script, HTML drag and drop (baseline
2010 on desktop, Safari 15 on iOS).

**Accessibility:** the move buttons are the keyboard and screen-reader path, named with the
item's title; the grip is decorative (`aria-hidden`). The first item has no "up" and the
last no "down"; an empty slot keeps the buttons of every row in line. On a touch screen
the buttons are 44px (`--lui-control-h-sm`).

**What it does not do without script:** dragging. Every move is a button press, one place
at a time.

**Fallback:** without view transitions a moved item is simply in its new place.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
let list = ui.sortable("Tasks", "/tasks/order")
    .item("a", "Write the docs").description("Due Friday")
    .item("b", "Ship the release");
let m = list.render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"name="item" value="a""#) && m.contains(r#"name="to" value="1""#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"aria-label="Move Write the docs down""#));
assert!(!m.contains("Move Write the docs up") && !m.contains("Move Ship the release down"));

// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Sortable("Tasks", "/tasks/order") {
    item "a" "Write the docs" description="Due Friday";
    item "b" "Ship the release";
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
```

# Alert

`loco_ui::alert` · demo: `/feedback`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Alert` | `ui.alert(title: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Alert`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | value | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A line of text under the title. |
| `body` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | Markup under the title (a list, a link), after the description. |
| `icon` | value | `icon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | Another icon than the tone's own. |
| `danger` | switch |  | `off` |  | Something went wrong. |
| `warn` | switch |  | `off` |  | Something to watch. |
| `ok` | switch |  | `off` |  | Something worked. |
| `info` | switch |  | `off` |  | Something to know: the brand scale, the default. |
| `surface` | switch |  | `off` |  | A paler tint inside a border in the level's colour. |
| `outline` | switch |  | `off` |  | No tint: a border in the level's colour on the page. |
| `size` | choice: 1, 2, 3 | `size: impl Into<Size>` | `2` |  | Radix's sizes 1 to 3: the padding, gaps and text. |
| `tone` | choice: neutral, brand, ok, warn, danger, info | `tone: Tone` | `info` |  | The colour; danger also makes it `role="alert"`. |
| `variant` | choice: solid, soft, surface, outline, ghost | `variant: Variant` | `soft` |  | Soft, surface or outline; ghost drops the frame, and solid draws as soft. |
| `action` | value | `button: Button<'a>` |  |  | A button or link button under the text. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  |  | The id its dismiss cookie is named after instead of the title's slug. |
| `dismiss` | switch |  | `off` |  | A close button that keeps it closed with a `lui-dismiss-<id>` cookie. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `role="alert"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `role="status"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Callout

## Documentation

A callout in the page, after Radix Themes Callout: a title, a line or two of explanation
and an icon, in an info, danger, warning or success tone (or any
`Tone` with `.tone(..)`), soft by default or `.surface()`,
`.outline()` (`.variant(..)`), at Radix's sizes 1 to 3. For a message that stays where it
is, unlike a flash or a toast. `.action(..)` adds a button under the text, and
`.dismiss()` a close button that keeps it closed, as a `crate::banner::Banner` does.

**Platform features:** a `role="alert"` box for the danger tone (read out when the page
loads) and `role="status"` for the others; the icon is decorative. The close button is a
`<form method="post">` to `crate::banner::DISMISS_PATH`, which sets a `lui-dismiss-<id>`
cookie and redirects back; the next page renders nothing for it.

**Accessibility:** `role="alert"` for the danger tone, `role="status"` for the others; the
icon is decorative. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both
capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** close in place: closing is a round trip.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.alert("Heads up").description("You can add components to your app.").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"role="status""#) && m.contains("Heads up"));
let m = ui.alert("Payment failed").danger().description("Your card was declined.").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"class="lui-alert lui-callout lui-callout-danger" data-tone="danger" role="alert""#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Alert("Payment failed") danger description="Your card was declined."; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// Surface and outline variants.
let m = ui.alert("Heads up").surface().render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("lui-callout-info lui-callout-surface"));
assert_eq!(lui! { Alert("Heads up") surface; }.into_string(), m);
// The typed setters: a quiet gray note, smaller.
let m = ui.alert("Draft").tone(Tone::Neutral).variant(Variant::Outline).size(1).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"class="lui-alert lui-callout lui-callout-neutral lui-callout-outline" data-size="1" data-tone="neutral" data-variant="outline""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Alert("Draft") tone="neutral" variant="outline" size=1; }.into_string(), m);
// A button under the text, and a close button that keeps it closed.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/billing", "", "");
let m = ui.alert("Trial ends Friday").info().action(ui.link_button("Upgrade", "/plans").small()).dismiss().render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<div class="lui-alert-actions"><a class="lui-button"#) && m.contains(r#"name="id" value="trial-ends-friday""#));
let same = lui! { Alert("Trial ends Friday") info action=(ui.link_button("Upgrade", "/plans").small()) dismiss; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
let gone = Ui::from_request("/billing", "", "lui-dismiss-trial-ends-friday=1");
assert_eq!(gone.alert("Trial ends Friday").dismiss().render().into_string(), "");
```

# Progress

`loco_ui::progress` · demo: `/feedback`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Progress` | `ui.progress(value: u64, max: u64)` | stable |

## Props of `Progress`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | value | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A label above the bar. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The bar's id instead of `lui-progress-<label>`. |
| `size` | choice: 1, 2, 3 | `size: impl Into<Size>` | `2` |  | The bar's height: 0.25, 0.5 or 0.75rem. |
| `tone` | choice: neutral, brand, ok, warn, danger, info | `tone: Tone` | `brand` |  | The fill's colour. |
| `variant` | choice: solid, soft, surface, outline, ghost | `variant: Variant` | `surface` |  | Soft tints the track with the tone; the others keep the gray track. |
| `radius` | choice: none, small, medium, large, full | `radius: Radius` | `full` |  | The ends of the track and the fill, from square to round. |
| `indeterminate` | switch |  | `off` |  | No value yet: a stripe slides along the track. |
| `show_value` | switch |  | `off` |  | The percentage beside the label, or above the bar without one. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<progress>` | 6 | 6 | 6 |
| `appearance: none` | 84 | 80 | 15.4 |

- Fallback: without the pseudo-elements a browser draws its own bar
- Needs script: partly: moving on its own needs a streamed page or the script
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Tremor ProgressBar

## Documentation

How far along a task is: a bar filled to a value out of a maximum, or an indeterminate
bar (`.indeterminate()`) when the server does not know yet; `.show_value()` writes the
percentage beside it. Radix Themes Progress's props: three heights
(`.size(..)`), a `Tone` for the fill, a soft or surface track
(`.variant(..)`) and `.radius(..)`.

**Platform features:** `<progress>` (baseline 2013) with its label tied by `<label for>`,
so a screen reader says the value; `appearance: none` and the `::-webkit-progress-*` and
`::-moz-progress-bar` pseudo-elements draw it in the shadcn shape. An indeterminate bar is
a `<progress>` with no value, matched by `:indeterminate` (baseline 2020) and drawn as a
sliding stripe that `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` stops.

**Accessibility:** a native `<progress>` with its label. Checked by axe-core in headless
Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or
critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** move on its own; the value is what the server knew
when it rendered the page (a streamed page or the enhancement script can send a newer one).

**Fallback:** without the pseudo-elements a browser draws its own bar.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.progress(33, 100).label("Upload").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<progress id="lui-progress-upload" class="lui-progress" value="33" max="100">33%</progress>"#));
assert!(!m.contains("lui-progress-value"), "the percentage only with .show_value()");
let m = ui.progress(33, 100).label("Upload").show_value().render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<span class="lui-progress-value">33%</span>"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Progress(33, 100) label="Upload" show_value; }.into_string(), m);
let m = ui.progress(0, 100).label("Waiting").indeterminate().render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"class="lui-progress">"#) && !m.contains("value="));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Progress(0, 100) label="Waiting" indeterminate; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// A thin green bar on a tinted track, square ends.
let m = ui.progress(9, 10).size(1).tone(Tone::Ok).variant(Variant::Soft).radius(Radius::None).render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<div class="lui-progress-field" data-size="1" data-tone="ok" data-variant="soft" data-radius="none">"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Progress(9, 10) size=1 tone="ok" variant="soft" radius="none"; }.into_string(), m);
```

# Meter

`loco_ui::meter` · demo: `/feedback`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Meter` | `ui.meter(value: impl Into<f64>, min: impl Into<f64>, max: impl Into<f64>)` | stable |

## Props of `Meter`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | value | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A label above the meter, with the value beside it. |
| `low` | number | `low: impl Into<f64>` |  | `low` | Below this is "low". |
| `high` | number | `high: impl Into<f64>` |  | `high` | Above this is "high". |
| `optimum` | number | `optimum: impl Into<f64>` |  | `optimum` | The best value. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The meter's id instead of `lui-meter-<label>`. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<meter>` | 6 | 16 | 6 |

- Fallback: without the pseudo-elements a browser draws its own meter
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Tremor CategoryBar colours

## Documentation

A measurement within a known range, like disk space or a password's strength: unlike a
progress bar it is not a task moving forward, and it turns warn or danger past thresholds.

**Platform features:** `<meter>` (Chrome 6, Firefox 16, Safari 6) with `low`, `high` and
`optimum`, so the browser picks the good, average or bad colour itself; the
`::-webkit-meter-*` and `::-moz-meter-bar` pseudo-elements map those to `--lui-ok`,
`--lui-warn` and `--lui-danger`.

**Accessibility:** a native `<meter>` with its label. Checked by axe-core in headless
Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or
critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** update live.

**Fallback:** without the pseudo-elements a browser draws its own meter, in its own colours.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.meter(82, 0, 100).label("Disk").low(60).high(80).optimum(0).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"value="82" min="0" max="100" low="60" high="80" optimum="0""#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Meter(82, 0, 100) label="Disk" low=60 high=80 optimum=0; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
```

# Tooltip

`loco_ui::tooltip` · demo: `/feedback`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Tooltip` | `ui.tooltip(text: &str, trigger: Markup)` | stable |

## Props of `Tooltip`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `below` | switch |  | `off` |  | Show the text under the trigger instead of above it: `.side(Side::Bottom)`. |
| `side` | choice: top, bottom, start, end | `side: Side` | `top` |  | The side of the trigger the text shows on. |
| `delay` | number | `ms: u32` | `0` |  | How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the text shows, in milliseconds. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The tooltip's id, `lui-tooltip-<slug of the text>` by default. |
| `trigger` | value | `button: Button<'a>` |  |  | A button builder as the trigger, in place of the markup: it gets `aria-describedby` as an attribute. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:focus-within` | 60 | 52 | 10.1 |
| `@media (hover: none)` | 41 | 64 | 9 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: partly: a delay before opening and Escape to close need script
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Tooltip

## Documentation

A short label that appears beside a control while the pointer is over it or it has focus:
what an icon button does, what a shortcut is.

**Platform features:** CSS only: the text is a `role="tooltip"` element shown by
`:hover` and `:focus-within` (baseline 2020) on the wrapper, and the trigger inside names
it with `aria-describedby` so a screen reader says it too. `@media (hover: none)` (Chrome
41, Firefox 64, Safari 9) keeps it off touch screens, where hover does not exist.

**Accessibility:** `role="tooltip"` joined to its trigger by `aria-describedby`; shown on
hover and on keyboard focus. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route,
both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

`.side(..)` puts it on any side of the trigger (the same `Side` as the popover's) and
`.delay(ms)` waits before showing it on hover: a `transition-delay` on the way in, none
on the way out.

**What it does not do without script:** close on Escape while the pointer stays over it,
or flip to fit the viewport. `popover="hint"` with hover triggers
would do some of this, but it is Chromium-only and needs script to open on hover.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.tooltip("Copy the link", html! { (ui.button("").icon_only().ghost().aria_label("Copy").body(html! { (Icon::Copy) })) });
let m = m.render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"role="tooltip""#) && m.contains("Copy the link"));
assert!(m.contains(r#"aria-describedby="lui-tooltip-copy-the-link""#));
let below = ui.tooltip("Saved", html! { span { "3" } }).below().render().into_string();
assert!(below.contains(r#"data-side="bottom""#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Tooltip("Copy the link", lui! {
    Button("") icon_only ghost aria_label="Copy" body=(html! { (Icon::Copy) });
}); };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// A button builder as the trigger.
let copy = ui.button("").icon_only().ghost().aria_label("Copy").leading(Icon::Copy);
let m = ui.tooltip("Copy the link", html! {}).trigger(copy).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"aria-label="Copy" aria-describedby="lui-tooltip-copy-the-link""#));
// At the end of the trigger, after half a second.
let m = ui.tooltip("Saved", html! { span { "3" } }).side(Side::End).delay(500).render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<span class="lui-tooltip" data-side="end" style="--lui-tooltip-delay: 500ms">"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Tooltip("Saved", html! { span { "3" } }) side=(Side::End) delay=500; }.into_string(), m);
```

|---|---|---|
| `Separator` | `ui.separator()` | stable |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `vertical` | switch |  | `off` |  | Down instead of across, between items in a row (a `ui.cluster`). |

|---|---|---|---|
| `<hr>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `aria-orientation` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Needs script: no

## Documentation

A hairline between groups of content, across or down, optionally with a word in the middle
("or" between two sign-in methods).

**Platform features:** `<hr>` for a plain horizontal rule (its semantics are a thematic
break); a labelled or vertical one is a `role="separator"` element with
`aria-orientation`.

**Accessibility:** a native `<hr>` or `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation`. Checked by

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
assert_eq!(ui.separator().render().into_string(), r#"<hr class="lui-separator">"#);

let same = lui! { Separator label="or"; };
```
