# Toast

`loco_ui::toast` · demo: `/toast`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Toasts` | `ui.toasts()` | stable |

## Props of `Toasts`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dismiss` | switch |  | `off` |  | A close link on each toast, back to this page. |
| `position` | choice: top-start, top-center, top-end, bottom-start, bottom-center, bottom-end | `position: Position` | `bottom-end` |  | Where the stack sits: a corner, or the middle of the top or bottom edge. |
| `duration` | number | `ms: u32` | `5000` |  | How long a calm toast stays before it fades, in milliseconds. |
| `action` | value | `label: &'a str, href: &'a str` |  |  | A link button on the newest toast ("Undo", "View"). |
| `max` | number | `n: usize` | `all` |  | Show only the newest `n` toasts. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `position: fixed` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `role="status"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `role="alert"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `@keyframes` | 43 | 16 | 9 |
| `prefers-reduced-motion` | 74 | 63 | 10.1 |
| `@starting-style` | 117 | 129 | 17.5 |

- Fallback: without CSS animations toasts stay until the next page
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: viewport
- Look after: shadcn Sonner

## Documentation

Short notices in a stack at the corner of the viewport, outside the page flow, that fade
on their own: "Copied", "Invite sent". The same one-shot cookie as `crate::Ui::flash` carries
them across a Post/Redirect/Get, with the same `level:` lines (`crate::flash::stack`).

The look follows shadcn Sonner: an icon by level, the message and a close ×, the toasts
stacked in depth (the newest in front, two behind it scaled and peeking) and fanned out
while the pointer is over the stack or a toast has focus, in CSS only; under reduced
motion they are shown fanned out, still.

`.position(..)` puts the stack in another corner or the middle of an edge, `.duration(..)`
sets how long a calm toast stays, `.max(..)` keeps the newest few, and `.action(..)` adds
a link button ("Undo") to the newest.

**Platform features:** `position: fixed` in the bottom-end corner (full width at the
bottom or top, 16px from the edges, on a narrow screen); overlapping grid items for the stack; `role="status"` per notice and `role="alert"` for danger; a CSS fade with
`@keyframes` that pauses on `:hover` and `:focus-within` and that
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` switches off. Danger toasts never fade. Each toast fades
in and rises on the `--lui-ease-spring` curve through `@starting-style` (Chrome 117,
Firefox 129, Safari 17.5); older browsers show it at once.

**Fallback:** without CSS animations the toasts stay until the next page; the dismiss link
(`.dismiss()`) clears them sooner. `/lui/enhance.js` carries the list across a
swap like the flash.

**Accessibility:** `role="status"` (errors `role="alert"`) in a live list; dismiss links are
named with the message. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both
capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** it cannot appear without a request (a toast is the
answer to a round trip), and dismissing one is a navigation, not an instant removal.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
// What `ui.redirect("/toast").ok("Invite sent.").danger("Mail server down.")` sends.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/toast", "", "lui-flash=ok%3AInvite%20sent.%0Adanger%3AMail%20server%20down.");
let m = ui.toasts().render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("lui-toast-ok") && m.contains(r#"role="alert""#));
assert!(ui.toasts().dismiss().render().into_string().contains(r#"href="/toast""#));
assert_eq!(Ui::default().toasts().render().into_string(), "");
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Toasts; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// At the top, the newest one only, with an undo link, for eight seconds.
let m = ui.toasts().position(Position::TopCenter).max(1).action("Undo", "/toast/undo").duration(8000).render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<ol class="lui-toasts" data-position="top-center" style="--lui-toast-duration: 8000ms">"#));
assert_eq!(m.matches("<li").count(), 1);
assert!(m.contains(r#"href="/toast/undo""#) && m.contains("Mail server down."));
let same = lui! { Toasts position=(Position::TopCenter) max=1 action=("Undo", "/toast/undo") duration=8000; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
```

# Breadcrumbs

`loco_ui::breadcrumbs` · demo: `/nav`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Breadcrumbs` | `ui.breadcrumbs()` | stable |

## Props of `Breadcrumbs`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `link` | item | `label: &'a str, href: &'a str` |  |  | One step from the root towards this page. |
| `here` | item | `label: &'a str` |  |  | The current page, last in the trail and not a link. |
| `max` | number | `n: usize` | `4` |  | The most crumbs shown, the current page included, before the middle folds into a menu. |
| `separator` | value | `glyph: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | A glyph or an icon between the crumbs instead of the chevron. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-current="page"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `::before` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `<details>` | 12 | 49 | 6 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: shadcn Breadcrumb

## Documentation

Where this page sits: a trail of links ending in the current page. A long trail folds its
middle into a disclosure so the ends stay readable on a phone.

**Platform features:** `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` around an ordered list, the last
item marked `aria-current="page"`; separators drawn by CSS `::before` so screen readers do
not read them; the folded middle is a `<details>` element.

**Accessibility:** a `<nav>` named "Breadcrumb" with an ordered list; the current page has
`aria-current="page"`; folded steps sit in a named `<details>`. Checked by axe-core in
headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious
or critical violation).

The look follows shadcn Breadcrumb: muted links, chevron separators, the current page in
the text colour. A trail of more than four (or `.max(n)`) folds its middle into a `…`
disclosure menu; a shorter one with a middle crumb folds it only when the breadcrumbs are
under 30rem wide (both are rendered; a container query shows one). `.separator(..)` puts
a glyph or an icon between the crumbs instead of the chevron, `aria-hidden`.

**What it does not do without script:** measure the text to fold exactly what does not fit;
the fold is decided by item count and the container's width.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
let m = ui.breadcrumbs().link("Home", "/").link("Projects", "/projects").here("loco-ui").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<a href="/projects">Projects</a>"#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"aria-current="page">loco-ui"#));
// More than four: the middle folds into <details>.
let long = ui.breadcrumbs().link("Home", "/").link("A", "/a").link("B", "/a/b").link("C", "/a/b/c").here("Here");
assert!(long.render().into_string().contains("<details"));
// One middle crumb: shown inline, and folded too for a narrow container.
let three = ui.breadcrumbs().link("Home", "/").link("A", "/a").link("B", "/a/b").here("Here").render().into_string();
assert!(three.contains("lui-breadcrumbs-mid") && three.contains("lui-breadcrumbs-fold-narrow"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Breadcrumbs {
    link "Home" "/"; link "Projects" "/projects"; here "loco-ui";
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// At most three crumbs before the middle folds, a slash between them.
let short = ui.breadcrumbs().max(3).separator("/").link("Home", "/").link("A", "/a").link("B", "/a/b").here("Here");
let short = short.render().into_string();
assert!(short.contains("<details") && short.contains(r#"<span class="lui-breadcrumbs-sep" aria-hidden="true">/</span>"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Breadcrumbs max=3 separator="/" { link "Home" "/"; link "A" "/a"; link "B" "/a/b"; here "Here"; } }.into_string(), short);
```

# Skeleton

`loco_ui::skeleton` · demo: `/feedback`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Skeleton` | `ui.skeleton(lines: usize)` | stable |

## Props of `Skeleton`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | value | `label: &'a str` | `Loading` |  | What screen readers hear instead of "Loading". |
| `heading` | switch |  | `off` |  | Start with a wider, taller bar standing in for a heading. |
| `circle` | switch |  | `off` |  | A 2.5rem circle beside the lines, standing in for an avatar. |
| `rect` | value | `width: &'a str, height: &'a str` |  |  | A block of that CSS width and height above the lines (an image, a chart). |
| `avatar_lines` | number | `n: usize` | `0` |  | `n` rows of a circle beside two lines, after the rest: a list of people. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-busy` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `role="status"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `@keyframes` | 43 | 16 | 9 |
| `prefers-reduced-motion` | 74 | 63 | 10.1 |

- Fallback: without CSS animations the bars are still
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Skeleton

## Documentation

Grey bars in the shape of content that is still coming: the placeholder for a streamed
`Ui::slot` (feature `http`), a lazy panel, anything the server fills in later. Besides
lines: `.circle()` puts an avatar's circle beside them, `.rect(w, h)` a block (an image,
a chart) above them, and `.avatar_lines(n)` makes `n` rows of a circle and two lines, a
list of people.

**Platform features:** `aria-busy="true"` and `role="status"` with a visually hidden
label, so assistive technology hears "Loading" once instead of reading empty boxes; a
shimmer drawn with `@keyframes` over a `linear-gradient` that
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` stops.

**Fallback:** without CSS animations the bars are still; nothing else differs.

**Accessibility:** `role="status"` with `aria-busy` and a "Loading" name; the bars are
`aria-hidden`. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability
variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** it cannot be removed by the client; it is replaced
when the real content arrives (a streamed slot, a swap, the next page).

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
assert_eq!(ui.skeleton(3).render().into_string().matches("lui-skeleton-line").count(), 3);
let m = ui.skeleton(2).label("Loading orders").heading().render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("Loading orders") && m.contains("lui-skeleton-heading"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Skeleton(2) label="Loading orders" heading; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// A card: an image block, then a circle beside two lines.
let m = ui.skeleton(2).rect("100%", "8rem").circle().render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<span class="lui-skeleton-rect" style="width:100%;height:8rem" aria-hidden="true"></span>"#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"<span class="lui-skeleton-circle" aria-hidden="true"></span>"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Skeleton(2) rect=("100%", "8rem") circle; }.into_string(), m);
// Three people in a list.
let m = ui.skeleton(0).avatar_lines(3).render().into_string();
assert_eq!(m.matches("lui-skeleton-circle").count(), 3);
assert_eq!(lui! { Skeleton(0) avatar_lines=3; }.into_string(), m);
```

# Empty state

`loco_ui::empty_state` · demo: `/dashboard`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `EmptyState` | `ui.empty_state(title: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `EmptyState`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | value | `icon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An icon, or a glyph or emoji, above the title, hidden from screen readers. |
| `body` | value | `text: Markup` |  |  | One or two sentences. |
| `link` | value | `label: &'a str, href: &'a str` |  |  | A link to follow. |
| `action` | value | `label: &'a str, action: &'a str` |  |  | A button posting to `action`. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<form method="post">` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: shadcn Empty

## Documentation

What a list, table or search shows when there is nothing in it: what is missing, why, and
the one thing to do next, as a real link or form button.

**Platform features:** plain HTML; the action is an `<a>` or, for something that changes
data, a `<form method="post">` button, so it works with nothing else.

**Accessibility:** a heading, a sentence and a real action; the illustration is
`aria-hidden`. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability
variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing; it is static content.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
assert!(ui.empty_state("No files yet").render().into_string().contains("No files yet"));
let m = ui.empty_state("No results for \u{201c}zzz\u{201d}")
    .icon("\u{1f50d}")
    .body(html! { "Check the spelling or clear the filter." })
    .link("Clear the filter", "/table")
    .action("Create a file", "/files/new");
let m = m.render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"href="/table""#) && m.contains(r#"action="/files/new""#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! {
    EmptyState("No results for \u{201c}zzz\u{201d}") icon="\u{1f50d}"
        body=(html! { "Check the spelling or clear the filter." }) {
        link "Clear the filter" "/table";
        action "Create a file" "/files/new";
    }
};
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
```

# Stat

`loco_ui::stat` · demo: `/dashboard`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Stat` | `ui.stat(label: &str, value: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Stat`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `delta` | value | `text: &'a str` |  |  | The change. |
| `trend` | value | `trend: Trend` |  |  | Override the direction read from the delta's sign. |
| `down_is_good` | switch |  | `off` |  | A fall is good news (error rates, latency). |
| `description` | value | `note: &'a str` |  |  | Small print under the value. |
| `href` | value | `href: &'a str` |  | `href` | Make the whole card a link to the details. |
| `reveal` | switch |  | `off` |  | Fades and rises as it scrolls into view. |
| `sample` | item | `value: f64` |  |  | A recent value for the sparkline along the card's bottom edge (oldest first). |
| `progress` | value | `value: u64, max: u64` |  |  | A bar under the value: how far towards a target. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repeat(auto-fit` | 57 | 52 | 10.1 |
| `animation-timeline: view()` | 115 | no | 26 |

- Fallback: none needed; a reveal tile is shown in place without animation-timeline
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Tremor KPI cards

## Documentation

One number that matters, with its label and how it moved: the tiles at the top of a
dashboard. Several sit in a `div.lui-stat-grid`, which wraps them to the width available.

**Platform features:** a card of `<p>` elements that reads in order; the change
carries its direction in words for screen readers (`<span class="lui-sr">`) as well as an
arrow and a colour; the grid is `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(12rem, 1fr))`, so no media query.
`.reveal()` fades and rises the tile as it scrolls into view, as a card's does: a
scroll-driven animation with `animation-timeline: view()` (Chrome 115, Firefox no,
Safari 26), off under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.

**Accessibility:** a label and a value in text; trend arrows are `aria-hidden` and the
change is in words. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both
capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** update live; the number is as fresh as the page.

**Fallback:** none needed. A `.reveal()` tile where `animation-timeline: view()` is missing,
or under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, is shown in place from the start.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
assert!(ui.stat("Visitors", "12,480").render().into_string().contains("12,480"));
// The sign of the delta says the direction: `+` up, `-` down, zero flat.
let m = ui.stat("Error rate", "0.4%")
    .delta("-0.2 pt")
    .down_is_good()
    .description("last 7 days")
    .href("/errors");
let m = m.render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("lui-stat-good") && m.contains("down") && m.contains(r#"href="/errors""#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! {
    Stat("Error rate", "0.4%") delta="-0.2 pt" down_is_good description="last 7 days" href="/errors";
};
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// Opt-in motion: it fades in as it scrolls into view.
let up = ui.stat("Visitors", "12,480").reveal().render().into_string();
assert!(up.starts_with(r#"<div class="lui-stat lui-stat-reveal">"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Stat("Visitors", "12,480") reveal; }.into_string(), up);
// A sparkline along the bottom and a progress bar towards a target.
let kpi = ui.stat("Revenue", "$48,210").sample(30.0).sample(34.0).sample(31.0).sample(38.0).progress(62, 100).render().into_string();
assert!(kpi.contains(r#"<progress class="lui-stat-progress" value="62" max="100""#) && kpi.contains("lui-stat-spark"));
assert_eq!(lui! { Stat("Revenue", "$48,210") sample=30.0 sample=34.0 sample=31.0 sample=38.0 progress=(62, 100); }.into_string(), kpi);
```

# Chart

`loco_ui::chart` · demo: `/chart`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Chart` | `ui.chart(title: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Chart`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `point` | item | `label: &'a str, value: f64` |  |  | One value, labelled on the x axis. |
| `points` | value | `points: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'a str, f64)>` |  |  | Many values at once, from a slice or a query: `(label, value)` pairs. |
| `description` | value | `text: &'a str` |  |  | What the chart shows, in a sentence: its `<desc>`. |
| `unit` | value | `unit: &'a str` |  |  | Written after every value, as `" ms"` or `"%"`. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The id its parts are named from; `chart-<title>` by default. |
| `bar` | switch |  | `off` |  | Bars, one per point (the default). |
| `line` | switch |  | `off` |  | A line through the points. |
| `sparkline` | switch |  | `off` |  | A small line with no axes, to sit beside a number. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<svg>` | 7 | 4 | 5.1 |
| `role="img"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `<title>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `CSS custom properties in SVG` | 49 | 31 | 9.1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: partly: zoom, pan and a crosshair that follows the pointer need script
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: Tremor AreaChart, BarChart, LineChart

## Documentation

A bar chart, a line chart or a sparkline drawn on the server as inline SVG: one series of
labelled values, a y axis rounded to readable steps, and the numbers themselves in a
visually hidden table for anyone who cannot see the picture. No chart library and no
script, where most kits need both.

**Platform features:**
- Inline `<svg>` in HTML (Chrome 7, Firefox 4, Safari 5.1), a `role="group"` named by its
  `<title>` and `<desc>` through `aria-labelledby` (a sparkline is one `role="img"`).
- Each bar and point is a focusable `<g tabindex="0" role="img">` named by its label and
  value, whose value chip CSS shows on `:hover` and `:focus-visible`.
- A container query (Chrome 105, Firefox 110, Safari 16) drops every other x label and
  draws the text larger in a chart under 30rem wide.
- CSS custom properties in SVG `fill` and `stroke` (Chrome 49, Firefox 31, Safari 9.1): the
  colours are `--lui-*` tokens, so a chart follows the theme and dark mode.

The look follows Tremor's charts: dashed gray gridlines, a legend swatch over the chart,
the series in the primary colour, a dark value chip on each mark.

**Accessibility:** the SVG is a group named by the chart's title and description, each
mark an image named "label: value" that takes the focus; the data is also a table (row headers are the labels) hidden visually but read by screen
readers; a sparkline, which sits in a sentence, lists its values as hidden text instead. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability
variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** zoom, pan, or a crosshair that follows the pointer;
the value shows on the mark under the pointer or the focus.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.chart("Signups").point("Mon", 12.0).point("Tue", 18.0).point("Wed", 9.0);
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"role="group""#) && html.contains(r#"aria-label="Tue: 18""#) && html.contains("<title id=\"chart-signups-title\">Signups</title>"));
assert!(html.contains(r#"<th scope="row">Tue</th><td>18</td>"#));
// Values from data in one call:
const SIGNUPS: [(&str, f64); 3] = [("Mon", 12.0), ("Tue", 18.0), ("Wed", 9.0)];
assert_eq!(ui.chart("Signups").points(SIGNUPS).render().into_string(), html);

let m = ui.chart("Latency").line().unit(" ms").description("p50 per day, last week")
    .point("Mon", 41.5).point("Tue", 38.0);
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains("lui-chart-line") && html.contains("<td>41.5 ms</td>"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Chart("Latency") line unit=" ms" description="p50 per day, last week" {
    point "Mon" 41.5; point "Tue" 38.0;
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Sidebar

`loco_ui::sidebar` · demo: `/sidebar`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Sidebar` | `ui.sidebar(label: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Sidebar`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | item | `heading: &'a str` |  |  | Start a group of links under a small heading. |
| `link` | item | `text: &'a str, href: &'a str` |  | `href` | A link; the one to the current path is marked current. |
| `icon` | modifier | `icon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An icon before the link added last. |
| `badge` | modifier | `text: impl Display` |  |  | A count after the link added last. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The prefix of the group headings' ids instead of `lui-sidebar-<label>`. |
| `collapsible` | switch |  | `off` |  | A toggle that folds it to an icon rail, the labels shown as tooltips. |
| `current_prefix` | switch |  | `off` |  | Mark a link current also when the path is under it (`/projects` on `/projects/42`). |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-current="page"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: partly: collapsing to an icon rail kept between pages needs script
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: shadcn Sidebar

## Documentation

An app's navigation as a column: groups under small headings, each link with an optional
icon and a count, the link to the current path highlighted. Put it in a
`Drawer` `.sidebar()` (or `ui.app_shell`) to have it collapse to a drawer
on narrow screens, or anywhere a column fits.

**Platform features:** a `<nav>` of lists; `aria-current="page"` on the link to the current
path, compared on the server.

**Accessibility:** a `<nav>` named by its label; each group is a list labelled by its
heading; the current page's link has `aria-current="page"`; icons are decorative, counts are
text. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants,
light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

The look follows the shadcn Sidebar block: muted group labels, 2rem rows with icons and
counts, the current row on gray-4. `.collapsible()` adds a toggle that folds it to an icon
rail whose labels show as tooltips.

**What it does not do without script:** keep the rail folded between pages (each page
renders it open); wrap it in a drawer for the narrow-screen case.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from_request("/inbox", "", "");
let m = ui.sidebar("Mail").link("Inbox", "/inbox").link("Sent", "/sent").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<a href="/inbox" aria-current="page">"#));

let m = ui.sidebar("Mail")
    .group("Mail")
    .link("Inbox", "/inbox").icon(Icon::Mail).badge("12")
    .link("Sent", "/sent")
    .group("Labels")
    .link("Work", "/labels/work");
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains("lui-sidebar-badge\">12<") && html.contains(">Labels</p>"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Sidebar("Mail") {
    group "Mail";
    link "Inbox" "/inbox" icon=(Icon::Mail) badge="12";
    link "Sent" "/sent";
    group "Labels";
    link "Work" "/labels/work";
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
// A toggle that folds it to an icon rail (where `::details-content` can be styled).
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
let rail = ui.sidebar("Mail").collapsible().link("Inbox", "/inbox").icon(Icon::Mail).render().into_string();
assert!(rail.starts_with(r#"<details class="lui-sidebar-rail" open>"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Sidebar("Mail") collapsible { link "Inbox" "/inbox" icon=(Icon::Mail); } }.into_string(), rail);
// `/projects/42` is under the link to `/projects`, which is marked current.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/projects/42", "", "");
let m = ui.sidebar("App").current_prefix().link("Home", "/").link("Projects", "/projects").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<a href="/projects" aria-current="page">"#) && !m.contains(r#"<a href="/" aria-current"#));
```

# Navigation menu

`loco_ui::nav_menu` · demo: `/nav-menu`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `NavMenu` | `ui.nav_menu(label: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `NavMenu`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `link` | item | `text: &'a str, href: &'a str` |  | `href` | A link in the row; the one to the current path is marked current. |
| `panel` | item | `text: &'a str, items: impl IntoIterator<Item = I>` |  |  | A button that opens a panel of `items` (`MenuItem`s or `(text, href)` links). |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The prefix of the panels' ids instead of `nav-<label>`. |
| `current_prefix` | switch |  | `off` |  | Mark a link current also when the path is under it (`/projects` on `/projects/42`). |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `popover` | 114 | 125 | 17 |
| `aria-current="page"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: a <details> dropdown without popover; a centred panel without anchor positioning
- Needs script: partly: opening a panel on hover needs script
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: shadcn Navigation Menu

## Documentation

A site's top navigation: a row of links, some of which open a panel of more links. Panels
are the popover menu's: they open on click, close on a click outside or
Escape, and are `<details>` dropdowns where popovers are missing.

**Platform features:** a `<nav>` of lists; the panels use `popover` and anchor positioning
as the popover menu does (see its header); `aria-current="page"` on the link to the current
path.

**Accessibility:** a `<nav>` named by its label; plain links are links, and a panel's button
says it opens a menu (`aria-haspopup`); the current page's link has `aria-current="page"`.
Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light
and dark (no serious or critical violation).

The look follows shadcn NavigationMenu: quiet triggers, and panels that are a grid of links,
each a title over a line of description (`(text, href, description)` items), two across
in a wide panel and one in a narrow one.

**What it does not do without script:** open a panel on hover; a click opens it.

**Fallback:** that of the popover menu: a `<details>` dropdown without `popover`, a centred
panel without anchor positioning.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let mut ui = Ui::from_request("/pricing", "", "");
ui.caps = Caps::all();
let m = ui.nav_menu("Main").link("Pricing", "/pricing").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<a class="lui-nav-menu-link" href="/pricing" aria-current="page">"#));

let m = ui.nav_menu("Main")
    .panel("Products", [("Mail", "/mail"), ("Calendar", "/calendar")])
    .link("Pricing", "/pricing");
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"popovertarget="nav-main-products""#) && html.contains(r#"href="/calendar""#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { NavMenu("Main") {
    panel "Products" ([("Mail", "/mail"), ("Calendar", "/calendar")]);
    link "Pricing" "/pricing";
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
// Panel links with a line of description each.
let m = ui.nav_menu("Main").panel("Products", [("Mail", "/mail", "Read and send")]).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<span class="lui-popover-description">Read and send</span>"#));
// `/blog/2026/hello` is under the link to `/blog`, which is marked current.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/blog/2026/hello", "", "");
let m = ui.nav_menu("Main").current_prefix().link("Blog", "/blog").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"href="/blog" aria-current="page""#));
```

# Description list

`loco_ui::description_list` · demo: `/description-list`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `DescriptionList` | `ui.description_list()` | beta |

## Props of `DescriptionList`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `item` | item | `term: &'a str, detail: impl Render` |  |  | A term and its detail (text, or markup such as a badge). |
| `stacked` | switch |  | `off` |  | Each term above its detail instead of beside it. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<dl>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `@container` | 105 | 110 | 16 |
| `subgrid` | 117 | 71 | 16 |

- Fallback: without container queries the terms stay above their details; without subgrid the term column is a fixed 10rem
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: Radix Themes DataList

## Documentation

Terms and what they are: a record's fields, a summary before confirming, key facts. Terms
sit in a column beside their details, or above them with `.stacked()`.

**Platform features:** `<dl>` with `<dt>`/`<dd>` pairs, each pair in a `<div>` (allowed in a
`<dl>`, every browser); container queries (`@container`: Chrome 105, Firefox 110, Safari 16) put the
terms beside their details once the list is 30rem wide; subgrid (Chrome 117, Firefox 71,
Safari 16) gives every row one shared term column, as wide as the longest term.

**Accessibility:** a real description list, so screen readers announce the pairs and their
count; a detail may hold any markup (a badge, a link). Checked by axe-core in headless
Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or
critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** without container queries the terms stay above their details; without
subgrid the term column is a fixed 10rem. An empty detail shows a dash.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.description_list().item("Plan", "Team").item("Seats", "12").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("<dt>Plan</dt><dd>Team</dd>"));

let m = ui.description_list().stacked().item("Status", ui.badge("Active").ok());
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains("lui-description-list lui-description-list-stacked") && html.contains("Active"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { DescriptionList stacked { item "Status" (ui.badge("Active").ok()); } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Toggle group

`loco_ui::toggle_group` · demo: `/toggle-group`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `ToggleGroup` | `ui.toggle_group(name: &str, label: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `ToggleGroup`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `option` | item | `value: &'a str, text: &'a str` |  | `value` | An option posting `value`, shown as `text`. |
| `icon` | modifier | `icon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | The option added last shows this icon, its text becoming a hidden label. |
| `disabled` | modifier |  |  | `disabled` | The option added last cannot be pressed. |
| `value` | value | `value: &'a str` |  | `checked` | Press this option (again for more with `.multiple()`); the query's own values by default. |
| `multiple` | switch |  | `off` | `type` | Several options may be pressed (checkboxes, not radios). |
| `size` | choice: 1, 2, 3 | `size: impl Into<Size>` | `2` |  | The items' height and text: Radix's sizes 1 to 3. |
| `radius` | choice: none, small, medium, large, full | `radius: Radius` | `medium` |  | The corners of the track and the chip, from square to a pill. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<fieldset>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `:checked` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `:focus-visible` | 86 | 85 | 15.4 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: partly: applying a choice the moment it is pressed needs script (or the form's submit)
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes SegmentedControl

## Documentation

A row of pressable options, one picked (alignment) or several (bold, italic), part of the
form around it. Each option is a real radio button or checkbox, drawn as a segmented
button, so the form posts the choice and the browser handles the keys.

**Platform features:** `<fieldset>` of `<input type="radio">` (one) or
`type="checkbox"` (several) inside their labels; `:checked` and `:focus-visible` on the
input style the face next to it (every browser).

**Accessibility:** a `<fieldset>` named by its visually hidden `<legend>`; arrow keys move
between radios and Space toggles a checkbox, as the platform does; an icon-only option has
its text as a hidden label. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route,
both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** apply a choice the moment it is pressed; the
surrounding form sends it (a submit button, or the enhancement script's in-place post).

The look follows Radix Themes SegmentedControl: a gray track, items of one width, the
picked one a raised chip; with one pick the chip slides between items (CSS only, `:has()`
and a transition), in Radix's sizes 1 to 3 (`.size(..)`) and radii (`.radius(..)`). A
narrow container scrolls the row inside itself.

**Fallback:** without `:has()` (Chrome < 105, Firefox < 121) the checked item takes the
chip look itself and nothing slides.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from_request("/editor", "align=center", "");
let m = ui.toggle_group("align", "Alignment").option("left", "Left").option("center", "Center");
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"type="radio" name="align" value="center" checked"#));

let m = ui.toggle_group("style", "Text style").multiple()
    .option("bold", "Bold").icon(Icon::Bold)
    .option("italic", "Italic").icon(Icon::Italic)
    .value("bold");
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"type="checkbox" name="style" value="bold" checked"#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { ToggleGroup("style", "Text style") multiple {
    option "bold" "Bold" icon=(Icon::Bold);
    option "italic" "Italic" icon=(Icon::Italic);
    value "bold";
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
// Smaller, and a pill.
let m = ui.toggle_group("view", "View").option("list", "List").option("grid", "Grid").size(1).radius(Radius::Full);
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"data-size="1" data-radius="full""#));
let same = lui! { ToggleGroup("view", "View") size=1 radius="full" { option "list" "List"; option "grid" "Grid"; } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Context menu

`loco_ui::context_menu` · demo: `/context-menu`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `ContextMenu` | `ui.context_menu(label: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `ContextMenu`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `link` | item | `text: &'a str, href: &'a str` |  |  | A link. |
| `action` | item | `text: &'a str, action: &'a str` |  | `action` | A `<form method="post">` button posting to `action`. |
| `group` | item | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A heading over the items after it. |
| `separator` | item |  |  |  | A rule between groups. |
| `icon` | modifier | `icon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An icon, or a glyph or emoji, before the item's text (decorative, hidden from assistive tech). |
| `shortcut` | modifier | `keys: &'a str` |  |  | A shortcut shown after the item's text, as `<kbd>`. |
| `disabled` | modifier |  |  | `disabled` | The item is shown but not usable. |
| `danger` | modifier |  |  |  | The item is destructive. |
| `body` | value | `body: Markup` |  |  | The thing the actions are on. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The menu's id instead of `ctx-<label>`. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `popover` | 114 | 125 | 17 |
| `popovertarget` | 114 | 125 | 17 |

- Fallback: that of the popover menu: a <details> dropdown
- Needs script: partly: opening on right-click or a long press needs script
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes ContextMenu

## Documentation

Actions on one thing (a file, a card, a row) from a small "more" button in its corner:
the popover menu the way a right-click menu would offer it. A right-click
cannot be caught without script, so the actions sit behind a visible button instead.

**Platform features:** those of the popover menu: `popover`, `popovertarget` and anchor
positioning, a `<details>` dropdown where popovers are missing.

**Accessibility:** the button is named "More actions" (or the label given) and says it opens
a menu; the menu is the popover menu's (`role="menu"`, Escape closes). Checked by axe-core in
headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious
or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** open on right-click or a long press; the button
does it.

**Fallback:** that of the popover menu.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
// The items are the popover menu's: `icon`, `shortcut`, `disabled` and `danger` apply to
// the item just added.
let m = ui.context_menu("report.pdf")
    .link("Open", "/files/1").shortcut("o")
    .separator()
    .action("Delete", "/files/1/delete").danger()
    .body(html! { p { "report.pdf" } });
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"aria-label="More actions: report.pdf""#) && html.contains(r#"action="/files/1/delete""#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { ContextMenu("report.pdf") {
    link "Open" "/files/1" shortcut="o";
    separator();
    action "Delete" "/files/1/delete" danger;
    body() { p { "report.pdf" } }
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# One-time code

`loco_ui::input_otp` · demo: `/otp`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `InputOtp` | `ui.input_otp(name: &str, label: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `InputOtp`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `length` | number | `digits: u8` | `6` | `maxlength` | How many digits the code has. |
| `group` | number | `size: u8` |  |  | A stronger divider after every `size` cells (3 for a 123 456 code). |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The field's id, `f-<name>` by default. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `autocomplete="one-time-code"` | 84 | no | 12 |
| `inputmode="numeric"` | 66 | 95 | 12.1 |
| `pattern` | 4 | 4 | 5 |

- Fallback: a plain spaced-out field; without autocomplete the code is typed or pasted
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: shadcn Input OTP, Origin UI

## Documentation

The box for a code sent by text or email: one field, drawn as a row of cells, that the
phone's keyboard offers to fill from the message. One field (not six) so paste, autofill
and the back key all just work.

**Platform features:** `autocomplete="one-time-code"` (Safari 12, and Chrome on Android
through the WebOTP flow), `inputmode="numeric"` (Chrome 66, Firefox 95, Safari 12.1),
`pattern` and `maxlength` for the length; a monospace face with `letter-spacing` and a
repeating background draws the cells; container query units (`cqi`: Chrome 105, Firefox
110, Safari 16) size them.

**Accessibility:** a labelled text field (not a row of fields), so it is announced once and
typed or pasted in one go; the pattern's hint says how many digits. Checked by axe-core in
headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious
or critical violation).

The look follows the Origin UI OTP input and shadcn InputOTP: joined cells rounded only at
the group's ends, `.group(n)` for a stronger divider after every `n` cells, a ring on the
cell the next digit goes in while the field has focus, and cells that shrink to fit a
narrow container.

**What it does not do without script:** move the caret to the next cell as it would with
separate boxes (there is one box), or send the form when the last digit is typed. The
ringed cell is the one after the value the server rendered; the enhancement script moves
it as digits are typed.

**Fallback:** without the cell background it is a plain spaced-out field.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.input_otp("code", "Code from the text message").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"autocomplete="one-time-code""#) && m.contains(r#"inputmode="numeric""#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"pattern="[0-9]{6}""#) && m.contains(r#"maxlength="6""#));

let m = ui.input_otp("code", "Code").length(4).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"pattern="[0-9]{4}""#) && m.contains("--lui-otp-cells: 4"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { InputOtp("code", "Code") length=4; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// Grouped three and three, like "123 456" in the message.
let m = ui.input_otp("code", "Code").group(3).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("lui-otp-grouped") && m.contains("--lui-otp-group: 3"));
assert_eq!(lui! { InputOtp("code", "Code") group=3; }.into_string(), m);
```

# Drawer

`loco_ui::drawer` · demo: `/nav`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Drawer` | `ui.drawer(label: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Drawer`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `nav` | value | `nav: Markup` |  |  | The navigation inside the drawer, usually a `ul` of links. |
| `body` | value | `body: Markup` |  |  | The page's content, beside the drawer. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The drawer's id instead of `lui-drawer-` and the label's slug. |
| `title` | value | `title: &'a str` |  |  | A heading at the top of the panel (also its accessible name). |
| `description` | value | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A line under the title, the panel's description. |
| `footer` | value | `footer: Markup` |  |  | Actions pinned to the bottom of the panel, under the scrolling navigation. |
| `sidebar` | switch |  | `off` |  | A permanent sidebar above 60rem. |
| `trigger` | value | `button: Button<'a>` |  |  | The opener as a styled button of the caller's; its command or link is the drawer's. |
| `no_trigger` | switch |  | `off` |  | No opener: a link to `?dialog=<id>` or a button elsewhere opens it. |
| `open` | condition | `open: bool` | `off` | `open` | Render it open (non-modal) from the server. |
| `side` | choice: top, bottom, start, end | `side: Side` | `start` |  | The edge it slides in from. |
| `size` | choice: 1, 2, 3 | `size: impl Into<Size>` | `2` |  | 18, 24 or 32rem wide (tall, from the top or bottom). |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<dialog>` | 37 | 98 | 15.4 |
| `command="show-modal"` | 135 | 144 | 26.2 |
| `closedby` | 134 | 141 | 26 |
| `@starting-style` | 117 | 129 | 17.5 |
| `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` | 117 | 129 | 17.4 |
| `@media` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: link to #id and a :target rule; open from the server
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: viewport
- Look after: shadcn Sheet and Drawer

## Documentation

Site navigation that is a sidebar on a wide screen and a drawer sliding in from the edge on
a narrow one, from the same markup: a menu button opens it, Escape, a click outside or the
close button shuts it. No script.

The look follows the shadcn Sheet: a header (title, `.description(..)`, the close ×), the
navigation scrolling in the middle and a `.footer(..)` pinned to the bottom. Under a 30rem
viewport it is the shadcn Drawer instead: the same `<dialog>` rises from the bottom with a
grab handle and rounded top corners, at most 85vh tall. `.side(..)` opens it from the end
edge, the top or the bottom instead of the start, and `.size(..)` makes it narrower or
wider (18, 24 or 32rem; the height for the top and bottom).

**Platform features:**
- `<dialog>` opened as a modal by an invoker button, `command="show-modal"` (Chrome 135+,
  Firefox 144+, Safari 26.2+), closed by `command="close"` and by `closedby="any"` for
  Escape and light dismiss.
- `@starting-style` (Chrome 117, Firefox 129, Safari 17.5) for the slide in, and
  `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` on `display` and `overlay` (Chrome 117,
  Firefox 129, Safari 17.4) for the slide out, the backdrop fading with it; off under
  `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Sidebar mode: above 60rem a `@media` rule shows the closed `<dialog>` in a grid column
  and hides the menu button, so desktop gets a permanent sidebar with no request.

**Fallback:** without `Caps` `Invokers`, the menu button is a link to `#id` and a `:target`
rule shows the drawer; its close control is a link to `#`. `?dialog=<id>` in the URL (or
`.open(true)`) renders it open from the server.

**Accessibility:** a native modal `<dialog>` named by its title: focus moves in, Escape
closes it. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability
variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** swipe to close; focus is not trapped in the
`:target` fallback.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
let nav = html! { ul { li { a href="/" { "Home" } } } };
// The id is `lui-drawer-` and the label's slug: this drawer is `#lui-drawer-menu`.
let m = ui.drawer("Menu").nav(nav.clone()).body(html! { p { "Page" } }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"command="show-modal" commandfor="lui-drawer-menu""#) && m.contains(r#"closedby="any""#));
// `?dialog=lui-drawer-menu` opens it from the server (and, for one release, the
// `?dialog=menu` written before the prefix).
let ui = Ui::from_request("/", "dialog=lui-drawer-menu", "");
let m = ui.drawer("Menu").title("Browse").sidebar().nav(nav.clone()).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("lui-drawer-sidebar") && m.contains(" open>"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Drawer("Menu") title="Browse" sidebar nav=(nav); };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// A description under the title and a footer under the navigation.
let m = ui.drawer("Menu").description("Everything in the app.").footer(html! { a href="/signout" { "Sign out" } });
let m = m.render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"aria-describedby="lui-drawer-menu-description""#) && m.contains(r#"<div class="lui-drawer-foot">"#));
let same = lui! { Drawer("Menu") description="Everything in the app." footer={ a href="/signout" { "Sign out" } }; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// A styled opener of your own.
let m = ui.drawer("Menu").trigger(ui.button("Browse").ghost().leading(Icon::Menu)).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"class="lui-button lui-button-ghost lui-drawer-open""#));
// From the end edge, wide.
let m = ui.drawer("Filters").side(Side::End).size(3).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"class="lui-drawer-panel" data-side="end" data-size="3""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Drawer("Filters") side=(Side::End) size=3; }.into_string(), m);
```

# Command palette

`loco_ui::palette` · demo: `/palette`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Palette` | `ui.palette(action: &str)` | stable |

## Props of `Palette`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `link` | item | `label: &'a str, href: &'a str` |  |  | A destination. |
| `links` | value | `links: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'a str, &'a str)>` |  |  | Several `(label, href)` destinations at once. |
| `keywords` | modifier | `keywords: &'a str` |  |  | Extra words that find the command added last, space-separated. |
| `icon` | modifier | `icon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An icon before the command added last. |
| `shortcut` | modifier | `keys: &'a str` |  |  | A key hint at the end of the command added last (shown, not bound). |
| `group` | item | `heading: &'a str` |  |  | List the commands added after this under a heading. |
| `label` | value | `label: &'a str` | `Search` |  | The opener's label (default "Search"). |
| `accesskey` | value | `key: &'a str` | `k` | `accesskey` | The opener's access key (default `k`). |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` | `lui-palette` | `id` | The palette's id instead of `lui-palette`. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `popover` | 114 | 125 | 17 |
| `<datalist>` | 20 | 4 | 12.1 |
| `<search>` | 118 | 118 | 17 |
| `accesskey` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: a <details> disclosure with the same form
- Needs script: partly: arrow keys through live results and a global Ctrl+K need script
- Responsive by: viewport
- Look after: shadcn Command

## Documentation

A search box that jumps anywhere: open it from a button or with an access key, type, pick
a suggestion, press Enter. The browser filters the suggestions as you type; the server does
the rest. An exact name goes straight to its page; anything else lands on a results list.
This is the flagship "no script needed" component.

**Platform features:**
- `popover` (Chrome 114, Firefox 125, Safari 17) opened by `popovertarget`; light dismiss
  and Escape for free; `autofocus` puts the caret in the box when it opens.
- `<datalist>` bound by `list=` for as-you-type suggestions, filtered by the browser.
- `<search>` (Chrome 118, Firefox 118, Safari 17) around a GET `<form>`; the server
  redirects an exact name (`Palette::exact`) and lists the matches of anything else.
- `accesskey` on the opener (Alt+Shift+K in Chrome and Firefox, Ctrl+Option+K in Safari),
  announced with `aria-keyshortcuts`.

**Fallback:** without `Caps` `Popover` the palette is a `<details>` disclosure with the
same form inside. A browser without `<datalist>` shows a plain search box; the results
page still works.

**Accessibility:** a labelled search field with `aria-keyshortcuts`, results in a section
named by its heading, every command a link. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every
demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** arrow-key navigation through a live results list
and the global Ctrl+K shortcut (the access key stands in for it).

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
// A search for "new" that matched no command exactly.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/search", "q=new", "");
let palette = ui.palette("/search")
    .group("Go to")
    .link("Open settings", "/settings")
    .link("New invoice", "/invoices/new").keywords("bill create");
assert_eq!(palette.exact(), None, "an exact name would redirect");
let m = palette.render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"popovertarget="lui-palette""#) && m.contains(r#"list="lui-palette-list""#));
assert!(m.contains("lui-palette-results") && m.contains("New invoice"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Palette("/search") {
    group "Go to";
    link "Open settings" "/settings";
    link "New invoice" "/invoices/new" keywords="bill create";
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
let ui = Ui::from_request("/search", "q=open+settings", "");
assert_eq!(ui.palette("/search").link("Open settings", "/settings").exact(), Some("/settings"));
// An icon and a key hint on a row.
let m = ui.palette("/search").link("Open settings", "/settings").icon(Icon::Pencil).shortcut("⌘ ,").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<kbd class="lui-palette-shortcut">⌘ ,</kbd>"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Palette("/search") { link "Open settings" "/settings" icon=(Icon::Pencil) shortcut="⌘ ,"; } }.into_string(), m);
```

# Marquee

`loco_ui::marquee` · demo: `/marquee`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Marquee` | `ui.marquee(label: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Marquee`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | item | `text: &'a str` |  |  | One item of plain text. |
| `item` | item | `markup: Markup` |  |  | One item of markup: a logo, a quote, a card. |
| `reverse` | switch |  | `off` |  | Scroll towards the end of the line instead of the start. |
| `duration` | number | `seconds: u32` | `40` | `style` | Seconds for one full loop (`--lui-marquee-duration`). |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inert` | 102 | 112 | 15.5 |
| `translate` | 104 | 72 | 14.1 |
| `animation-play-state` | 43 | 16 | 9 |
| `mask-image` | 120 | 53 | 15.4 |

- Fallback: at rest: the items wrap and the copy is hidden, without translate or under reduced motion
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Magic UI Marquee

## Documentation

A row that scrolls sideways on its own and loops: customer logos, a line of testimonials,
the tags of a changelog. It stops while the pointer is over it or focus is inside it, so a
link in it can be read and followed.

**Platform features:** a `<ul>` of the items, then the same list again with
`aria-hidden="true"` and `inert` (Chrome 102, Firefox 112, Safari 15.5), so the copy is
neither read nor focused. A `@keyframes` animation moves the pair with the `translate`
property (Chrome 104, Firefox 72, Safari 14.1) by exactly one list and a gap, so the copy
lands where the first list began and the loop has no seam; `animation-play-state` pauses it
on `:hover` and `:focus-within`. The edges fade out with `mask-image` (Chrome 120, Firefox
53, Safari 15.4). The pace is `--lui-marquee-duration` (40s), or `.duration(..)`.

**Accessibility:** a `role="region"` named by the label; the items are read once, in order,
since the copy is `aria-hidden` and `inert`; the motion stops on hover and focus, and does
not start under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox
on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical
violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** the motion sits inside `@supports (translate: 100%)` and
`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. Without either, the row is at rest: the
items wrap onto as many lines as they need and the copy is not shown.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.marquee("Customers").text("Acme").text("Globex").render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<div class="lui-marquee" role="region" aria-label="Customers">"#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"<ul class="lui-marquee-group" aria-hidden="true" inert>"#));
assert_eq!(m.matches("<li class=\"lui-marquee-item\">Acme</li>").count(), 2);
// Markup items, the other way round, at its own pace.
let quotes = ui.marquee("What people say")
    .item(html! { blockquote { "Fast." } })
    .item(html! { blockquote { "No script!" } })
    .reverse()
    .duration(20);
let quotes = quotes.render().into_string();
assert!(quotes.contains("lui-marquee lui-marquee-reverse") && quotes.contains("--lui-marquee-duration: 20s"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! {
    Marquee("What people say") reverse duration=20 {
        item() { blockquote { "Fast." } }
        item() { blockquote { "No script!" } }
    }
};
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), quotes);
```

# Heading

`loco_ui::heading` · demo: `/typography`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Heading` | `ui.heading(text: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Heading`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | value | `size: u8` | `6` |  | Radix's sizes 1–9: 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 24, 28, 35 or 60px. |
| `as_h` | number | `level: u8` | `1` |  | The element, `<h1>` to `<h6>`: the level in the page's outline. |
| `weight` | choice: light, regular, medium, bold | `weight: Weight` | `bold` |  | How heavy the letters are. |
| `trim` | switch |  | `off` |  | Trim the space above the capitals and below the baseline. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<h1>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `text-wrap: balance` | 114 | 121 | 17.5 |
| `text-box` | 133 | no | 18.2 |

- Fallback: untrimmed line box without text-box; greedy line breaks without balance
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: Radix Themes Heading

## Documentation

A section title at one of nine sizes, its level chosen apart from its size so the outline
stays right when the look calls for a small `<h1>` or a large `<h3>`. After Radix Themes
Heading: sizes 1 to 9 on Radix's type scale (12 to 60px), size 6 and bold by default,
the letters drawn tighter as they grow, and `.trim()` for the space above the capitals
and below the baseline.

**Platform features:** `<h1>` to `<h6>` (baseline 1995); `text-wrap: balance` (Chrome 114,
Firefox 121, Safari 17.5) so a long title breaks into even lines; `.trim()` uses
`text-box` (Chrome 133, Safari 18.2, not Firefox yet) under `@supports`.

**Accessibility:** a real heading element, so screen readers list it and jump to it; the
level is `.as_h(..)`, never implied by the size. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on
every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical
violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** without `text-box` a trimmed heading keeps its line's half-leading above and
below; without `text-wrap: balance` the lines break greedily.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let h = ui.heading("Projects").render().into_string();
assert_eq!(h, r#"<h1 class="lui-heading" data-size="6">Projects</h1>"#);
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Heading("Projects"); };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), h);
// A small second-level heading in medium weight, its line box trimmed.
let h = ui.heading("Members").size(3).as_h(2).weight(Weight::Medium).trim().render().into_string();
assert_eq!(h, r#"<h2 class="lui-heading lui-heading-trim" data-size="3" data-weight="medium">Members</h2>"#);
assert_eq!(lui! { Heading("Members") size=3 as_h=2 weight="medium" trim; }.into_string(), h);
```

# Text

`loco_ui::text` · demo: `/toggle-group`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Text` | `ui.text(text: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Text`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | value | `size: u8` | `inherit` |  | Radix's sizes 1–9: 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 24, 28, 35 or 60px. |
| `weight` | choice: light, regular, medium, bold | `weight: Weight` | `inherit` |  | How heavy the letters are. |
| `tone` | choice: neutral, brand, ok, warn, danger, info | `tone: Tone` | `inherit` |  | The colour: step 11 of the tone's scale. |
| `as_p` | switch |  | `off` |  | A `<p>`: a paragraph of its own. |
| `as_div` | switch |  | `off` |  | A `<div>`: a block that is not a paragraph (a caption, a cell's second line). |
| `muted` | switch |  | `off` |  | The muted gray of hints and secondary lines. |
| `truncate` | switch |  | `off` |  | One line, cut with an ellipsis where it overflows. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text-overflow: ellipsis` | 1 | 7 | 1.3 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: Radix Themes Text

## Documentation

A run of text at a size, weight and colour from the type scale: a caption, a lede, a
muted hint, a status in the danger colour, a file name cut short with an ellipsis. After
Radix Themes Text: sizes 1 to 9 on the scale Heading uses, an inline `<span>` by default
and a `<p>` or `<div>` on request, `.truncate()` for one line.

`ui.text(..)` is also how a component reads its own words: given a
`Text` key it returns the word in the visitor's language, given a
`&str` it returns this builder (`TextArg`).

**Platform features:** `<span>`, `<p>` and `<div>` (baseline 1995); `.truncate()` is
`text-overflow: ellipsis` (Chrome 1, Firefox 7, Safari 1.3) on one line.

**Accessibility:** plain text, read in place; colour is never the only signal (a danger
text says what went wrong). A truncated text keeps its whole content in the DOM, so a
screen reader reads all of it. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route,
both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let t = ui.text("Last edited today").render().into_string();
assert_eq!(t, r#"<span class="lui-text">Last edited today</span>"#);
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Text("Last edited today"); };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), t);
// A muted paragraph at size 2, and a danger line in medium weight.
let p = ui.text("No invoices yet.").as_p().size(2).muted().render().into_string();
assert_eq!(p, r#"<p class="lui-text lui-text-muted" data-size="2">No invoices yet.</p>"#);
assert_eq!(lui! { Text("No invoices yet.") as_p size=2 muted; }.into_string(), p);
let e = ui.text("Payment failed").tone(Tone::Danger).weight(Weight::Medium).truncate();
let e = e.render().into_string();
assert!(e.contains(r#"class="lui-text lui-text-truncate" data-weight="medium" data-tone="danger""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Text("Payment failed") tone="danger" weight="medium" truncate; }.into_string(), e);
```

# Link

`loco_ui::link` · demo: `/toast`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Link` | `ui.link(text: &str, href: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Link`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `underline` | choice: always, hover, none | `underline: Underline` | `always` |  | When the underline shows: always, on hover, or never. |
| `external` | switch |  | `off` |  | Opens in a new tab, with an arrow and a hint for screen readers. |
| `muted` | switch |  | `off` |  | The muted gray, the text colour on hover: a footer's or a caption's links. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<a href>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `text-underline-offset` | 87 | 70 | 12.1 |
| `target="_blank"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: Radix Themes Link

## Documentation

A styled `<a>`: in running text, in a footer, in a table cell, or out to another site with
an arrow and a hint that it opens a new tab. After Radix Themes Link: step 11 of the brand
scale, a thin underline offset below the baseline in a paler step, and the three
`underline` choices (always, on hover, never).

**Platform features:** `<a href>` (baseline 1995); `text-underline-offset` and
`text-decoration-thickness` (Chrome 87, Firefox 70, Safari 12.1); `.external()` adds
`target="_blank"` with `rel="noreferrer"` (which implies `noopener`).

**Accessibility:** a real link, so it is in the tab order and listed as one. Underlined by
default so it never relies on colour alone in a paragraph; an external link says "(opens
in a new tab)" to a screen reader and draws its arrow `aria-hidden`. Checked by axe-core
in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no
serious or critical violation).
A link in running text keeps the text's height under a coarse pointer: WCAG 2.5.8
exempts inline targets, and a 44px link would break the line spacing.

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let a = ui.link("Pricing", "/pricing").render().into_string();
assert_eq!(a, r#"<a class="lui-link" href="/pricing">Pricing</a>"#);
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Link("Pricing", "/pricing"); };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), a);
// Out to another site, muted, underlined only under the pointer.
let a = ui.link("Radix", "https://www.radix-ui.com").external().muted().underline(Underline::Hover);
let a = a.render().into_string();
assert!(a.starts_with(r#"<a class="lui-link lui-link-muted" data-underline="hover" href="https://www.radix-ui.com" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">Radix"#));
assert!(a.contains(r#"<span class="lui-sr"> (opens in a new tab)</span>"#));
let same = lui! { Link("Radix", "https://www.radix-ui.com") external muted underline="hover"; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), a);
```

# Kbd

`loco_ui::kbd` · demo: `/typography`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Kbd` | `ui.kbd(keys: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Kbd`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | choice: 1, 2, 3 | `size: impl Into<Size>` | `2` |  | Size 1 at 0.7em of the text around it, 2 at 0.75rem (the default), 3 at 0.875rem. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<kbd>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `box-shadow` | 10 | 4 | 5.1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: Radix Themes Kbd

## Documentation

A key or a shortcut drawn as a keycap: `⌘K` in a menu, `Esc` in a dialog's hint, `Ctrl`
`Shift` `P` in the docs. After Radix Themes Kbd: the system font at 0.75rem, a box
1.75em tall and at least as wide, a pale fill and a two-part inset shadow that reads as a
key's edge.

**Platform features:** `<kbd>` (baseline 1995); `box-shadow` (Chrome 10, Firefox 4,
Safari 5.1).

**Accessibility:** `<kbd>` is user input, read as its text ("⌘K" is read as the
characters it holds; write `Ctrl K` where the symbol would be unclear). Checked by axe-core
in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no
serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing; it shows a shortcut, it does
not bind one (`accesskey` on a button does that).

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let k = ui.kbd("⌘K").render().into_string();
assert_eq!(k, r#"<kbd class="lui-kbd">⌘K</kbd>"#);
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Kbd("⌘K"); };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), k);
// Larger, in a heading-sized hint.
let k = ui.kbd("Esc").size(3).render().into_string();
assert_eq!(k, r#"<kbd class="lui-kbd" data-size="3">Esc</kbd>"#);
assert_eq!(lui! { Kbd("Esc") size=3; }.into_string(), k);
```

# Code

`loco_ui::code` · demo: `/otp`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Code` | `ui.code(text: &str)` | beta |
| `CodeBlock` | `ui.code_block(text: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Code`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tone` | choice: neutral, brand, ok, warn, danger, info | `tone: Tone` | `neutral` |  | The colour of the tint and the text. |
| `variant` | choice: solid, soft, surface, outline, ghost | `variant: Variant` | `soft` |  | A tint (soft), a fill (solid), a tint in a border (surface), a border (outline) or the text alone (ghost). |

## Props of `CodeBlock`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `language` | value | `language: &'a str` |  |  | The language, written as `class="language-…"` for a highlighter. |
| `title` | value | `title: &'a str` |  |  | A file name or caption above the code; it names the region too. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | Replace the id derived from the title (or the code). |
| `copy` | switch |  | `off` |  | A copy button in the corner, shown and wired by the enhancement script only. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<pre>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `overflow-x: auto` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `tab-size` | 21 | 91 | 7 |
| `navigator.clipboard` | 66 | 63 | 13.1 |

- Fallback: select the text: the copy button is hidden until the script shows it
- Needs script: partly: the copy button needs script; without it the code is selected by hand
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Code, shadcn/ui docs code block

## Documentation

Code in two shapes: `Ui::code` for a name or a command inside a sentence, and
`Ui::code_block` for lines of it, kept as written and scrolled sideways inside their
own box. After Radix Themes Code (inline: the monospace font at 0.95em on a soft tint of
the tone, or solid, surface, outline or ghost) and the shadcn/ui docs' code block (a
bordered panel, an optional file name above, a copy button in the corner).

The library does no syntax highlighting, so it stays free of dependencies: `.language("rust")`
writes `class="language-rust"` on the `<code>`, which any highlighter (a server-side one
such as syntect, as the demo uses, or highlight.js) picks up.

**Platform features:** `<code>` and `<pre>` (baseline 1995); `overflow-x: auto` so long
lines scroll inside the block, never the page; `tab-size` (Chrome 21, Firefox 91,
Safari 7). `.copy()` adds a button for the enhancement script, which writes the code with
`navigator.clipboard` (Chrome 66, Firefox 63, Safari 13.1).

**Accessibility:** the block is a `role="region"` named by its title, or by "Code", with
`tabindex="0"` so a keyboard can scroll a long line. The copy button is a real button
reading "Copy", then "Copied" for two seconds. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on
every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical
violation).

**What it does not do without script:** copy. The button is rendered `hidden` and only the
enhancement script shows it, so a page without script has no button that does nothing.

**Fallback:** select the text: the code is plain text in the page.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let c = ui.code("cargo add loco-ui").render().into_string();
assert_eq!(c, r#"<code class="lui-code">cargo add loco-ui</code>"#);
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Code("cargo add loco-ui"); };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), c);
let c = ui.code("Ok(())").tone(Tone::Brand).variant(Variant::Outline).render().into_string();
assert_eq!(c, r#"<code class="lui-code" data-tone="brand" data-variant="outline">Ok(())</code>"#);
assert_eq!(lui! { Code("Ok(())") tone="brand" variant="outline"; }.into_string(), c);
// A block with a file name and a copy button (shown by the script only).
let block = ui.code_block("[dependencies]\nloco-ui = \"0.2\"").language("toml").title("Cargo.toml").copy();
let block = block.render().into_string();
assert!(block.contains(r#"<pre class="lui-code-block-pre" id="code-cargo-toml" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Cargo.toml"><code class="lui-code-block-code language-toml">[dependencies]"#));
assert!(block.contains(r#"data-lui="copy" hidden"#));
let same = lui! { CodeBlock("[dependencies]\nloco-ui = \"0.2\"") language="toml" title="Cargo.toml" copy; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), block);
```

# Blockquote

`loco_ui::blockquote` · demo: `/typography`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Blockquote` | `ui.blockquote()` | beta |

## Props of `Blockquote`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `body` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | The quotation. |
| `caption` | value | `source: &'a str` |  |  | Who said it, or the work it is from, in a `<cite>` under the quotation. |
| `cite` | value | `url: &'a str` |  | `cite` | The URL of the source, written as the blockquote's `cite` attribute. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<figure>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `border-inline-start` | 87 | 66 | 14.1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: Radix Themes Blockquote

## Documentation

A quotation set apart from the text around it, with the person or work it comes from
underneath: a testimonial, a passage from the docs, a line from a review. After Radix
Themes Blockquote: a bar in a pale step of the brand scale down the start edge, the text
indented past it at the size around it, and a muted caption.

**Platform features:** `<figure>`, `<blockquote>`, `<figcaption>` and `<cite>` (baseline
2011 for figure); `border-inline-start` (Chrome 87, Firefox 66, Safari 14.1) so the bar
moves to the right in a right-to-left page.

**Accessibility:** a `<blockquote>` inside a `<figure>` whose `<figcaption>` holds the
source, the pattern the HTML standard gives for a quotation with its attribution. Checked by
axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark
(no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let q = ui.blockquote().body(html! { p { "Simple things should be simple." } }).render().into_string();
assert_eq!(q, r#"<figure class="lui-blockquote"><blockquote class="lui-blockquote-quote"><p>Simple things should be simple.</p></blockquote></figure>"#);
// The same in `lui!`, where the block is the quotation:
let same = lui! { Blockquote { p { "Simple things should be simple." } } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), q);
// With its source, as text and as a URL.
let q = ui.blockquote().caption("Alan Kay").cite("https://example.com/kay").body(html! { "Simple things should be simple." });
let q = q.render().into_string();
assert_eq!(q, r#"<figure class="lui-blockquote"><blockquote class="lui-blockquote-quote" cite="https://example.com/kay">Simple things should be simple.</blockquote><figcaption class="lui-blockquote-caption"><cite>Alan Kay</cite></figcaption></figure>"#);
let same = lui! { Blockquote caption="Alan Kay" cite="https://example.com/kay" { "Simple things should be simple." } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), q);
```

# Prose

`loco_ui::prose` · demo: `/prose`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Prose` | `ui.prose()` | beta |

## Props of `Prose`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `body` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | The HTML to style: headings, paragraphs, lists, quotes, code, tables. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:where()` | 88 | 78 | 14 |
| `text-wrap: pretty` | 117 | no | 26 |

- Fallback: greedy line breaks without text-wrap: pretty
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: shadcn/ui Typography

## Documentation

Styles for plain HTML you did not build from components: a blog post rendered from
Markdown, a help page, release notes. Inside it, bare `h1` to `h4`, `p`, `a`, lists,
`blockquote`, `code`, `pre`, `kbd`, `hr`, `table` and `img` get a readable rhythm; outside
it, those elements keep the browser's look and the components keep theirs. After shadcn/ui
Typography: an extra-bold `h1`, a ruled `h2`, 1.75rem lines, 1.5rem between paragraphs,
lists indented 1.5rem, an italic quote behind a 2px bar.

**Platform features:** `:where()` and `:is()` (Chrome 88, Firefox 78, Safari 14) keep
every rule at the weight of one element, so a component placed inside prose, or a class
of the app's own, wins; `text-wrap: pretty` (Chrome 117, Safari 26) where present.

**Accessibility:** styles only; the HTML it wraps keeps its own headings, lists and
tables. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability
variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** without `text-wrap: pretty` paragraphs break greedily.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
// Markdown rendered elsewhere goes in as `PreEscaped`, after it has been sanitised.
let m = ui.prose().body(PreEscaped("<p>From <em>Markdown</em>.</p>".to_owned())).render().into_string();
assert!(m.ends_with("<p>From <em>Markdown</em>.</p></div>"));
let doc = html! { h2 { "Install" } p { "Add the crate." } };
let m = ui.prose().body(doc.clone()).render().into_string();
assert_eq!(m, r#"<div class="lui-prose"><h2>Install</h2><p>Add the crate.</p></div>"#);
// The same in `lui!`, where the block is the content:
let same = lui! { Prose { h2 { "Install" } p { "Add the crate." } } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
```

# Container

`loco_ui::container` · demo: `/container`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Container` | `ui.container()` | beta |

## Props of `Container`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `body` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | What the column holds. |
| `size` | value | `size: u8` | `4` |  | Radix's sizes 1–4: at most 448, 688, 880 or 1136px wide. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max-width` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `min()` | 79 | 75 | 11.1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Container

## Documentation

A centred column of a fixed greatest width: the readable middle of a page, a narrow form,
a wide dashboard. After Radix Themes Container: four widths (448, 688, 880 and 1136px),
size 4 by default, centred by auto margins, as wide as its parent below that.

**Platform features:** `max-width` with `margin-inline: auto` (baseline 2010); `min()`
(Chrome 79, Firefox 75, Safari 11.1) keeps the column inside a narrower parent.

**Accessibility:** layout only: a `<div>` with no role; reading order is source order.

light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;

let m = ui.container().body(html! { p { "Centred" } }).render().into_string();
assert_eq!(m, r#"<div class="lui-container"><p>Centred</p></div>"#);
// The same in `lui!`, where the block is the body:
let same = lui! { Container { p { "Centred" } } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// Size 1: 448px, for a sign-in form.
let m = ui.container().size(1).body(html! { p { "Narrow" } }).render().into_string();
assert_eq!(m, r#"<div class="lui-container" data-size="1"><p>Narrow</p></div>"#);
```
