
# Section

`loco_ui::section` · demo: `/container`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Section` | `ui.section()` | beta |

## Props of `Section`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `body` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | What the band holds. |
| `size` | value | `size: u8` | `3` |  | Radix's sizes 1–4: 24, 40, 64 or 80px above and below. |
| `label` | value | `label: &'a str` |  | `aria-label` | A name (`aria-label`), which makes the section a region landmark. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<section>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `padding-block` | 87 | 66 | 14.1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: Radix Themes Section

## Documentation

A band of a page with room above and below it: the hero, the features, the pricing, each
one `<section>` apart from the next. After Radix Themes Section: four heights of vertical
padding (24, 40, 64 and 80px), size 3 by default.

**Platform features:** `<section>` (baseline 2011) and `padding-block` (Chrome 87,
Firefox 66, Safari 14.1).

**Accessibility:** a `<section>` with no name is a generic block to assistive tech; give it
a heading inside (a `ui.heading(..)`) and `.label(..)` to make it a named region in the
page's landmarks. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both
capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.section().body(html! { h2 { "Features" } }).render().into_string();
assert_eq!(m, r#"<section class="lui-section"><h2>Features</h2></section>"#);
// The same in `lui!`, where the block is the body:
let same = lui! { Section { h2 { "Features" } } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// The tallest band, named for the landmarks list.
let m = ui.section().size(4).label("Pricing").body(html! { h2 { "Pricing" } }).render().into_string();
assert_eq!(m, r#"<section class="lui-section" data-size="4" aria-label="Pricing"><h2>Pricing</h2></section>"#);
assert_eq!(lui! { Section size=4 label="Pricing" { h2 { "Pricing" } } }.into_string(), m);
```

# Inset

`loco_ui::inset` · demo: `/container`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Inset` | `ui.inset()` | beta |

## Props of `Inset`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `body` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | What reaches the edges: a picture, a map, a table. |
| `top` | switch |  | `off` |  | Bleed through the card's top edge too (first in a card with no header). |
| `bottom` | switch |  | `off` |  | Bleed through the card's bottom edge too (last in a card with no footer). |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overflow: clip` | 90 | 81 | 16 |

- Fallback: overflow: hidden cuts the same corners
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: Radix Themes Inset

## Documentation

Content that reaches the edges of the card it sits in: a cover picture across the top, a
map, a table with no margin around it. After Radix Themes Inset: it cancels the card's
padding with negative margins on the sides it names, and rounds the corners it shares
with the card.

**Platform features:** negative `margin-inline` and `margin-block` against the card's
padding (baseline); `overflow: clip` (Chrome 90, Firefox 81, Safari 16) so a picture
takes the card's rounded corners.

**Accessibility:** layout only: a `<div>` with no role. Checked by axe-core in headless
Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or
critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** without `overflow: clip` the corners are cut by `overflow: hidden`, the same
to the eye.

An inset bleeds through a card's sides by default. `.top()` and `.bottom()` add the
edges; they work when the inset is the first (or last) thing in a card with no header
(or footer), as Radix's do.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.inset().body(html! { img src="/cover.jpg" alt=""; }).render().into_string();
assert_eq!(m, r#"<div class="lui-inset"><img src="/cover.jpg" alt=""></div>"#);
// The same in `lui!`, where the block is the body:
let same = lui! { Inset { img src="/cover.jpg" alt=""; } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// A cover picture across the top of a card.
let m = ui.inset().top().body(html! { img src="/cover.jpg" alt=""; }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<div class="lui-inset lui-inset-top">"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Inset top { img src="/cover.jpg" alt=""; } }.into_string(), m);
```

# Aspect ratio

`loco_ui::aspect_ratio` · demo: `/container`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `AspectRatio` | `ui.aspect_ratio()` | beta |

## Props of `AspectRatio`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `body` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | What fills the box: a picture, a video, a map. |
| `ratio` | value | `width: u32, height: u32` | `1 / 1` |  | Width to height: `(16, 9)`, `(4, 3)`. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aspect-ratio` | 88 | 89 | 15 |
| `object-fit: cover` | 32 | 36 | 10 |

- Fallback: the box takes its content's height
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes AspectRatio

## Documentation

A box that keeps its width-to-height ratio at every width: a video, a map, a picture whose
file may not have loaded yet, so nothing below it jumps when it does. After Radix Themes
AspectRatio: the ratio as a number (16 / 9, 4 / 3, 1), square by default, the child
stretched to fill it.

**Platform features:** the `aspect-ratio` property (Chrome 88, Firefox 89, Safari 15),
set in a `style` attribute; `object-fit: cover` (Chrome 32, Firefox 36, Safari 10) crops a
picture to the box.

**Accessibility:** layout only: a `<div>` with no role; an `<img>` inside keeps its own
`alt`. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability
variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** a browser without `aspect-ratio` leaves the content in the flow (the child
is stretched over the box only under `@supports (aspect-ratio: 1 / 1)`), so the box takes
its content's height.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.aspect_ratio().body(html! { img src="/a.jpg" alt="A lake"; }).render().into_string();
assert_eq!(m, r#"<div class="lui-aspect-ratio"><img src="/a.jpg" alt="A lake"></div>"#);
// The same in `lui!`, where the block is the body:
let same = lui! { AspectRatio { img src="/a.jpg" alt="A lake"; } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// Widescreen.
let m = ui.aspect_ratio().ratio(16, 9).body(html! { img src="/a.jpg" alt="A lake"; }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<div class="lui-aspect-ratio" style="aspect-ratio: 16 / 9">"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { AspectRatio ratio=(16, 9) { img src="/a.jpg" alt="A lake"; } }.into_string(), m);
```

# Scroll area

`loco_ui::scroll_area` · demo: `/scroll-area`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `ScrollArea` | `ui.scroll_area(label: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `ScrollArea`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `body` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | What scrolls. |
| `height` | value | `height: &'a str` | `16rem` |  | The box's height as a CSS length (`12rem`, `50vh`). |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scrollbar-gutter: stable` | 94 | 97 | 18.2 |
| `scrollbar-width` | 121 | 64 | 18.2 |
| `scroll-state()` | 133 | no | no |

- Fallback: no edge shadows without scroll-state(): the scrollbar alone shows there is more
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes ScrollArea

## Documentation

A box of a set height whose content scrolls inside it: a long list in a sidebar, a log, a
changelog in a card. After Radix Themes ScrollArea: a thin scrollbar in a gray step that
does not move the content when it appears, and (where the browser can tell) a soft shadow
at an edge that has more to scroll to.

**Platform features:** `overflow: auto` (baseline); `scrollbar-gutter: stable` (Chrome 94,
Firefox 97, Safari 18.2) keeps the width when the bar comes and goes; `scrollbar-width`
(Chrome 121, Firefox 64, Safari 18.2) and `scrollbar-color` (Safari 26); the edge shadows are
`scroll-state()` container queries (Chrome 133, not Firefox or Safari yet) on two sticky
edges.

**Accessibility:** a `role="region"` named by its label, with `tabindex="0"` so a keyboard
user can focus it and scroll with the arrow keys (axe's scrollable-region-focusable).
Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants,
light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** without `scroll-state()` there are no edge shadows: the scrollbar alone says
there is more.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.scroll_area("Changelog").body(html! { p { "v0.2" } }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<div class="lui-scroll-area" role="region" aria-label="Changelog" tabindex="0">"#));
// The same in `lui!`, where the block is the body:
let same = lui! { ScrollArea("Changelog") { p { "v0.2" } } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// 12rem tall.
let m = ui.scroll_area("Log").height("12rem").body(html! { p { "…" } }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"style="--lui-scroll-area-height: 12rem""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { ScrollArea("Log") height="12rem" { p { "…" } } }.into_string(), m);
```

# Center

`loco_ui::center` · demo: `/container`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Center` | `ui.center()` | beta |

## Props of `Center`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `body` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | What is centred. |
| `min_height` | value | `height: &'a str` |  |  | At least this tall (a CSS length), so there is room to centre in. |
| `text_center` | switch |  | `off` |  | Centre the lines of text too. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `place-items: center` | 59 | 45 | 11 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Flex align=center justify=center

## Documentation

Its content in the middle of the space it is given, across and down: an empty state in a
panel, a spinner in a card, a sign-in form on a page. After Radix Themes Flex with
`align="center" justify="center"`, as one word.

**Platform features:** `display: grid` with `place-items: center` (Chrome 59, Firefox 45,
Safari 11).

**Accessibility:** layout only: a `<div>` with no role; reading order is source order.
Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants,
light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.center().body(html! { p { "Nothing here yet" } }).render().into_string();
assert_eq!(m, r#"<div class="lui-center"><p>Nothing here yet</p></div>"#);
// The same in `lui!`, where the block is the body:
let same = lui! { Center { p { "Nothing here yet" } } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// At least 12rem tall, the text centred too.
let m = ui.center().min_height("12rem").text_center().body(html! { p { "Nothing here yet" } }).render().into_string();
assert_eq!(m, r#"<div class="lui-center lui-center-text" style="min-height: 12rem"><p>Nothing here yet</p></div>"#);
assert_eq!(lui! { Center min_height="12rem" text_center { p { "Nothing here yet" } } }.into_string(), m);
```

# Spacer

`loco_ui::spacer`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Spacer` | `ui.spacer()` | beta |

## Props of `Spacer`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `min` | value | `length: &'a str` |  |  | The least room it keeps (a CSS length), even when the row is full. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flex: 1 1 auto` | 29 | 28 | 9 |

- Fallback: an empty block outside a flex container
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Box flexGrow=1

## Documentation

An empty part of a row or column that takes the room left over, pushing what follows it to
the far end: the account menu to the right of a toolbar, a footer to the bottom of a
sidebar. After Radix Themes Box with `flexGrow="1"`, the way Radix's own examples push
a toolbar apart (Radix has no spacer component).

**Platform features:** `flex: 1 1 auto` (Chrome 29, Firefox 28, Safari 9) inside a flex
row or column (a `ui.cluster()`, a `ui.stack()`).

**Accessibility:** `aria-hidden`: it holds nothing. Checked by axe-core in headless
Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or
critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** outside a flex container it is an empty block of no height.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;

// At least 2rem, even when the row is full.
let m = ui.spacer().min("2rem").render().into_string();
assert_eq!(m, r#"<div class="lui-spacer" aria-hidden="true" style="flex: 1 0 2rem"></div>"#);
```

# Spinner

`loco_ui::spinner` · demo: `/spinner`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Spinner` | `ui.spinner()` | beta |

## Props of `Spinner`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `size` | choice: 1, 2, 3 | `size: impl Into<Size>` | `2` |  | 12px (size 1), 16px (2, the default) or 20px (3) across. |
| `label` | value | `label: &'a str` | `Loading` |  | What a screen reader announces: what is loading. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@keyframes` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `prefers-reduced-motion` | 74 | 63 | 10.1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: Radix Themes Spinner

## Documentation

A small turning ring that says something is on its way: a panel streaming in, a search
waiting on the server, a busy button (which draws this same ring). After Radix Themes
Spinner: three sizes (12, 16 and 20px), in the colour of the text around it.

**Platform features:** a CSS `@keyframes` rotation (baseline 2015) of a bordered circle with
one side clear; `prefers-reduced-motion` (Chrome 74, Firefox 63, Safari 10.1) slows it
down rather than stopping it, so it still reads as busy.

**Accessibility:** `role="status"` named "Loading" (or `.label(..)`), so a screen reader
announces it once without moving the focus. The ring inside a busy button is
`aria-hidden`, since the button says `aria-busy`. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox
on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical
violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing; it turns while it is on the
page, and the server takes it off by sending the next page (or a stream's next chunk).

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let s = ui.spinner().render().into_string();
assert_eq!(s, r#"<span class="lui-spinner" role="status" aria-label="Loading"></span>"#);
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Spinner; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), s);
// Larger, saying what it waits for.
let s = ui.spinner().size(3).label("Loading results").render().into_string();
assert_eq!(s, r#"<span class="lui-spinner" role="status" aria-label="Loading results" data-size="3"></span>"#);
assert_eq!(lui! { Spinner size=3 label="Loading results"; }.into_string(), s);
```

# Indicator

`loco_ui::indicator` · demo: `/spinner`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Indicator` | `ui.indicator(count: u64)` | beta |

## Props of `Indicator`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `body` | value | `markup: Markup` |  |  | What the badge sits on: a button, an avatar, a link. |
| `max` | number | `max: u64` |  |  | Above this count, show `max+` (`99+`). |
| `tone` | choice: neutral, brand, ok, warn, danger, info | `tone: Tone` | `danger` |  | The badge's colour. |
| `label` | value | `label: &'a str` | `{n} new` |  | What a screen reader says instead of the count in words. |
| `dot` | switch |  | `off` |  | A dot instead of the number. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `inset-inline-end` | 87 | 63 | 14.1 |
| `translate` | 104 | 72 | 14.1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: Origin UI notification badge

## Documentation

A count or a dot pinned to the corner of what it wraps: unread messages on an inbox
button, a status dot on an avatar, new items on a tab. After Origin UI's notification
badges: a solid pill 1.25rem tall in the danger colour (or any tone) on the top end corner,
ringed in the page colour so it reads against the thing under it; "99+" past a maximum.

**Platform features:** `position: absolute` with `inset-inline-end` (Chrome 87, Firefox 63,
Safari 14.1), so the badge moves to the left corner in a right-to-left page;
`translate` (Chrome 104, Firefox 72, Safari 14.1) centres it on the corner.

**Accessibility:** the visible number is `aria-hidden` and a visually hidden text says the
count in words ("3 new", in the visitor's language, or `.label(..)`), so a screen reader
reads "Inbox, 3 new" on a wrapped button. A count of 0 shows nothing. Checked by axe-core
in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no
serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing; the count is the server's, as
of this page (a swap root around it updates it in place with the script).

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.indicator(3).body(html! { (ui.button("Inbox")) }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<span class="lui-indicator"><button type="submit" class="lui-button">Inbox</button>"#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"<span class="lui-indicator-badge" aria-hidden="true">"#) && m.contains(r#"<span class="lui-sr">3 new</span>"#));
// The same in `lui!`, where the block is what it wraps:
let same = lui! { Indicator(3) { Button("Inbox"); } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// A brand dot, and a capped count.
let dot = ui.indicator(1).dot().tone(Tone::Brand).body(html! { (ui.avatar("Ada Lovelace")) });
let dot = dot.render().into_string();
assert!(dot.contains(r#"<span class="lui-indicator-dot" data-tone="brand" aria-hidden="true"></span>"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Indicator(1) dot tone="brand" { Avatar("Ada Lovelace"); } }.into_string(), dot);
let many = ui.indicator(120).max(99).body(html! { "Mail" }).render().into_string();
assert!(many.contains(">99+</span>") && many.contains("120 new"));
assert_eq!(lui! { Indicator(120) max=99 { "Mail" } }.into_string(), many);
```

# Banner

`loco_ui::banner` · demo: `/banner`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Banner` | `ui.banner(text: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Banner`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tone` | choice: neutral, brand, ok, warn, danger, info | `tone: Tone` | `neutral` |  | The bar's colour: neutral is the dark bar, the others a tint. |
| `link` | value | `label: &'a str, href: &'a str` |  |  | A link after the text, with an arrow. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  |  | The id its dismiss cookie is named after instead of the text's slug. |
| `dismiss` | switch |  | `off` |  | A close button that keeps it closed with a `lui-dismiss-<id>` cookie. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<aside>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `cookie` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `<form method="post">` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: Origin UI Banner

## Documentation

A full-width bar across the top of the page for news that concerns the whole site: a
release, planned downtime, a trial running out. One line of text, an optional link, and an
optional close button that keeps it closed on every page from then on. After Origin UI
Banner: a dark bar by default (the neutral tone), or tinted in a `Tone`.

**Platform features:** an `<aside>` named by its text, and a `<form method="post">` (every browser) for
the close button. The form posts to `DISMISS_PATH`, which sets a `cookie`
`lui-dismiss-<id>` for a year and redirects back (Post/Redirect/Get); the next page reads
the cookie through `Ui::dismissed` and renders nothing. The `axum` feature serves that
route in `crate::enhance::router` (Loco's initializer mounts it too); another server
answers it with `dismiss_cookie`.

**Accessibility:** a complementary landmark named by its text; the close button is named
"Dismiss: <text>". Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both
capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** close in place: closing is a round trip (with the
enhancement script too, since the answer is a redirect).

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from_request("/pricing", "", "");
let m = ui.banner("Version 2 is out.").render().into_string();
assert_eq!(m, r#"<aside class="lui-banner" aria-label="Version 2 is out."><p class="lui-banner-text">Version 2 is out.</p></aside>"#);
let m = ui.banner("Version 2 is out.").tone(Tone::Brand).link("Read the notes", "/changelog").dismiss().render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"action="/lui/dismiss""#) && m.contains(r#"name="id" value="version-2-is-out""#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"name="returns_to" value="/pricing""#) && m.contains(r#"href="/changelog""#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Banner("Version 2 is out.") tone="brand" link=("Read the notes", "/changelog") dismiss; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// Once dismissed, the cookie hides it.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/pricing", "", "lui-dismiss-version-2-is-out=1");
assert_eq!(ui.banner("Version 2 is out.").dismiss().render().into_string(), "");
```

# Popover

`loco_ui::popover_card` · demo: `/popover-card`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Popover` | `ui.popover(trigger: &str, body: Markup)` | beta |

## Props of `Popover`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `side` | choice: top, bottom, start, end | `side: Side` | `bottom` |  | The side of the button it opens on; it flips when there is no room. |
| `align` | choice: start, center, end, baseline, stretch | `align: Align` | `start` |  | How it lines up with the button along that side. |
| `arrow` | switch |  | `off` |  | A small arrow pointing at the button. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The panel's id instead of the trigger's slug. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `popover` | 114 | 125 | 17 |
| `anchor-name` | 125 | 147 | 26 |
| `position-try-fallbacks` | 128 | 147 | 26 |
| `@starting-style` | 117 | 129 | 17.5 |

- Fallback: centred in the viewport without anchor positioning; a <details> disclosure without popover
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Radix Themes Popover

## Documentation

A panel of anything (a short form, a profile card, help text) that opens over the page from
a button and closes on a click outside or Escape. Unlike a `crate::popover::Menu` it has
no items: the body is the caller's markup. After Radix Themes Popover: a popover surface
with a medium radius and shadow, 0.5rem from its button (0.75rem with the arrow), on the side and alignment asked
for, with an optional arrow.

**Platform features:**
- `popover` attribute with a `popovertarget` button (Chrome 114, Firefox 125, Safari 17):
  light dismiss, Escape and the top layer.
- CSS anchor positioning (Baseline 2026: Chrome 125, Firefox 147, Safari 26), used
  whatever the caps say: `anchor-name` on the button, `position-anchor` and `position-area`
  on the panel for `.side(..)` and `.align(..)`, and `position-try-fallbacks: flip-block,
  flip-inline` (Chrome 128, Firefox 147, Safari 26) so a panel that would leave the
  viewport opens on the other side. `crate::popover::Menu` and the context menu take
  the same fallbacks; `crate::tooltip::Tooltip` takes the same `Side`.
- `@starting-style` (Chrome 117, Firefox 129, Safari 17.5) and `transition-behavior:
  allow-discrete` for the fade in and out.

**Accessibility:** the button says `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and the platform reports it
expanded while the panel is open; the panel is `role="dialog"` named by the button's text.
Tab moves from the button into the panel. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every
demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** turn the arrow when a fallback flips the panel
(that needs anchored container queries, Chrome-only); the arrow points the asked-for way.

**Fallback:** a browser without anchor positioning shows the popover centred in the
viewport, still usable. Without `Caps` `Popover` it is a `<details>` disclosure whose panel
drops under the button; it closes on a second click, not on a click outside.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
let m = ui.popover("Share", html! { p { "Anyone with the link can view." } }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"popovertarget="share""#) && m.contains(r#"<div id="share" class="lui-popover-card-panel" popover role="dialog" aria-label="Share""#));
let m = ui.popover("Share", html! { p { "Copied." } }).side(Side::Top).align(Align::End).arrow().id("share-2").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("position-area: block-start span-inline-start") && m.contains("lui-popover-card-arrow"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Popover("Share", html! { p { "Copied." } }) side=(Side::Top) align=(Align::End) arrow id="share-2"; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// Without the popover attribute: a <details> disclosure.
let m = Ui::from(Caps::NONE).popover("Share", html! { "x" }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<details class="lui-popover-card lui-popover-card-details""#));
```

# Carousel

`loco_ui::carousel` · demo: `/carousel`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Carousel` | `ui.carousel(label: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Carousel`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `item` | item | `markup: Markup` |  |  | A slide. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  |  | The prefix of the slides' ids (`<id>-<n>`) instead of the label's slug. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scroll-snap-type` | 69 | 68 | 11 |
| `::scroll-button()` | 135 | no | no |
| `::scroll-marker` | 135 | no | no |

- Fallback: fragment links to each slide's id stand in for the scroll buttons and markers
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: shadcn/ui Carousel

## Documentation

Slides side by side in a row that scrolls sideways and snaps to each one, with previous
and next buttons and a dot per slide. After shadcn/ui Carousel: full-width slides, round
outline buttons beside them, small dots under them; rebuilt on CSS scroll snapping instead
of a script.

**Platform features:**
- `scroll-snap-type` (Chrome 69, Firefox 68, Safari 11) and `scroll-behavior: smooth` on
  a scroll container that takes the keyboard (`tabindex="0"`): swipe, trackpad, arrow keys
  and Shift+wheel all move it a slide at a time.
- Where the browser has them, `::scroll-button()` (Chrome 135; not yet in Firefox or
  Safari) draws the previous and next buttons and `::scroll-marker` with
  `scroll-marker-group` (Chrome 135) the dots, both under `@supports`; their names come
  from `data-prev` and `data-next` on the scroller through `attr()`, so they are translated.
  Spec: <https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow-5/>.
- Elsewhere, plain links: each slide has an `id` (`<id>-<n>`) and carries a previous and
  a next link to its neighbours' fragments, and a row of links under the row is the dots.

**Accessibility:** a `<section>` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"` named by its
label; each slide a `role="group"` "slide" named "Slide n of N". The fallback links are
named the same way. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both
capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** play on its own, loop from the last slide to the
first, or mark the current dot in the link fallback (the `::scroll-marker` dots show it
with `:target-current`); a fallback link scrolls the page to the row if it is out of view.

**Fallback:** without `::scroll-button()` and `::scroll-marker` (Firefox, Safari today),
the fragment links above; without scroll snapping, a row that scrolls freely.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.carousel("Photos").item(html! { "One" }).item(html! { "Two" }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<section class="lui-carousel" aria-roledescription="carousel" aria-label="Photos">"#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"id="photos-2" class="lui-carousel-item" role="group" aria-roledescription="slide" aria-label="Slide 2 of 2""#));
assert!(m.contains(r##"href="#photos-1""##) && m.contains(r##"href="#photos-2""##));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Carousel("Photos") { item (html! { "One" }); item (html! { "Two" }); } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
let m = ui.carousel("Photos").id("trip").item(html! { "One" }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"id="trip-1""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Carousel("Photos") id="trip" { item (html! { "One" }); } }.into_string(), m);
```

# Pagination

`loco_ui::pagination` · demo: `/pagination`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Pagination` | `ui.pagination(href: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Pagination`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  |  | Read and write `?page.<id>=` instead of `?page=`, so two lists on one page page on their own. |
| `page` | number | `page: usize` |  |  | Show page `page` (1-based) whatever the request says. |
| `total` | number | `total: usize` | `0` |  | How many items the list holds. |
| `per_page` | number | `per_page: usize` | `10` |  | Items a page. |
| `window` | number | `neighbours: usize` | `1` |  | How many pages to number on each side of the current one. |
| `param` | item | `key: &'a str, value: &'a str` |  |  | A query pair every link carries (a filter, a sort). |
| `first_last` | switch |  | `off` |  | "First" and "Last" links outside Previous and Next. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<nav>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `aria-current="page"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `rel="prev"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `<link rel>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `@container` | 105 | 110 | 16 |

- Fallback: none needed: every page is a link
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: shadcn/ui Pagination

## Documentation

Numbered page links for a list too long for one page: previous and next, the first and
last pages, the current page's neighbours and an ellipsis over each gap. The page shown is
the request's `?page=` (or `?page.<id>=` once given an id), so every page is a URL that
can be bookmarked, and the links keep whatever else the caller names. After shadcn/ui
Pagination.

**Platform features:** a `<nav>` of ordinary links (baseline since HTML 2), the current
page marked `aria-current="page"`, the previous and next links `rel="prev"` and
`rel="next"`; `Pagination::link_rels` puts the same two in the page's `<head>` as
`<link rel>`. A container query (`@container`, Chrome 105, Firefox 110, Safari 16) shows
every number from 30rem; narrower, only the first, the current and the last stay, and
Previous and Next keep their icons.

**Accessibility:** a `<nav>` named "Pages" around a list of links; the current page has
`aria-current="page"`; the ellipses are `aria-hidden`; at either end Previous or Next is a
disabled link (`aria-disabled`, no `href`) so the row keeps its shape. Checked by axe-core
in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no
serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing: each page is a navigation.

**Fallback:** none needed. Every control is a link.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
// Page 5 of 20 (200 items, 10 a page).
let ui = Ui::from_request("/posts", "page=5", "");
let m = ui.pagination("/posts").total(200);
assert_eq!((m.current(), m.pages(), m.range()), (5, 20, 40..50));
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"href="/posts?page=5" aria-current="page""#));
assert!(html.contains(r#"href="/posts?page=4" rel="prev""#) && html.contains(r#"href="/posts?page=6" rel="next""#));
// An id of its own, 25 a page, two neighbours each side, first and last links, and the
// filter carried along.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/posts", "page.posts=3&q=rust", "");
let m = ui.pagination("/posts").id("posts").total(400).per_page(25).window(2).first_last().param("q", "rust");
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"href="/posts?q=rust&amp;page.posts=16">"#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Pagination("/posts") id="posts" total=400 per_page=25 window=2 first_last param=("q", "rust"); };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Steps

`loco_ui::steps` · demo: `/steps`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Steps` | `ui.steps()` | beta |

## Props of `Steps`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `step` | item | `title: &'a str` |  |  | A step titled `title`. |
| `done` | modifier |  |  |  | The step added last is done: a check in its dot, the connector after it filled. |
| `current` | modifier |  |  |  | The step added last is the one the visitor is on (`aria-current="step"`). |
| `invalid` | modifier |  |  |  | The step added last needs attention: a "!" in a danger dot. |
| `optional` | modifier |  |  |  | The step added last can be skipped: "Optional" beside its title. |
| `href` | modifier | `href: &'a str` |  | `href` | The title of the step added last links here. |
| `description` | modifier | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A muted line under the title of the step added last. |
| `vertical` | switch |  | `off` |  | A column at every width instead of a row from 30rem. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<ol>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `aria-current="step"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `@container` | 105 | 110 | 16 |

- Fallback: none needed: a list of links
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: Origin UI Stepper

## Documentation

Where a visitor is in a process of several steps: numbered dots joined by connectors,
each step done, current or still to come, a done step a link back to it. A row of dots
with the titles under them from 30rem, a column below that (or always, with
`.vertical()`). The wizard shows its progress with it. After the Origin
UI Stepper.

**Platform features:** an `<ol>` (baseline since HTML 2) whose current step carries
`aria-current="step"`; the connectors are `::after` boxes; a container query
(`@container`, Chrome 105, Firefox 110, Safari 16) on the list turns the column into a
row.

**Accessibility:** an ordered list, so a screen reader announces "step 2 of 4"; the
current step has `aria-current="step"`; a done step is followed by a hidden "completed",
a step in error by "has errors"; the dots are `aria-hidden`. Checked by axe-core in
headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no
serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing; it is a list of links.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.steps().step("Cart").done().step("Address").current().step("Pay").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<li class="lui-steps-current" aria-current="step">"#));
// A done step that links back, an optional one with a line under it, a column.
let m = ui.steps()
    .step("Account").done().href("/signup?step=0")
    .step("Profile").current().optional().description("A photo and a bio.")
    .step("Review")
    .vertical();
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"<a href="/signup?step=0">Account</a>"#) && html.contains("lui-steps-vertical"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Steps vertical {
    step "Account" done href="/signup?step=0";
    step "Profile" current optional description="A photo and a bio.";
    step "Review";
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Timeline

`loco_ui::timeline` · demo: `/timeline`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Timeline` | `ui.timeline()` | beta |

## Props of `Timeline`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `event` | item | `title: &'a str` |  |  | An event titled `title`. |
| `when` | modifier | `text: &'a str` |  |  | When the event added last happened, as the reader should see it. |
| `datetime` | modifier | `iso: &'a str` |  | `datetime` | The same date for machines (`2026-10-12`): the date becomes a `<time datetime>`. |
| `description` | modifier | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A muted line under the title of the event added last. |
| `icon` | modifier | `icon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An icon in a ring on the line instead of the dot, for the event added last. |
| `tone` | choice: neutral, brand, ok, warn, danger, info | `tone: Tone` |  |  | The colour of the event added last's dot or icon (neutral by default). |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<ol>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `<time datetime>` | 62 | 22 | 7 |
| `@container` | 105 | 110 | 16 |

- Fallback: none needed
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: Flowbite Timeline

## Documentation

What happened, in order: a vertical line with a dot (or an icon) per event, each with
when it happened, a title and a line of description. From 30rem the dates move into a
column of their own left of the line. After the Flowbite Timeline.

**Platform features:** an `<ol>` (baseline since HTML 2); the line is each item's
`::before`; a date given with `.datetime(..)` is a `<time datetime>` (Chrome 62, Firefox
22, Safari 7); a container query (`@container`, Chrome 105, Firefox 110, Safari 16) adds
the date column from 30rem.

**Accessibility:** an ordered list read in order; each event's dot or icon is
`aria-hidden`, so the date, title and description are what is read. Checked by axe-core in
headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no
serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.timeline().event("Founded").when("2019").event("First release").when("2021").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<span class="lui-timeline-when">2019</span>"#));
// An icon and a tone on an event, a description and a machine-readable date.
let m = ui.timeline()
    .event("Deployed").when("12 October").datetime("2026-10-12").icon(Icon::Check).tone(Tone::Ok)
    .description("Version 0.2 is live.")
    .event("Rolled back").when("13 October").tone(Tone::Danger);
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"<li data-tone="ok">"#) && html.contains(r#"<time class="lui-timeline-when" datetime="2026-10-12">"#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Timeline {
    event "Deployed" when="12 October" datetime="2026-10-12" icon=(Icon::Check) tone="ok" description="Version 0.2 is live.";
    event "Rolled back" when="13 October" tone="danger";
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Tree

`loco_ui::tree` · demo: `/tree`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Tree` | `ui.tree(label: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Tree`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `node` | item | `label: &'a str` |  |  | A node reading `label`. |
| `link` | modifier | `href: &'a str` |  |  | The node added last is a link; the one to the current path is marked current. |
| `icon` | modifier | `icon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An icon before the label of the node added last. |
| `children` | modifier | `nodes: impl FnOnce(Tree<'a>) -> Tree<'a>` |  |  | The nodes under the node added last, which makes it a folder. |
| `open` | modifier | `open: bool` |  | `open` | The folder added last starts open while `open` holds. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  |  | The key in `?open.<id>=` instead of the label's slug. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<details>` | 12 | 49 | 6 |
| `aria-current="page"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `--lui-tree-depth` | 49 | 31 | 9.1 |

- Fallback: none needed: <details> works everywhere
- Needs script: partly: arrow keys between nodes (the WAI-ARIA tree pattern) need script
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Origin UI Tree

## Documentation

Nested navigation: folders that open and close, each node a link or a heading, the node
of the current page marked and its folders open. A file browser, a docs outline, a
category tree. After the Origin UI Tree.

**Platform features:** nested `<details>`/`<summary>` (baseline 2020) for the folders,
inside a `<nav>` of lists; `aria-current="page"` on the link to the current path; the
indent is `--lui-tree-depth`, a custom property on each item.

**Accessibility:** a `<nav>` named by its label; each folder is a `<summary>` (Enter or
Space opens it); a folder that is also a link has its link beside the summary, never in
it, and the summary is named by the folder's label; icons and chevrons are `aria-hidden`.
Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants,
light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** arrow keys between nodes (the WAI-ARIA tree
pattern) and remembering a folder opened by hand on the next page: the server opens the
folders `?open.<id>=` names and those around the current page.

**Fallback:** none needed; `<details>` works everywhere.

**Server state:** the folders are numbered in document order from 0, and
`?open.<id>=0,2` (a comma list, see `crate::UiState::opens`, remembered in the `lui-ui`
cookie like an accordion) opens them; so do `.open(true)` and holding the current page.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from_request("/docs/install", "", "");
let m = ui.tree("Docs")
    .node("Intro").link("/docs")
    .node("Guide").children(|t| t.node("Install").link("/docs/install").node("Use").link("/docs/use"))
    .render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"href="/docs/install" aria-current="page""#));
assert!(m.contains("<details open>"), "the folder holding the current page is open");
// Icons, a folder that is a link too, a folder opened by the URL.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/files", "open.files=1", "");
let m = ui.tree("Files")
    .node("src").icon(Icon::Folder).link("/files/src").children(|t| t
        .node("lib.rs").icon(Icon::File).link("/files/src/lib.rs")
        .node("bin").icon(Icon::Folder).children(|t| t.node("main.rs").icon(Icon::File)))
    .node("README.md").icon(Icon::File);
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"<summary class="lui-tree-toggle">"#) && !html.contains("<summary class=\"lui-tree-toggle\"><a"));
assert!(html.contains("--lui-tree-depth: 2"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Tree("Files") {
    node "src" icon=(Icon::Folder) link="/files/src" children=(|t| t
        .node("lib.rs").icon(Icon::File).link("/files/src/lib.rs")
        .node("bin").icon(Icon::Folder).children(|t| t.node("main.rs").icon(Icon::File)));
    node "README.md" icon=(Icon::File);
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Collapsible

`loco_ui::collapsible` · demo: `/collapsible`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Collapsible` | `ui.collapsible(trigger: &str, body: Markup)` | beta |

## Props of `Collapsible`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | condition | `open: bool` | `off` | `open` | Render it open. |
| `ghost` | switch |  | `off` |  | The ghost button look instead of the outline one. |
| `name` | value | `group: &'a str` |  | `name` | Collapsibles with the same `name` are exclusive: opening one closes the others. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<details>` | 12 | 49 | 6 |
| `<details name` | 120 | 130 | 17.2 |
| `::details-content` | 131 | 143 | 18.4 |

- Fallback: opens and closes at once without ::details-content
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: shadcn/ui Collapsible

## Documentation

One section that shows and hides under a button: "Show 3 more", advanced options, the
rest of a long message. The accordion's single cousin, with no group and no state in the
URL. After the shadcn/ui Collapsible.

**Platform features:** one `<details>`/`<summary>` (baseline 2020) whose summary wears the
button look; `<details name>` (baseline 2024) makes several collapsibles exclusive.
`::details-content` (Chrome 131, Firefox 143, Safari 18.4) under `@supports`, with
`interpolate-size: allow-keywords` (Chrome 129), animates the height; elsewhere it snaps.

**Accessibility:** a `<summary>` is a button with an expanded state; Enter or Space
toggles it; the chevron is `aria-hidden`. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every
demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** without `::details-content` it opens and closes at once; without `name` the
sections are not exclusive. No `Caps` branch is needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.collapsible("Show 3 more", html! { p { "The rest." } }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<details class="lui-collapsible"><summary class="lui-button lui-collapsible-trigger">"#));
// Open from the server, ghost, and one of a group where one opens at a time.
let m = ui.collapsible("Advanced", html! { p { "Options." } }).open(true).ghost().name("settings");
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"<details class="lui-collapsible" name="settings" open>"#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Collapsible("Advanced", html! { p { "Options." } }) open=(true) ghost name="settings"; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Hover card

`loco_ui::hover_card` · demo: `/hover-card`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `HoverCard` | `ui.hover_card(trigger: &str, body: Markup)` | beta |

## Props of `HoverCard`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `href` | value | `href: &'a str` |  | `href` | The trigger is a link to `href` instead of a button. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The card's id, `lui-hover-card-<slug of the trigger>` by default. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `interestfor` | 142 | no | no |
| `popover="hint"` | 133 | no | no |
| `popovertarget` | 114 | 125 | 17 |
| `position-area` | 125 | 147 | 26 |

- Fallback: without interestfor a click opens the card (popovertarget); without popover a <details>
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: -
- Look after: Radix Themes HoverCard

## Documentation

A preview card that shows while the pointer rests on a link or it has focus: who a user
is behind their @name, what a linked page holds. Where the browser cannot open it on
hover, a click opens the same card. After the Radix Themes HoverCard.

**Platform features:** with `Caps::InterestInvokers`, `interestfor` on the trigger
(Chrome 142; Firefox and Safari not yet) opens a `popover="hint"` (Chrome 133) on hover
and focus, and closes it when both leave; the trigger is the popover's implicit anchor,
so `position-area` (anchor positioning, Chrome 125, Firefox 147, Safari 26) puts the card
under it. Without it, `popover` with `popovertarget` (Chrome 114, Firefox 125, Safari 17)
opens the card on click and light dismiss closes it.

**Accessibility:** the trigger is a link or a button, and the card follows it in the
document, so a screen reader reaches it after the trigger. A button trigger toggles the card
with Enter or Space; a link trigger gets a separate button, named "More about …", where
hover cannot open the card. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route,
both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** wait before opening (the platform's
`interest-delay` decides) or open on hover where `interestfor` is missing.

**Fallback:** without `Caps::InterestInvokers` the card is `popover="auto"` opened by
click through `popovertarget`: on a button trigger the button itself, on a link trigger a
small chevron button after the link (a link cannot target a popover). Without
`Caps::Popover` it is a `<details>` disclosure under the trigger. Without anchor
positioning the popover sits where the browser centres it.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from(Caps::all());
let m = ui.hover_card("@ada", html! { "Ada Lovelace, first programmer." }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"interestfor="lui-hover-card-ada""#) && m.contains(r#"popover="hint""#));
// A link trigger with its own id; without interest invokers a click opens the card.
let old = Ui::from(Caps::ASSUMED);
let m = old.hover_card("Release notes", html! { "What changed in 0.2." }).href("/changelog").id("notes");
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"<a class="lui-hover-card-link" href="/changelog">Release notes</a>"#) && html.contains(r#"popovertarget="notes""#));
assert!(html.contains(r#"popover="auto""#) && !html.contains("interestfor"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let ui = old;
let same = lui! { HoverCard("Release notes", html! { "What changed in 0.2." }) href="/changelog" id="notes"; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Checkbox group

`loco_ui::checkbox_group` · demo: `/checkbox-group`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `CheckboxGroup` | `ui.checkbox_group(name: &str, legend: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `CheckboxGroup`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `option` | item | `value: &'a str, label: &'a str` |  |  | One choice posting `value` under `<name>[]` when ticked, labelled `label`. |
| `description` | modifier | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A line under the choice added last, read out with it. |
| `disabled` | modifier |  |  | `disabled` | The choice added last cannot be ticked. |
| `cards` | switch |  | `off` |  | Each choice a card, 1, 2 or 3 across by the container's width. |
| `value` | value | `values: &'a [&'a str]` |  | `checked` | The ticked values, instead of the query's `<name>[]`. |
| `help` | value | `help: &'a str` |  |  | Help text under the choices. |
| `error` | value | `message: &'a str` |  |  | A server message under the choices. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | What the checkboxes' ids start from, `f-<name>` by default. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<fieldset>` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `appearance: none` | 84 | 80 | 15.4 |
| `:has()` | 105 | 121 | 15.4 |

- Fallback: none needed: native checkboxes; a ticked card shows no ring without :has()
- Needs script: partly: requiring at least one tick needs the server: HTML has no required for a group
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: Radix Themes CheckboxGroup and CheckboxCards

## Documentation

Several choices under one legend, any number of them ticked: the topics of a newsletter,
the days a shop opens. Each choice is a native checkbox posting `<name>[]`, so the form
sends one pair per ticked box and the server reads them with `Posted::all("<name>[]")`.
A form adds one with `.checkboxes(..)`.

After Radix Themes CheckboxGroup and CheckboxCards: a column of drawn checkboxes with the
label beside each and an optional line under it, or `.cards()` for a grid of bordered
cards that ring in the primary colour when ticked.

**Platform features:** `<fieldset>` + `<legend>` (Chrome 1, Firefox 1, Safari 3) around
`<input type="checkbox">`, drawn with `appearance: none` (Chrome 84, Firefox 80, Safari 15.4); `:has()`
(Chrome 105, Firefox 121, Safari 15.4) rings a ticked card; a container query (Chrome 105,
Firefox 110, Safari 16) lays cards 1, 2 or 3 across.

**Accessibility:** the legend names the group; each checkbox has its `<label>`, a choice's
description is joined by `aria-describedby`, help and the server's error describe the
fieldset, which gets `aria-invalid` with an error. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox
on every demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical
violation).

**What it does not do without script:** require at least one tick (HTML has no
`required` for a group of checkboxes); the server checks it and sends an `.error(..)`.

**Fallback:** none needed: native checkboxes. Without `:has()` a ticked card shows its
tick but no ring; without container queries the cards stay one per row.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
// The ticked values are the query's `topics[]`, or `.value(..)` (saved ones).
let ui = Ui::from_request("/news", "topics%5B%5D=rust", "");
let m = ui.checkbox_group("topics", "Topics").option("rust", "Rust").option("css", "CSS");
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"<legend>Topics</legend>"#));
assert!(html.contains(r#"type="checkbox" name="topics[]" value="rust" checked"#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { CheckboxGroup("topics", "Topics") { option "rust" "Rust"; option "css" "CSS"; } };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
// Cards, a description and a choice that cannot be ticked, with saved values.
let m = ui.checkbox_group("days", "Open on").cards()
    .option("sat", "Saturday").description("10:00 to 14:00")
    .option("sun", "Sunday").disabled()
    .value(&["sat"]).help("Pick the days you open.");
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains("lui-checkbox-cards") && html.contains(r#"value="sun" disabled"#));
assert!(html.contains(r#"aria-describedby="f-days-0-description""#));
let same = lui! { CheckboxGroup("days", "Open on") cards value=(&["sat"]) help="Pick the days you open." {
    option "sat" "Saturday" description="10:00 to 14:00";
    option "sun" "Sunday" disabled;
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Number

`loco_ui::number` · demo: `/number`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Number` | `ui.number(name: &str, label: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Number`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `min` | number | `min: impl Into<f64>` |  | `min` | Lowest value. |
| `max` | number | `max: impl Into<f64>` |  | `max` | Highest value. |
| `step` | number | `step: impl Into<f64>` | `1` | `step` | How far one step moves; the browser accepts only values on a step. |
| `value` | number | `value: impl Into<f64>` |  | `value` | The value, instead of the query's `name`. |
| `prefix` | value | `addon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An addon joined to the field's start (`"$"`). |
| `suffix` | value | `addon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An addon joined to the field's end (`"kg"`). |
| `steppers` | switch |  | `off` |  | Buttons stepping the value down and up: a post without script, `stepUp()` with it. |
| `required` | switch |  | `off` | `required` | The `required` attribute, and a `*` after the label. |
| `disabled` | switch |  | `off` | `disabled` | `disabled` and `aria-disabled`: shown greyed and not posted. |
| `readonly` | switch |  | `off` |  | Shown and posted, not editable; the steppers are off. |
| `hide_label` | switch |  | `off` |  | Only the control, the label kept as its `aria-label`. |
| `help` | value | `help: &'a str` |  |  | Help text under the field. |
| `error` | value | `message: &'a str` |  |  | A server message under the field. |
| `placeholder` | value | `placeholder: &'a str` |  | `placeholder` | Placeholder text. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The control's id, `f-<name>` by default. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type="number"` | 6 | 29 | 5.1 |
| `formnovalidate` | 4 | 4 | 5 |
| `:has()` | 105 | 121 | 15.4 |

- Fallback: none needed: a native number field; a stepper posts the stepped value
- Needs script: partly: stepping in place without a round trip needs the enhancement script
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Origin UI number inputs

## Documentation

A number field with its unit beside it and buttons that step it: a quantity, a price, a
weight. The value is an `f64` written the way Rust writes it, so `2.0` shows as `2` and
`0.1 + 0.2` as `0.3`.

After the Origin UI number inputs ("with chevrons" and "with add-ons"): one bordered row
holding the field, a gray `.prefix(..)`/`.suffix(..)` addon at either end, and
`.steppers()` as two stacked chevron buttons at the end.

**Platform features:** `<input type="number">` with `min`, `max` and `step` (baseline
2015), so the browser refuses a value off the bounds or the step and its arrow keys step
it; the steppers are `<button name value formnovalidate>` (baseline 2015) posting the
value one step down or up; `:has()` (Chrome 105, Firefox 121, Safari 15.4) draws the row's
focus ring.

**Accessibility:** a labelled number field; a text addon is read out with it
(`aria-describedby`), an icon is decoration; the steppers are named "increment" and
"decrement" and disabled at the bounds. Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every
demo route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** step in place. Without the script a stepper
submits the form around it with the stepped value as the first `name` posted (the buttons
come before the field in the markup and show after it), which `crate::Posted::get` and
`Ui::param` read (a derived serde struct rejects the repeated name); the page answers
with the new value. With the enhancement script a
stepper calls `stepUp()`/`stepDown()` on the field and nothing is sent. A stepper is a
submit button, and Enter in any field presses a form's first submit button wherever the
field is: give a stepped number a form of its own, or put a submit button before it.

**Fallback:** none needed: a native number field. Without `:has()` the field keeps its
own focus outline inside the row.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
// The value is the query's `qty`, or `.value(..)` (a saved one).
let ui = Ui::from_request("/cart", "qty=2", "");
let m = ui.number("qty", "Quantity").min(1).max(10).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"name="qty" type="number" value="2" min="1" max="10""#));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { Number("qty", "Quantity") min=1 max=10; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
// A price with its currency and steppers that post 2.5 and 1.5.
let m = ui.number("price", "Price").value(2).step(0.5).min(0).prefix("$").steppers();
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"name="price" value="2.5""#) && html.contains(r#"name="price" value="1.5""#));
assert!(html.contains(r#"<span id="f-price-prefix" class="lui-input-group-prefix">$</span>"#));
let same = lui! { Number("price", "Price") value=2 step=0.5 min=0 prefix="$" steppers; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Search

`loco_ui::search` · demo: `/field`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Search` | `ui.search(name: &str, label: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Search`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | value | `action: &'a str` |  | `action` | Where the search goes; this page by default. |
| `placeholder` | value | `placeholder: &'a str` |  | `placeholder` | Placeholder text. |
| `results_id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `aria-controls` | The id of the results it updates, for `aria-controls`. |
| `keep` | item | `name: &'a str` |  |  | A query parameter of this page carried by the search and by Clear. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The field's id, `f-<name>` by default. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<search>` | 118 | 118 | 17 |
| `type="search"` | 5 | 4 | 5 |
| `aria-controls` | 1 | 1 | 1 |

- Fallback: none needed: an unknown <search> is a block holding the same GET form
- Needs script: partly: searching as you type needs script
- Responsive by: container
- Look after: Radix Themes TextField, shadcn search form

## Documentation

A search box for a page's results: a GET form in a `<search>` landmark, the query in the
URL (`?q=`), so the answer is a page that can be bookmarked, shared and reloaded. A Clear
link appears once there is a query; it is a plain link to the same page without it.

After Radix Themes TextField with a leading magnifier slot (its search example), and the
shadcn/ui search form: the field, then the Search button; Clear as a ghost link.

**Platform features:** the `<search>` element (Chrome 118, Firefox 118, Safari 17; an
unknown element before, which is still a block holding a form), `<form method="get">`
and `<input type="search">` (baseline 2015), `aria-controls` naming the results it
updates.

**Accessibility:** a `search` landmark; the field is named by its label (visually
hidden, as `aria-label`), the magnifier is decoration, Clear is a link named "Clear".
Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants,
light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** search as you type; each search is a page load.
With the enhancement script, a search inside a swap root replaces only that root.

**Fallback:** none needed; where `<search>` is unknown it is an ordinary block and the
form inside works the same.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
// The query is the request's `q`; the form goes back to this page.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/notes", "q=rust&view=list", "");
let m = ui.search("q", "Search notes").render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<search class="lui-search"><form method="get" action="/notes">"#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"name="q" type="search" value="rust""#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"href="/notes""#), "Clear drops the query");
// The same in `lui!`:
assert_eq!(lui! { Search("q", "Search notes"); }.into_string(), m);
// Keep another parameter, name the results it updates, post elsewhere.
let m = ui.search("q", "Search notes").keep("view").results_id("notes").action("/find");
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"<input type="hidden" name="view" value="list">"#));
assert!(html.contains(r#"aria-controls="notes""#) && html.contains(r#"href="/find?view=list""#));
let same = lui! { Search("q", "Search notes") keep="view" results_id="notes" action="/find"; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# Rating

`loco_ui::rating` · demo: `/rating`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `Rating` | `ui.rating(name: &str, label: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `Rating`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max` | number | `stars: u8` | `5` |  | How many stars (1 to 10). |
| `value` | number | `stars: u8` |  | `checked` | The picked score, instead of the query's `name`; 0 for none. |
| `required` | switch |  | `off` | `required` | A star must be picked before the form submits. |
| `readonly` | switch |  | `off` |  | The score shown as an image and posted from a hidden input, not changeable. |
| `disabled` | switch |  | `off` | `disabled` | `disabled` and `aria-disabled`: shown greyed and not posted. |
| `help` | value | `help: &'a str` |  |  | Help text under the stars. |
| `error` | value | `message: &'a str` |  |  | A server message under the stars. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | What the stars' ids start from, `f-<name>` by default. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type="radio"` | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| `:has()` | 105 | 121 | 15.4 |

- Fallback: only the picked star is filled, and hovering fills nothing, without :has()
- Needs script: no
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Origin UI star rating

## Documentation

A row of stars to pick a score from 1 to 5 (or `.max(n)`), part of the form around it:
each star is a radio button, so the form posts the number and the arrow keys move it.
`.readonly()` shows a score without letting it change, and still posts it.

After the Origin UI star ratings: 1.25rem stars in --lui-gray-7, filled in the warning
colour up to the picked one, the stars up to the pointer filled while it hovers.

**Platform features:** `<fieldset>` of `<input type="radio">` (every browser), each star an
inline SVG; `:has()` (Chrome 105, Firefox 121, Safari 15.4) fills the stars before the
checked one and the ones up to the hovered star.

**Accessibility:** a `<fieldset>` named by its legend, each radio named "3 stars"
(visually hidden text), arrow keys move the pick as in any radio group; a read-only rating
is an image named "3 out of 5". Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo
route, both capability variants, light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing: picking a star is choosing a
radio, and the surrounding form sends it.

**Fallback:** without `:has()` only the picked star is filled (a general-sibling `~` rule),
not the ones before it, and hovering fills nothing.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
// The score is the query's `stars`, or `.value(..)` (a saved one).
let ui = Ui::from_request("/review", "stars=4", "");
let m = ui.rating("stars", "Your rating").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<legend>Your rating</legend>"#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"type="radio" name="stars" value="4" checked"#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"<span class="lui-sr">4 stars</span>"#));
// The same in `lui!`:
assert_eq!(lui! { Rating("stars", "Your rating"); }.into_string(), m);
// Out of 10, shown and posted but not changeable.
let m = ui.rating("score", "Score").max(10).value(7).readonly().render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"role="img" aria-label="7 out of 10""#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"<input type="hidden" name="score" value="7">"#));
assert_eq!(lui! { Rating("score", "Score") max=10 value=7 readonly; }.into_string(), m);
```

# Tag input

`loco_ui::tag_input` · demo: `/tag-input`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `TagInput` | `ui.tag_input(name: &str, label: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `TagInput`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tags` | value | `tags: &'a [&'a str]` |  |  | The tags, instead of the query's `<name>[]`. |
| `action` | value | `action: &'a str` |  | `formaction` | The page Add sends the form back to with GET; this page by default. |
| `placeholder` | value | `placeholder: &'a str` |  | `placeholder` | Placeholder of the text box. |
| `help` | value | `help: &'a str` |  |  | Help text under the box. |
| `error` | value | `message: &'a str` |  |  | A server message under the box. |
| `id` | value | `id: &'a str` |  | `id` | The text box's id, `f-<name>` by default. |

## Platform

| Feature | Chrome | Firefox | Safari |
|---|---|---|---|
| `formmethod` | 9 | 4 | 5.1 |
| `formnovalidate` | 4 | 4 | 5 |
| `:has()` | 105 | 121 | 15.4 |

- Fallback: none needed: Add and remove are page loads that keep the tags in the URL
- Needs script: partly: a chip on Enter or a comma, and removing one in place, need script
- Responsive by: content
- Look after: Origin UI tag input, shadcn Badge

## Documentation

A field that collects several short values (labels, keywords, emails) as removable chips.
The tags travel in the form as hidden `<name>[]` fields, so the post that saves the form
sends them all; the text box beside them is a `<name>[]` too, so a typed tag rides along
with that post as well. Without script, the Add button sends the form back to the page
with GET and the tag becomes a chip; each chip's × is a link to the page without it.

After the Origin UI tag inputs and the shadcn/ui badge: one bordered box holding soft
brand chips (a remove × in each), the text box and the Add button, wrapping as it fills.
A combobox's selected values use the same chips (`.lui-tag-input-chip`).

**Platform features:** hidden inputs named `<name>[]` (every browser), a button with
`formmethod="get"`, `formaction` and `formnovalidate` (baseline 2015) for Add, plain links
for remove, and `:has()` (Chrome 105, Firefox 121, Safari 15.4) for the box's focus ring.

**Accessibility:** the text box has the field's `<label>`; the chips are a list named
"Selected", each × a link named "Remove rust"; help and error describe the text box.
Checked by axe-core in headless Firefox on every demo route, both capability variants,
light and dark (no serious or critical violation).

**What it does not do without script:** turn a tag into a chip on Enter or a comma, or
remove one without a round trip. Without script Add and × are page loads that keep the
other tags in the URL.

**Fallback:** none needed. Without `:has()` the box keeps no ring and the text box shows
its own focus outline.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
// The tags are the query's `tags[]` (an Add round trip leaves them there), or `.tags(..)`.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/note", "tags%5B%5D=rust&tags%5B%5D=web", "");
let m = ui.tag_input("tags", "Tags").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<input type="hidden" name="tags[]" value="rust">"#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"href="/note?tags%5B%5D=web" aria-label="Remove rust""#));
assert!(m.contains(r#"formmethod="get" formaction="/note""#));
// The same in `lui!`:
assert_eq!(lui! { TagInput("tags", "Tags"); }.into_string(), m);
// Saved tags, a placeholder and the page the Add round trip goes to.
let m = ui.tag_input("tags", "Tags").tags(&["css"]).placeholder("Add a tag").action("/note/edit");
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(r#"value="css""#) && !html.contains(r#"value="rust""#));
let same = lui! { TagInput("tags", "Tags") tags=(&["css"]) placeholder="Add a tag" action="/note/edit"; };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
```

# AppShell

`loco_ui::blocks::app_shell` · demo: `/blocks/shell`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `AppShell` | `ui.app_shell(name: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `AppShell`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `group` | item | `heading: &'a str` |  |  | Start a group of links under a small heading. |
| `link` | item | `label: &'a str, href: &'a str` |  |  | A link in the sidebar; the one to the current path is marked current. |
| `icon` | modifier | `icon: impl Into<Glyph<'a>>` |  |  | An icon before the link added last. |
| `badge` | modifier | `text: impl Display` |  |  | A count after the link added last. |
| `user` | value | `name: &'a str, signout: &'a str` |  |  | Who is signed in, and where the sign-out button posts. |
| `body` | value | `body: Markup` |  |  | The page's content. |
| `banner` | value | `banner: Markup` |  |  | A bar across the top, above the sidebar and the content (a `ui.banner(..)`). |
| `current_prefix` | switch |  | `off` |  | Mark a link current also when the path is under it (`/projects` on `/projects/42`). |

## Documentation

The frame of a signed-in app: its name and navigation in a sidebar (a drawer on narrow
screens), in groups with icons and counts as a `crate::sidebar`, who is signed in with a sign-out button at the foot, and the page's content
beside it. The link to the current path is marked `aria-current="page"`.

**Platform features:** those of `crate::drawer` (a modal `<dialog>` on narrow screens, a
plain sidebar when wide); the sign-out is a form that posts.

**Accessibility:** the navigation is a `<nav>` inside the drawer, named by the app's name;
the current page's link has `aria-current="page"`; sign-out is a real button. Checked by
axe-core with the demo routes.

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** that of the drawer: without invoker commands the menu opens through
`?dialog=`.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::from_request("/", "", "");
let m = ui.app_shell("Acme").link("Dashboard", "/").user("Ada Lovelace", "/signout")
    .body(html! { h1 { "Hello" } }).render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains("Ada Lovelace") && m.contains(r#"action="/signout""#));

// Groups under small headings, an icon and a count on a link, as in [`crate::sidebar`]:
let m = ui.app_shell("Acme")
    .link("Inbox", "/").icon(Icon::Mail).badge(3)
    .group("Projects").link("Apollo", "/p/apollo").badge(12)
    .user("Ada Lovelace", "/signout").body(html! { h1 { "Hello" } });
let html = m.render().into_string();
assert!(html.contains(">Projects</p>") && html.contains("lui-sidebar-badge\">12<"));
// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { AppShell("Acme") user=("Ada Lovelace", "/signout") {
    link "Inbox" "/" icon=(Icon::Mail) badge=3;
    group "Projects";
    link "Apollo" "/p/apollo" badge=12;
    body (html! { h1 { "Hello" } });
} };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), html);
// A banner across the top, above the sidebar and the content.
let m = ui.app_shell("Acme").banner(ui.banner("Maintenance at 22:00.").render()).render().into_string();
assert!(m.starts_with(r#"<div class="lui-app-shell"><aside class="lui-banner""#));
assert_eq!(lui! { AppShell("Acme") banner=(ui.banner("Maintenance at 22:00.").render()); }.into_string(), m);
// On `/p/apollo/settings` the link to `/p/apollo` is current.
let ui = Ui::from_request("/p/apollo/settings", "", "");
let m = ui.app_shell("Acme").current_prefix().link("Apollo", "/p/apollo").render().into_string();
assert!(m.contains(r#"<a href="/p/apollo" aria-current="page">"#));
```

# AuthPage

`loco_ui::blocks::auth_page` · demo: `/blocks/auth`

## Constructors

| `lui!` | Constructor | Status |
|---|---|---|

## Props of `AuthPage`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | value | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A line under the title. |
| `body` | value | `body: Markup` |  |  | The form. |
| `footer` | value | `footer: Markup` |  |  | Under the card: links to the other account pages. |

## Documentation

A sign-in, sign-up or reset page: a narrow card in the middle of the page with a title, a
line under it, the form, and the links to the other account pages below. `cargo lui auth`
writes plain views; this is the same page ready-made.

**Platform features:** none of its own: a card and a form that posts.

**Accessibility:** the title is the page's `<h1>`; the form brings its labels, error
summary and focus handling. Checked by axe-core with the demo routes.

**What it does not do without script:** nothing is missing.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let form = ui.form("/signin").email("email", "Email").required().submit("Sign in");
let m = ui.auth_page("Sign in").description("Welcome back.").body(form.render())
    .footer(html! { a href="/signup" { "Create an account" } }).render().into_string();

// The same in `lui!`:
let same = lui! { AuthPage("Sign in") description="Welcome back." body=(form.render())
    footer=(html! { a href="/signup" { "Create an account" } }); };
assert_eq!(same.into_string(), m);
```

# DashboardPage

`loco_ui::blocks::dashboard_page` · demo: `/blocks/dashboard`

## Constructors

| `DashboardPage` | `ui.dashboard_page(title: &str)` | beta |

## Props of `DashboardPage`

| Prop | Kind | Arguments | Default | HTML | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | value | `text: &'a str` |  |  | A line under the title. |
| `stat` | item | `stat: Stat<'a>` |  |  | A number in the row of stats. |
| `body` | value | `body: Markup` |  |  | What goes under the stats. |

## Documentation

A page of numbers: a title and a line, a row of stats that wraps to the width available,
and whatever goes under them (a table, a chart, recent activity).

**Platform features:** those of `crate::stat`: an auto-fit grid, no media query.

**Accessibility:** the title is the page's `<h1>`; each stat says its change in words.
Checked by axe-core with the demo routes.

**What it does not do without script:** update live; the numbers are as fresh as the page.

**Fallback:** none needed.

```rust
use loco_ui::prelude::*;
let ui = Ui::default();
let m = ui.dashboard_page("Overview").description("Last 30 days.")
    .stat(ui.stat("Revenue", "$12,480").delta("+8%"))
    .stat(ui.stat("Customers", "312"))
    .body(html! { p { "Recent orders" } })
    .render().into_string();
```
